Equal layers use normal tree/source order, with the later item above the earlier item where they overlap.
Layer controls depth only; it does not by itself imply modal behaviour or layout.
Modal behaviour
Modal is a separate property. Modal=True traps applicable focus/input inside the modal subtree and blocks lower-layer interaction in the same render surface until dismissal. Nonmodal high-layer popups may sit above content without blocking unrelated lower-layer interaction outside their bounds.
Anchor and runtime placement
Anchor is an optional named placement point, not a prerequisite for loading a Prefab or dynamically created UI.
<Anchor::bob>
Runtime placement MUST support at least:
LoadAt(anchor) — place at an Anchor.
LoadAt(x,y) — fixed proportional coordinates in the selected/current Absolute coordinate scope.
LoadAtPixels(x,y) and LoadAtPercent(x,y).
LoadUnder(element), LoadAbove(element), LoadLeftOf(element) and LoadRightOf(element).
LoadIn(grid,row,column, optional spans/alignment).
LoadInto(container).
Relative placement operations such as LoadUnder, LoadAbove, LoadAt(anchor) and LoadIn(grid,...) remain live placement relationships and track target movement/resizing. Raw coordinate placement is fixed in the chosen coordinate scope unless the caller changes it.
When multiple Prefabs/UI instances are loaded at the same Anchor without another placement rule, they flow downward from that Anchor in load order. Raw repeated coordinate loads overlap unless another rule is supplied.
Style and property precedence
Effective presentation MUST resolve deterministically in the following order from lowest to highest precedence:
CUI built-in property default.
Inherited Theme.
element Type/(Definition) default.
explicit instance property.
scoped <$Property> region.
active Style/event overlay.
A direct runtime property assignment changes the stored explicit property value at its normal level; it is not an invisible new top-level precedence layer. If a temporary event Style currently overrides that property, the new stored value becomes visible when the temporary overlay ends.
Style rules and ActionEvent
Action events use the long form <ActionEvent Type="..."> or & shorthand.
<&Hover>
<&Clicked>
<&PointerEnter>
<&PointerExit>
Inside a Style, an ActionEvent begins a rule and following property/action declarations belong to that event until the next ActionEvent or the end of the Style. A property declaration before any event is an unconditional Style property while that Style is active.
<Style>
    <&Hover{::button}>
    <$Color:Pink{::label}>
    <$Background:Black{::label}>
</Style>
Event target syntax
Curly braces declare an explicit target. {::foo} targets ID foo; {:::foo} targets Group foo. TargetID and TargetGroup are the verbose equivalent attributes.
<&Hover{::greenText}>
<&Hover TargetID="greenText">
<$Color:Pink{:::labels}>
<$Color:Pink TargetGroup="labels">
When an event/property declaration is owned by an element/Style and no explicit target is provided, it targets the owning element/context according to that construct's standard rule.
Temporary versus Once events
Stateful events such as Hover apply their associated Style overlay only while the state is active; ending Hover automatically reveals the previously effective values. OnceHover commits the resulting mutation so it remains after Hover ends.
The same temporary-versus-committed distinction applies to corresponding event families such as Clicked/OnceClick, Loaded/OnceLoaded and Deactivated/OnceDeactivated where meaningful. Once-prefixed events may execute on later qualifying occurrences; 'Once' denotes committed effect semantics, not a one-time lifetime subscription.
Event source, propagation and cancellation
Events target the actual originating element by default and do not automatically bubble through every parent. Bubble=True enables supported upward propagation.
Event context MUST expose at least Event.Source, Event.Target, Event.Type and applicable Event.Value. For a Group trigger, Event.Source identifies the particular Group member that generated the event, enabling a single Group rule to affect only that member when desired.
Event.Cancel() cancels further compatible propagation/action when the event family permits cancellation.
Typed actions and asynchronous work
ActionEvent MAY invoke a named typed application/domain action in addition to Style/property changes. UI actions MUST converge on the same domain operations used by the app's API/Automation surface where an equivalent operation exists; CUI MUST NOT become a parallel private business-logic layer.
<&Clicked{::SaveButton} Action:SaveDocument>
Long-running/async actions MUST NOT block the UI thread and must expose typed running/completed/failed/cancelled state/events usable by CUI.
Input and two-way value flow
Displaying a variable is one-way by default. Writable Input properties bind two-way by default when the source is writable and the conversion is valid.
<Input Type:Text Value=<:Name:>>
<Input Type:Checkbox Checked=<:Enabled:>>
<Input Type:Slider Value=<:Volume:>>
WriteBack=False disables automatic source update. A :static reference is snapshot-only and has no automatic write-back.
When typed conversion fails during input, the control retains the invalid entered representation and exposes validation error state; the source variable is not overwritten until conversion succeeds.
Conditional UI
CUI MUST provide structural conditional composition.
<If Condition=<:LoggedIn:>>
    ...
</If>
<Else>
    ...
</Else>
Condition is live by default. When the condition changes, the applicable branch is instantiated and the other branch is removed from the structural tree. A static condition reevaluates only on explicit containing-scope refresh.
Structural removal is stronger than Active inheritance: an ActiveIndependently child cannot remain alive after the entire conditional branch that owns it ceases to exist.
Repeated UI
Repeat creates one generated UI instance per source item and MUST preserve item identity across live collection additions/removals/reordering.
<Repeat Source=<:Users:> As:user Key=<:user.ID:>>
    <Text><:user.Name:></Text>
</Repeat>
Key may be omitted only when each item exposes an unambiguous stable ID. A live Repeat without stable identity MUST fail rather than recreate items with ambiguous state transfer. The iteration variable exists only inside its Repeat instance.
Property catalogue and transform support
The CUI property registry MUST include mature CSS/Avalonia-like visual properties and transforms rather than limiting authors to basic colours and dimensions.
At minimum, applicable registered properties include:
Rotate, Scale, ScaleX, ScaleY, Skew, SkewX, SkewY, Translate, TranslateX and TranslateY.
Opacity, Background, Foreground/Color, Border, BorderColor, BorderWidth, CornerRadius, Shadow, Clip and Effect.
Typography, text alignment/wrapping, layout sizing/alignment, scrolling, cursor/input/focus and accessibility properties.
Animation and animation-control properties.
Properties remain strongly typed. Unknown/incompatible property names or values are compiler errors when statically knowable.
Effect versus Background backdrop processing
Effect and Background modifier chains have different targets.
Effect processes the element's own rendered appearance. Effect:Blur(1), for example, blurs that element.
Background modifier chains process only the live rendered appearance of content behind the element as seen through the element's background region. They MUST NOT mutate, rotate, recolour, blur, move, restyle or otherwise change the actual underlying elements, their layout, hitboxes, state, events, Layer or accessibility tree.
Backdrop processing is live, not a captured fake snapshot. If content behind the background changes because of user interaction, variable updates, animation, video, scrolling, layout or any other render change, the appearance seen through the Background MUST update automatically without calling Refresh(). The compositor MAY cache safely but must invalidate affected backdrop dependencies correctly.
A fully transparent background exposes the processed backdrop directly; a semi-transparent colour/material composites over the processed backdrop; a fully opaque result may make the backdrop invisible and may be optimised away when observationally equivalent.
Blur, Refract and chained backdrop modifiers
Gaussian blur is built in.
Effect:Blur(1)
Background:Blur(1).Red
Blur uses a ratio by default: Blur(1) is equivalent to Blur(100%), Blur(0.5) to Blur(50%). The renderer maps the public ratio to the platform blur implementation deterministically.
Refract is a built-in live backdrop modifier that refracts/distorts content behind the Background, enabling liquid-glass-like materials.
Background:Refract(1).Blur(1).Color(Green).Red
Backdrop modifiers are evaluated left-to-right. Visual properties with a defined backdrop-rendering interpretation may participate as modifiers. For example:
Background:Refract(1).Blur(1).Color(Green).Rotate(30deg).Red
In the example above, only the sampled live backdrop appearance inside the Background is refracted, blurred, colour-treated and rotated; the underlying elements themselves remain unchanged. A property with no meaningful/registered backdrop interpretation MUST produce a typed compiler/runtime error rather than being silently ignored.
Gradients
Gradient is a first-class property value/modifier.
Gradient(Linear),Red(10%),Blue(20%),Green(70%)
Gradient(Linear),Red,Blue,Green
Gradient(Linear).Red, Blue, Green
Explicit stop percentages define stop positions. When stops omit positions, they are distributed evenly. Radial and other registered gradient forms are supported through the same Gradient(Type) model. Stop positions MUST be deterministic and validated; duplicate positions MAY be used for hard transitions where supported.
Animation and Keyframes
Animation is the canonical property used to apply a named animation.
<Button Animation:ShinyButton>
Named animations are declared using @ shorthand or Keyframe long form.
<@ShinyButton>
<Keyframe Name="ShinyButton">
Keyframe positions may be percentages or absolute time in milliseconds.
<$10%>
<$1000>
<$1000> means 1000 milliseconds / one second. Explicit ms/s duration syntax is also supported. Percentage keyframes require a declared/inferable Animation duration; absolute-time keyframes may infer total duration from the greatest absolute keyframe when no longer Duration is declared.
Keyframe bodies contain ordinary typed property declarations. Animatable/interpolatable property types interpolate between frames; non-interpolatable properties switch at the relevant frame boundary.
Animation control properties MUST cover at least Duration, Delay, Easing, Repeat/iteration, direction/playback and reduced-motion behaviour. The exact property registry is versioned with CUI.
Assigning/changing Animation while an element is active starts/restarts it according to its playback properties. An animation applied by a temporary Style follows that Style's lifetime unless its action explicitly commits/persists animation state.
Theme, Definition and property interaction
Theme defaults, Type/Definition defaults, explicit properties, property regions, Styles, animations and runtime changes MUST all resolve through the same registered CUI property system. There MUST NOT be separate incompatible colour/layout/transform implementations for each syntax.
Theme changes at runtime MUST invalidate only affected presentation state and preserve canonical app/domain state.
Runtime loading and element methods
Named/ID-addressable elements expose generated typed runtime handles. Runtime APIs MUST provide property mutation plus lifecycle/content operations including Active(...), Refresh(), Text/Children Replace/Add and placement/load functions where supported.
Runtime calls and markup directives MUST converge on the same underlying CUI property/lifecycle/action operations so behaviour does not depend on how a mutation was initiated.
Imports and project file discovery
The CUI toolchain automatically indexes supported local .cui, .cui-theme and .cui-prefab files within the declared project/source roots. External/shared packages use Import.
<Import Source:"package/path">
Ambiguous symbols from multiple imports MUST fail until disambiguated, including by an explicit alias such as As:SharedUI. Circular Definition/Prefab import dependencies are rejected.
Accessibility, focus and keyboard semantics
CUI MUST make accessible behaviour the default. Interactive built-ins provide appropriate semantic roles, focusability and keyboard behaviour unless explicitly overridden for a valid reason.
Framework accessibility/focus properties include:
AccessibleName and AccessibleDescription.
Role.
TabIndex and Focusable.
Shortcut and focus-state presentation.
Focus order follows semantic/tree/layout order unless explicitly overridden. Inactive elements cannot receive user focus. Hidden-but-interactive controls are technically representable under CUI's Hidden semantics, but first-party accessibility lint MUST reject invisible focusable/interactive constructs unless an explicit justified accessibility contract is supplied.
Reduced motion, high contrast, scaling/zoom and non-colour-only state communication MUST be framework-level capabilities rather than app-specific reinventions.
Localisation and directionality
CUI MUST support resource-backed/localisable user-visible strings, locale-aware number/date formatting and right-to-left directionality. Direction/layout mirroring is framework-managed where applicable. Literal developer/debug strings MAY remain literal; shipping product copy SHOULD use the localisation/resource system.
Security and dynamic CUI
First-party compiled .cui, Plugin CUI and Generative UI are different trust classes.
Compiled first-party CUI may reference its declared application contracts.
Plugin/external CUI surfaces execute inside their declared/authorised host capability environment and do not gain action permissions merely by rendering controls.
Generative UI is structured data rendered through approved CUI components/actions and MUST NOT become arbitrary trusted .cui/C# execution.
Dynamic Children strings are parsed as CUI only when the caller intentionally uses Children. User/external text should normally use Text or an explicit AddText-equivalent. Dynamic markup MUST be constrained to registered/authorised elements, properties, variables and actions of the current host.
Error boundaries and failure behaviour
Static syntax/type/property/binding errors are build/compile errors with file, line and column diagnostics and, where safe, suggested corrections.
Runtime failures from dynamic CUI, plugin content, specialised Object hosts, data or async actions MUST be isolated at the nearest declared/default error boundary where feasible so one failed component does not unnecessarily destroy the entire window/application.
An invalid dynamic CUI update must preserve the last valid tree/content. Unknown incompatible compiled CUI/runtime versions fail with a structured compatibility error.
Hot reload and developer tooling
CUI tooling MUST include compiler/build integration, formatter, linter, hot reload, component/Prefab preview, semantic tree inspector, accessibility inspector, binding/variable dependency inspection, Theme/resource inspection and rendering/performance diagnostics.
Hot reload preserves the current valid runtime tree when edited CUI is invalid. Once valid again, compatible nodes are patched while preserving state by stable IDs where unambiguous. Definition/Theme/Prefab changes update compatible live instances without arbitrarily resetting unrelated runtime state.
Testing and semantic selectors
CUI MUST expose a semantic test/accessibility tree so automated tests can locate elements by ID, role, accessible name and other stable semantic selectors rather than raw screen coordinates when semantic targeting exists.
The test harness MUST be able to render a CUI Page/Prefab at declared dimensions, Theme, scale, accessibility/reduced-motion settings and platform capability profile; interact through semantic input; inspect resulting state; and capture deterministic visual evidence where applicable.
Performance and rendering
CUI MUST use Avalonia's mature low-level rendering/composition foundations while adding CUI-level invalidation, dependency and component semantics without introducing unnecessary full-tree work.
Live variable changes invalidate only dependent expressions/properties/subtrees.
Virtualisable lists/grids/trees MUST use framework virtualisation rather than constructing every off-screen item by default.
Backdrop Blur/Refract/Gradient processing MAY use compositor caching, but cache invalidation MUST remain live and correct when sampled content changes.
Animation/input loops MUST avoid blocking application/domain work on the UI thread.
Caches must be bounded and revision/dependency invalidated.
Performance acceptance requires measured evidence on the declared supported-hardware/platform baseline. 'Looks fast' is not sufficient.
Platform and Home runtime integration
Native CUI applications depend on the compatible Home-managed CUI/shared runtime under the global Home runtime-dependency contract. The CUI compiler/toolchain belongs to the development/build environment; the runtime version/capability requirement is recorded in app/package metadata.
Web CUI MAY use a browser-specific implementation/runtime, but it MUST preserve the same public CUI semantics, component contracts, state identities and supported action/property behaviour except for explicitly declared platform capability differences.
Platform differences such as unsupported backdrop effects, specialised renderer capabilities or input hardware MUST be capability-negotiated explicitly. The runtime MUST NOT silently reinterpret unsupported CUI into materially different behaviour.
Language/runtime versioning
Compiled CUI output MUST record at least CUI language version, CUI runtime ABI/component-registry version and required capability set. Breaking language/runtime changes require migration tooling or explicit compatibility handling.
Custom distributed Themes/Prefabs/packages SHOULD carry their own version/dependency metadata. Missing/incompatible package versions surface as structured build/runtime dependency errors.
CUI compiler pipeline
The canonical pipeline is parse -> shorthand normalization -> symbol/import resolution -> Definition/Prefab/Theme expansion metadata -> typed property/variable/action validation -> accessibility/static lint -> dependency graph generation -> compiled CUI representation/source maps -> runtime binding.
The compiler MUST NOT silently accept unknown attributes/tags/types/events/properties. Typographical mistakes such as Type:Vertcal_Stack SHOULD produce an unknown-symbol error with an unambiguous suggestion such as Vertical Stack when available.
Acceptance criteria
CUI is implementation-complete only when real compiled/runtime behaviour proves the agreed language and framework semantics. Source presence, parsing a toy file or rendering a static Button is insufficient.
Release validation MUST demonstrate at minimum:
A real app surface authored only in .cui with .axaml/.hui rejected as app markup while using the pinned Avalonia fork underneath.
Fixed core elements, Container Grid/Vertical Stack/Horizontal Stack/Absolute Types, scrolling and mature layout properties.
Colon attribute shorthand, underscore-to-space shorthand, comments, strict ambiguity detection and explicit quoted disambiguation.
(Definition) custom elements and Types plus built-in/custom inherited Themes including Professional, Glow, Playful, Bubble and Cinematic.
Static and dynamic Prefabs loaded in multiple hosts, proving shared versus per-instance internal state.
Live/default and static variable references, typed conversion forms and Live(x,y) dependency relationships without per-frame polling.
ID/Name aliases, :: ID shorthand, ::: Group shorthand, scoped Prefab IDs/Groups and deterministic cross-scope access.
Property long form, $ shorthand, property IDs/Groups, inferred single-property Group mutation and mandatory explicit property selection for multi-property Groups.
Text versus Children semantics, Replace/Add and rollback on invalid dynamic child markup.
Active, Hidden, Interactive and !/ActiveIndependently lifecycle semantics including restoration of stored state.
Layer tag/property with positive/negative values, element override, same-layer ordering and separate Modal behaviour.
Absolute decimal ratio coordinates, x/y pixel and percent modes, X-Inherited/Y-Inherited recalibration and nested independent axis scopes.
Prefab/UI placement at Anchor, raw coordinates, pixels, percentages, above/below/left/right of elements and Grid positions, including live relative tracking.
Style rules with Hover/OnceHover, Clicked/OnceClick, Loaded/OnceLoaded and Deactivated/OnceDeactivated plus TargetID/TargetGroup and {::}/{:::} shorthand.
Event.Source for Group triggers, opt-in bubbling/cancellation and typed async action invocation.
Conditional If/Else and identity-preserving Repeat over live collections.
Two-way Input write-back with conversion/validation failure handling.
Rotate/Scale/Skew/Translate and representative CSS/Avalonia-like visual/layout properties through the common typed registry.
Element Effect:Blur and live Background:Blur/Refract modifier chains proving that underlying elements remain semantically/visually unchanged outside the backdrop view.
A backdrop over changing/animated/video content updates live without Refresh().
Linear and Radial gradients with explicit and evenly distributed stops.
Named Animation: application using <@Name>/<Keyframe Name=...>, percentage and millisecond keyframes, interpolation, easing/repeat and reduced-motion handling.
Hot reload preserving the last valid UI and stable state across compatible updates.
Keyboard-only operation, screen-reader semantics, high-contrast/reduced-motion/scaling and accessibility lint.
Semantic UI automation/test selection without coordinate clicking when IDs/roles are available.
Native and web/platform capability negotiation plus language/runtime version mismatch handling.
Any implementation that recreates CUI as an AXAML preprocessor, uses polling for ordinary live variables, treats Hidden as unloaded, treats Active as destructive property reset, mutates underlying elements through Background backdrop modifiers, snapshots Blur/Refract instead of keeping them live, silently guesses ambiguous shorthand, partially applies incompatible Group mutations, or exposes unreviewed donor/property capability gaps MUST fail release conformance.
Apps
Home runtime dependency
Every installable/native 9to1 app has a hard runtime dependency on 9-1 Home. Before initialising the app’s normal UI or opening user artifacts, the app MUST complete a local Home availability/version handshake against the Home-managed shared services it requires.
If Home is not installed, the app MUST refuse normal startup and display only a minimal bootstrap surface explaining that 9-1 Home is required. The bootstrap surface MUST provide an Install Home action that opens/starts the trusted Home installation flow. It MUST NOT create or mutate normal app data while Home is absent.
If Home is installed but the required shared service/API version is missing, incompatible or damaged, the app MUST refuse unsafe normal startup and offer the appropriate Home update/repair flow with a structured reason. Apps MUST NOT silently launch private replacement services to bypass the missing Home dependency.
This local-install dependency applies to native/installable clients. Browser-hosted web surfaces cannot require a local Home installation; they instead use the corresponding authenticated 9to1 shared web services and capability negotiation defined for web clients.
Home owns shared platform services including the permission broker, shared Dulche broker/runtime coordination, package/update metadata and the Shared Productivity Engine defined in the Home section.
Persistent contextual AI bar
Every interactive 9to1 app MUST expose the shared persistent floating contextual AI bar at the bottom of its primary content surface. The bar uses Dulche plus the owning app's authorised semantic state. It MUST be able to inspect the current artifact/surface semantically and, when permitted, edit it through the owning app's typed APIs. The bar is not limited to whatever pixels happen to be visible in the viewport.
The shared bar MUST expose an explicit persistent AI access-mode switcher with at least Read-only and Write mode. The current mode MUST remain visible enough that the user can tell whether Dulche may only inspect the surface or may also request mutations. This switcher is a platform-wide interaction contract used consistently by Write, Present, Boards, Files, Canvas, Data, Mail, Planner and every other surface that hosts the shared bar.
In Read-only mode, Dulche MAY read, search, compare, reason over, summarise, explain and navigate the full authorised semantic surface, including off-screen content that the owning app exposes. It MAY generate proposed changes in conversation, but MUST NOT mutate the owning artifact, structure or app state. Read-only access does not imply permission to inspect data outside the caller's normal authorisation boundary.
In Write mode, Dulche receives the same semantic read context plus the owning app's permitted typed mutation actions. Write mode is capability to request/perform edits, not permission to bypass app state, trust, confirmation, review, external-side-effect or security rules. Mutations MUST use stable semantic identities such as ArtifactID, PageID, SectionID, ObjectID, row/range/entity IDs or equivalent domain identifiers and the owning app's normal revision/conflict semantics.
The AI-bar mode is separate from the host app's own Edit/View/Suggest/Locked/Unlocked or equivalent state. For example, an AI bar in Write mode does not silently bypass a Board that is currently in View mode, and a Write document in Suggest mode represents permitted AI edits as suggestions rather than accepted direct edits. Host-surface rules may narrow the effective mutation set further.
Apps MUST provide a permission-filtered semantic context snapshot including the active artifact/page/entity, current selection, relevant stable object IDs, structure necessary to understand the task, current revision/state and supported typed actions. The bar MUST prefer this semantic context over screenshot/OCR/pixel interpretation and MUST NOT substitute raw mouse/keyboard/desktop automation when typed context/actions exist.
The AI bar MUST remain visually separate from document/page content and MUST NOT change the underlying artifact layout merely by being shown. It MAY collapse to a compact state but MUST remain directly reachable without navigating to a separate AI page. Read/Write mode changes the AI's effective capability only; it does not create a second copy of the current artifact.
Surface-specific mutation protections MAY be stricter than the shared Write-mode baseline and cannot be weakened by AI mode or trust state. Data is the mandatory example: every AI-requested Data mutation requires explicit approval for that specific action even while the bar is in Write mode. When the target is a live database, Data MUST additionally show a meaningful preview/diff, validate the operation and create a recoverable backup/snapshot/checkpoint before execution. If the required live-database backup cannot be created, the mutation MUST NOT proceed as though rollback exists.
For Data live-database changes, the approval surface SHOULD identify the intended operation, affected tables/entities/rows where knowable, schema/dependency impact, external side effects and backup identity. Execution MUST occur only after approval, then verify the actual result and preserve rollback/recovery information. Prior approval, Accept and Trust or Always Trust MUST NOT suppress this Data-specific per-action approval invariant.
Equivalent bar actions MUST behave consistently across product surfaces, while menus and available operations remain context-sensitive to the owning app. Unsupported or inapplicable actions MUST not be exposed merely to make the bar look feature-complete.
Chat bar — expanded-mode formatting and emoji controls
Visibility and placement: Show the following buttons inline next to the plus (+) button only when the chat bar is both focused and in its expanded composer layout, with the text-entry area above the bottom controls. These buttons must not appear in compact/mini mode, even when the compact/mini chat bar is focused.
Format (Aa): Opens a floating toolbar containing Markdown formatting options, including bold and italics.
Emojis (😀): Opens a CUI emoji picker.
Chat-bar control acceptance
Verify that Aa and the emoji button appear beside + only while the expanded composer is focused; neither appears in compact/mini mode. The formatting toolbar and CUI emoji picker MUST work with keyboard input, labelled controls, focus return and preserved draft/selection state.
Cross-app invocation and compose contract
Every interactive 9to1 app that hosts the shared persistent AI bar MUST use Home's canonical compose invocation component and cross-app dispatcher. Plugins, Skills, Apps, Agents, Files and the reserved @Computer Use capability MUST therefore resolve consistently across apps rather than each product implementing a private @ syntax or resource picker.
A model may cross an app boundary only when that action is authorised by user intent: explicit @ invocation, an explicit instruction naming the target capability/app, or an unambiguous requested outcome whose canonical owner is another 9to1 app. Implied intent is semantic, not opportunistic; unrelated app access remains out of scope.
When a target 9to1 app owns the requested artifact/action, the originating model MUST use the target app's typed API/shared semantic action contract and MAY ask Home to launch/reveal the target app so the user can observe progress. For example, a request to create a presentation routes to Present and creates/edits a canonical Present artifact rather than fabricating a slide-like object in the originating app.
Computer Use MUST NOT be selected automatically as a fallback when typed app execution is unavailable, inconvenient or fails. It is usable only after explicit @Computer Use invocation and remains subject to the Computer Use eligibility, permission, game-exclusion and Autoreview rules.
Model-driven typed edits MAY be visualised in the target app with live object motion, selection highlights, text insertion and a synthetic/virtual cursor. This visualisation is not evidence that Dulche is literally controlling the pointer; the typed action/result remains authoritative and the synthetic cursor MUST be visually distinguishable from the user's actual input cursor.
Launch Screens
A launch/home screen is the app’s start surface: the equivalent of the modern Microsoft Word start page shown in the reference image, not simply an empty editor or project view. It appears when the app is opened without an existing artifact/session to restore, and whenever the user deliberately returns to the app’s Home/start surface.
For every app listed below, the launch screen MUST implement each capability in the following list when that capability exists for the product. If a capability is not applicable, the product section MUST explicitly state the exclusion and reason rather than silently omit it:
Create a blank document/project/artifact.
Templates, starter projects and a way to browse more templates where the app supports them.
Recent items, with useful location/path and modified-state information.
Favourites/pinned items.
Shared with Me or equivalent collaborative content where applicable.
Search across the app’s relevant files/projects.
Open/import entry points for existing files/projects and supported external formats.
The launch screen must use CUI and the app’s real storage/project model. Recent, favourite, shared and template entries must be functional data-backed surfaces rather than static mock content. Apps may add app-specific quick actions, onboarding/tours or account/storage indicators where useful.
The following apps must include a launch/home screen:
Write
Present
Data
Canvas
Boards
Picture
Wave
Motion
Forms
AI Studio
Web Apps
Cakemods.com MUST host a web version of every 9-1 Workspace/AI product that is not explicitly listed as web-exempt. Web surfaces MUST share the same CAKE ID identity, canonical artifact formats, domain APIs, permission model and underlying server-side entities as desktop equivalents. Browser-specific UI/layout MAY differ, but it MUST NOT create a separate incompatible product model.
The default rule is to provide a web version whenever the product’s core value can sensibly work in a browser. Browser-specific capability limits are acceptable when they are explicit and the useful core product remains intact; a single desktop-only feature is not by itself a reason to omit an otherwise useful web app.
Web exemption is permitted only when the product’s core function requires infrastructure, privileged device access or hosted compute that CAKE does not currently provide. Each exemption MUST state the blocking capability/infrastructure. Exemptions MUST be re-evaluated when that blocker is removed; exemption is not a permanent product classification.
Current exemption:
Mini Computer — a useful web version would require hosted virtualisation/server compute that CAKE does not currently have capacity to provide.
Mini Computer may gain a hosted web mode in the future as a 9to1 subscription capability if sufficient server compute is available. The same principle applies to future apps whose meaningful web implementation requires paid hosted compute.
Accounts & Subscription
CAKE ID and authentication
CAKE ID is the shared identity used across CAKE and 9to1. A normal CAKE ID is separate from a WordPress user account; WordPress may remain linked for site administration, but ordinary 9to1 users must not need WordPress accounts.
9to1 web apps authenticate against CAKEMODS/CAKE ID using a browser-based OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE or an equivalent secure public-client flow. Desktop, web and open-source/custom clients are treated as untrusted public clients: they receive short-lived user access tokens and never contain provider keys, billing secrets or entitlement-signing secrets.
The server is authoritative for account state, sessions, entitlements, organisation policy, Dust, storage/site quotas, billing and provider credentials. A modified or self-built client can change its own interface or features but cannot grant itself paid entitlements, bypass quotas or mint trusted usage.
Authentication/session operations must support account sign-in/sign-out, current-user/profile lookup, active-session/device inspection and revocation. Sensitive account or billing changes use trusted CAKEMODS web flows rather than accepting raw payment credentials through the open-source client.
Profiles — customisation and Jacob's reserved account
Profile customisation MUST include changing the display name and username through the profile/account UI and equivalent authorised APIs. Username availability, uniqueness and reservation checks MUST apply consistently across UI, APIs, registration and rename flows. Changes MUST preserve the canonical CAKE ID/UserID, ownership, history, permissions and entitlements; mutable names MUST NOT become identity or authorisation keys.
The exact handle @CroakyJake MUST be reserved exclusively for Jacob. Registration and rename flows MUST prevent other accounts from claiming it, including case variants that would bypass the reservation. The reservation MUST be bound through trusted provisioning to Jacob's verified canonical account ID, not awarded to whichever account first requests that text. Production identifiers MUST be verified rather than guessed.
Jacob's verified account MUST automatically receive all Business features free of charge, including subsequently added Business features, without requiring a paid Business subscription. This is an account-bound entitlement: changing a display name or username MUST NOT grant it to another person or remove it from Jacob. Reservation and entitlement administration MUST be privileged, auditable operations, separate from ordinary profile editing. Free Business access does not bypass security permissions or authorise third-party spending.
Profile customisation — required and optional fields
The profile editor MUST include the following fields. An asterisk (*) denotes a required field; only Name and Username are required within this field set.
Name* — REQUIRED. The user's profile/display name, extending the existing display-name customisation requirement.
Username* — REQUIRED. The user's account handle, subject to the existing availability, uniqueness and reservation rules.
Icon — OPTIONAL. The user's profile icon, which the user can add, change or remove.
Pronouns — OPTIONAL. User-provided pronouns, which the user can add, change or clear.
Job — OPTIONAL. The user's job/job title. This field is especially relevant in a Business context but MUST also be available to ordinary personal users; it MUST NOT be Business-only or mandatory for Business users.
The UI MUST visibly mark Name and Username with an asterisk and explain that * denotes required. Icon, Pronouns and Job MUST be allowed to remain unset and to be cleared without preventing an otherwise valid profile from being saved. Name and Username MUST NOT be saved as empty or whitespace-only values. Optional personal information MUST NOT be inferred or populated without the user's input.
The equivalent authorised profile APIs MUST expose the same five fields and apply the same required/optional validation rules. Partial updates MUST preserve fields omitted from the request rather than clearing them. Existing canonical account identity, ownership, permissions, username reservation and account-bound Business entitlement requirements remain unchanged, including Jacob's reserved @CroakyJake handle and free Business features.
Acceptance MUST verify that a profile can be saved with valid Name and Username while Icon, Pronouns and Job are unset; all three optional fields can subsequently be added, changed and cleared; Job is available to both personal and Business users without becoming required; blank required fields produce validation errors; and equivalent authorised API operations preserve the same behaviour and account identity.
Profile API, provisioning and acceptance
Extend the existing account/profile APIs for profile reads and partial updates, icon management and username availability. Reservation and account-bound Business-entitlement provisioning MUST remain privileged, auditable operations. APIs MUST expose the same validation as the UI, preserve omitted fields and return structured conflicts or validation failures. Ordinary clients MUST NOT self-grant Business access. Test rename without identity or ownership loss, rejected unauthorised @CroakyJake claims and case variants, and automatic free Business access for Jacob’s verified account only; security permissions and third-party spending approvals still apply.
Subscription model
9to1 uses a preset-first subscription model with optional customisation. Subscription state has two separate dimensions: price-threshold entitlements and resource configuration. The two MUST be stored and evaluated independently.
Price-threshold entitlements determine which feature/model/site capabilities the account unlocks as its canonical configured monthly price crosses defined thresholds. Resource configuration determines the account’s allocated quantities, including AI Dust, storage, hosted-site capacity and other metered resources.
Named plans Free, Boost, Plus, Pro, Ultra, Ultra+ and Max serve both as threshold names and as preset configuration names. Their canonical ascending PlanLevel order is Free = 0, Boost = 1, Plus = 2, Pro = 3, Ultra = 4, Ultra+ = 5 and Max = 6. APIs, billing logic and entitlement checks MUST use stable PlanID/PlanLevel rather than inferring ordering from display names. A preset is a convenience starting configuration; the preset label MUST NOT be treated as the sole source of entitlement truth.
Local models and core local tools are not metered through cloud AI Dust. The Free configuration MUST retain useful local/core functionality while cloud AI, hosted storage/sites and other server-funded resources remain subject to server-authoritative entitlements and quotas.
Price thresholds
Let EntitlementPriceMonthly be the canonical monthly price assigned by the subscription backend to the account’s current configuration. The backend MUST compute effective threshold entitlements from this value; clients MUST NOT infer them from the displayed preset name.
Thresholds are cumulative. For every threshold T where EntitlementPriceMonthly >= T.Price, all entitlements defined by T are added to the account’s effective entitlement set. Therefore a Max-priced configuration also receives all lower-threshold grants, including Ultra grants, unless a future threshold explicitly defines a non-cumulative exception.
Selecting a preset does not bypass threshold evaluation. If a user customises a preset and the resulting configured price crosses a different threshold, the backend MUST recalculate the effective threshold set from the resulting EntitlementPriceMonthly.
The currently defined commercial thresholds are:
Free — £0/month. Unlocks access to select free cloud models and unlimited local/core tools.
Boost — £7.99/month. Entry paid cloud-AI tier. It unlocks CAKE-funded cloud models within the Boost model-cost band, benchmarked against Luna-class pricing rather than tied to one specific named model.
Plus — £19.99/month. Adds a materially larger cloud-AI/resource allowance than Boost while retaining access to the Boost model-cost band and any other models priced within that effective band. Plus exists as the regular-use tier between Boost and Pro.
Pro — £34.99/month. Adds a higher CAKE-funded model-cost band benchmarked against Sol-class pricing, while retaining all lower-band model access. Pro also permits materially higher cloud-AI, storage and hosted-site allocations than Plus.
Ultra — £69.99/month. Adds the highest standard CAKE-funded model-cost band, benchmarked against Astra-class pricing, while retaining all lower-band model access.
Ultra+ — £99.99/month. Retains at least the complete Ultra model-access set and enables materially larger cloud-AI, storage, hosted-site and concurrency allocations than Ultra.
Max — £149.99/month. Retains at least the complete Ultra+ model-access set and enables the highest standard preset cloud-AI, storage, hosted-site and concurrency allocations. Because thresholds are cumulative, Max-priced configurations retain every lower-threshold entitlement.
Cloud model entitlement MUST be expressed through versioned effective model-cost/capability bands rather than a permanent allow-list of model brand names. References such as Luna-class, Sol-class and Astra-class are pricing/capability benchmarks for the current commercial design, not exclusive model identities. Any CAKE-funded model whose effective provider cost and capability profile fit within the user's unlocked band may be made available, subject to provider availability, safety/privacy policy and backend configuration. Replacing a benchmark model with another comparably priced model MUST NOT require renaming the subscription tier.
OPEN: the backend still needs one canonical rule defining how temporary discounts, promotional credits, tax and non-monthly billing cadence affect EntitlementPriceMonthly. Until that rule is defined, threshold eligibility MUST be calculated only by the server and MUST NOT be reproduced locally by clients.
Preset configurations
Free, Boost, Plus, Pro, Ultra, Ultra+ and Max also exist as pre-made subscription configurations. A preset MUST define explicit resource values such as allocated AI Dust, storage allocation, hosted-site limits, concurrency/burst limits where applicable and any other metered resources supported by the subscription system.
Preset configuration and threshold entitlement state MUST remain separate server-side fields. Changing resource values MAY change the configured monthly price and therefore the unlocked threshold set, but MUST NOT mutate the canonical definition of the source preset.
A customised plan MUST retain the concrete resource values selected by the user even when those values no longer match any named preset. The UI MAY display the source preset for context, but APIs MUST return the actual resource configuration rather than reconstructing it from a tier name.
Preset definitions MUST be versioned. Existing accounts MUST retain an auditable reference to the preset version they originally selected plus subsequent customisation state. Updating a preset definition MUST NOT silently rewrite existing subscriber allocations.
Known preset requirements are now: Boost is £7.99/month with light cloud-AI usage, small hosted storage, a maximum of 1 full hosted site and 3 single-page sites; Plus is £19.99/month with materially higher cloud-AI usage and storage, a maximum of 3 full hosted sites and 5 single-page sites. Pro (£34.99), Ultra (£69.99), Ultra+ (£99.99) and Max (£149.99) MUST each provide materially more included cloud-AI usage, storage and hosted-site capacity than the preceding paid preset. Exact AI Dust/storage/site quantities above Plus are not yet fully specified and MUST NOT be invented.
Canonical subscription state
The server-authoritative subscription object MUST expose at least the following fields:
PresetID? — stable identifier of the preset used as the starting configuration, or null when no preset applies.
PresetVersion? — version of the referenced preset, or null when no preset applies.
IsCustomised — true when the current resource configuration differs from the referenced preset/version.
EntitlementPriceMonthly — canonical monthly price used for threshold evaluation.
EffectiveThresholds — ordered list/set of all currently unlocked thresholds.
EffectiveEntitlements — resolved feature/model/site entitlements after threshold, account and organisation-policy evaluation.
AIDustAllocated — allocated cloud-AI Dust for the current billing/configuration period.
StorageAllocatedBytes — storage allocation in bytes.
HostedSiteLimit — concurrent/full hosted-site allowance.
SinglePageSiteLimit — additional single-page-site allowance after threshold/resource evaluation.
AdditionalResources — versioned typed object/map for future metered resources. Clients MUST ignore unknown keys they do not understand while preserving them when round-tripping configuration.
Free hosted-site inactivity
For a Free hosted site, inactivity takes the site offline rather than deleting it. During the first 120 days the account MUST sign in at least once every 30 days to keep the free site online. After that period, the current rule requires at least one account sign-in per year. Taking a site offline MUST NOT delete its stored site data.
Custom resource allocation
The custom-plan editor includes the high-level choice “What do you want to use 9to1 for?” with these profiles:
Full Workspace (Balanced)
Prioritise AI Limits
Prioritise Storage & Sites Limits
Current £10 allocation examples are:
Balanced: 250 GB storage + 35,000 AI Dust.
AI-priority: 25 GB storage + 65,000 AI Dust.
Storage/Sites-priority: 500 GB storage + 15,000 AI Dust.
The current internal allocation baseline is £1 of plan budget = 10,000 AI Dust before commercial margin/profit. The server remains authoritative for the actual commercial conversion and account balance.
Business add-ons — pricing, seats and resource billing
Business costs an additional USD $5 per month per organisation and supports a maximum of 50 seats. Business + costs an additional USD $15 per month per organisation and has no subscription seat cap. Neither add-on has a separate per-seat fee. Purchased AI usage/credits, storage and other funded resources remain separately configured and may be pooled or allocated individually; unlimited seats do not mean unlimited resources.
Both add-ons include 9to1 Admin and the functional Business capabilities specified below. Business + includes the Business capability set; further exclusive Business + capabilities are OPEN and MUST NOT be invented from its name. Pricing displays, quotes, invoices and entitlement APIs MUST distinguish the organisation add-on, seat capacity and resource charges. A base-resource quote in another currency MUST NOT be silently relabelled as USD; the trusted billing quote must make currency/conversion explicit.
Billing state MUST store AddOnID, add-on definition version, OrgID, seat-limit value or explicit Unlimited, effective dates and applicable account-bound grants separately from user resource configurations. No client-supplied role, username or plan label can self-grant Business. The free Business entitlement for Jacob remains governed by the Profiles subsection and does not authorise paid resource purchases or third-party spending.
Changing Business + to Business with more than 50 active members MUST require a seat-remediation preview or retain a visibly constrained pending-downgrade state; it must not silently remove users or delete shared content. Add-on cancellation and billing failure MUST have explicit entitlement/recovery states. Account-level billing, export and recovery remain available through appropriate authorised routes even when normal Business editing is unavailable. Exact grace periods, proration and suspended/pending-seat accounting remain OPEN unless defined in the canonical billing policy.
Entitlements and usage API
The subscription/account layer must expose supported first-party APIs for the information and actions available to the user, following the global API-parity rule. The core surface includes:
9to1.Account.GetCurrent();
9to1.Account.GetEntitlements();
9to1.Account.ListSessions();
9to1.Account.RevokeSession(sessionID);
9to1.Account.RevokeAllOtherSessions();
9to1.Subscription.GetPlan();
9to1.Subscription.GetUsage();
9to1.Subscription.GetDustBalance();
9to1.Subscription.GetStorageUsage();
9to1.Subscription.GetSiteUsage();
9to1.Subscription.ListPresets();
9to1.Subscription.PreviewConfiguration(config);
9to1.Subscription.OpenCheckout(config);
9to1.Subscription.OpenManage();
9to1.Subscription.GetPersonalAPIStatus();
Billing-changing calls do not accept raw payment-card details. OpenCheckout/OpenManage hand off to an authenticated trusted CAKEMODS billing flow. Read APIs return the server-authoritative account state rather than trusting client-maintained counters.
Server-authoritative enforcement
All paid/cloud usage is enforced server-side. The open-source client is never the authority for remaining Dust, model access, storage, site count, billing state or quotas. Custom/forked clients use the same live account entitlements and cannot bypass limits by changing local code.
For cloud AI, the trusted gateway checks identity, organisation policy where applicable, model entitlement, hard limits and Dust before execution. Usage follows a reserve → run → settle model so concurrent requests cannot overspend the same balance. Provider keys and commercial billing logic remain server-side.
Short-lived or one-time signed capability tokens may be used internally for narrowly scoped operations, but they do not become reusable secrets embedded in applications. Server-side storage/site operations perform the same authoritative entitlement checks.
Personal API access
Accounts with at least 80,000 allocated AI Dust unlock Personal API access. Personal API usage consumes the same account Dust allowance as normal 9to1 cloud-AI usage; it is not a separate unlimited pool.
Personal API access is for the account holder’s own external integrations and workflows. It is not a public-facing resale allowance and does not grant permission to redistribute CAKE provider credentials or resell the underlying service.
Web subscription behaviour
Web and desktop clients MUST resolve account state from the same CAKE ID and entitlement service. For the same account and organisation context, plan identity, Dust balance, hosted-storage usage, site quota/usage and applicable feature entitlements MUST be consistent across official clients, subject only to explicitly documented platform capability differences.
Where a future web feature requires material hosted compute that is not available on the free/local product - for example hosted Mini Computer virtual machines - it may be offered as a subscription-backed server capability with explicit resource limits. The browser UI must never pretend that local-only or unavailable server compute exists.
Business features — functional specification
BIZ-01 — Organisation boundary and shared state
Business is an organisation collaboration and management capability set, not merely labels on pricing cards. It comprises Team Space and an organisation drive; organisation Connect; cross-account device Mesh; pooled or individually partitioned usage; team-wide Agents; and device-level policy controls for managed 9to1-OS Business accounts. 9to1 Admin supplies their management interface, while the existing apps retain canonical ownership of their domain data.
Every organisation-scoped operation MUST carry an explicit OrgID and authenticated membership/delegation context. Personal and organisation work remain separately identifiable in switchers, search, storage, AI context and billing. Joining an organisation MUST NOT merge personal files, chats, memories, devices or credentials into it. Moving/sharing personal material requires a deliberate authorised operation with destination ownership, access and billing impact shown. Leaving one organisation cannot revoke or destroy unrelated personal work or membership elsewhere.
BIZ-02 — Team Space and organisation drive
Each organisation MUST support a canonical shared Team Space backed by organisation-owned shared storage, not an independent copy of every member’s files. Space membership, role/group access, instructions, permitted models/tools and shared Agent bindings are managed through the existing Spaces model. Files, Pages, Boards and other app artifacts retain stable canonical IDs and their owning formats; references/embeds do not create silent forks.
The organisation drive MUST support folders, create/upload/open/edit where the owning app supports it, search, move/rename, version history, sharing/access review, archive/delete/recover and authorised export. Access may be assigned to organisation roles/groups or explicitly scoped members. Effective object access is checked by storage, search/indexing, previews, AI retrieval and exports, not just the Files UI. External sharing requires policy permission and explicit recipient/link scope; revocation must remove future server access and invalidate applicable derived access paths.
Shared-storage accounting MUST identify the owning organisation and charge canonical stored data once according to the storage policy rather than once per viewer. Access removal preserves organisation-owned artifacts and transfers responsibilities where necessary; it does not give administrators ownership of a departed member’s unrelated personal files. Restore/export workflows retain identity and permissions deliberately rather than accidentally republishing private content.
BIZ-03 — Organisation Connect
Connect MUST provide an organisation directory and scoped organisational groups/channels and contact endpoints, with role-controlled membership, creation and management. Where shared business identities or communication endpoints are configured, delegates act through named authorised roles with auditable attribution, not password sharing or undetectable impersonation. Inviting an external correspondent to communicate is distinct from making them an organisation seat or allocating paid usage.
Organisation communications MUST use Connect’s canonical conversations, contacts, calls and message identities. Agent email/call/text endpoints resolve to the same canonical team Agent and its permissions. External providers and device-backed transports require actual supported connections and credentials; provisioning paid endpoints needs separate approval. Membership or admin status does not create blanket permission to read private/E2EE content, export it to a model or bypass participant consent and retention controls.
BIZ-04 — Cross-account device Mesh
Business Mesh MUST allow explicitly authorised devices belonging to different organisation members to share supported compute/storage capabilities through Home/Mesh. Enrolment records MUST bind DeviceID, device/account owner, OrgID, verified trust/key material reference, supported capabilities, resource limits and grant expiry/revocation state. Organisation membership alone must not automatically pair a personal device or expose its files, GPU or network.
A resource grant MUST specify permitted consumers/workloads, CPU/GPU/memory/storage/concurrency budgets and permitted data locations. Job admission checks both requester permissions and the contributing device’s current policy. Data/secrets are scoped to the job and authorised endpoint; device contribution does not grant unrelated file, screen, microphone or personal-session access. Sensitive/local-only work cannot silently migrate to a different member’s device or a cloud provider without an authorised processing route.
Mesh MUST expose availability, queued/running jobs, utilisation, failure and cancellation/revocation outcomes. Revocation blocks new work and cancels or safely terminates existing work where supported; it must not claim to undo already completed actions or erase copies outside its actual control. A disconnected device remains unavailable/pending, never fictitiously running a workload. Windows and 9to1-OS expose only supported native capabilities; web can manage grants and observe jobs without pretending to supply privileged local resources.
BIZ-05 — Shared and individual usage pools
An organisation MUST be able to use a shared funded AI/resource pool or individually partition its purchased allocation by member/role. Partitioning is accounting over the same authoritative ledger, not duplicate credits. Store PoolID, source allocation, period, remaining/reserved/settled amounts, allocation owner and applicable policy. Member views show their effective allowance; authorised administrators can inspect aggregate and scoped consumption without exposing private work content.
Requests reserve capacity before execution and settle actual usage afterwards, releasing unused reservation according to the backend contract. The organisation total, individual ceiling and role ceiling all apply where configured. Parallel requests, retries and delayed provider reports MUST NOT spend the same balance twice. Changing pool mode preserves in-flight reservations and history and requires a validated allocation plan; insufficient funds or ambiguous settlement blocks unsafe transfer rather than inventing capacity.
Role-based rollover permission defined in Admin MUST be applied to eligible credit lots at rollover/expiry transitions and be visible in member balances. Changes preserve original lot provenance and settled charges. The product MUST distinguish rolled-over credits from newly purchased allocation and show the effective expiry. No personal balance is swept into an organisation pool merely because its owner joins; no organisation-funded balance becomes a departed member’s personal credit without an explicit supported transfer policy.
BIZ-06 — Team-wide Agents
A team Agent is a canonical Dulche Agent with organisation ownership/scope and configurable discovery, invocation, authoring and administration grants. Eligible members MUST be able to discover and invoke it from supported Spaces/app pickers and configured Connect channels without creating separate private copies. Shared configuration and approved knowledge are distinct from per-user conversations and private memories; access to one member’s context cannot leak into another member’s response.
Agent publishing/versioning, ownership transfer, required Plugins, allowed models, tool scopes, approval boundaries, schedules, budgets and concurrency limits MUST be enforced by Dulche/Home and the owning services. An Agent cannot use its owner’s wider authority to bypass the requesting member’s restrictions unless an explicit, separately authorised delegated service capability covers that operation. Persistent scheduled work records the service principal, scope and funding source and is re-evaluated on role, policy or membership changes.
Pausing, revoking or archiving a team Agent MUST stop new authorised dispatch, preserve auditable run history and report what happened to queued/running work. Sensitive credentials remain secure references; publishing an Agent is not permission to reveal them. AI Studio, Admin and runtime surfaces all edit or reference the same Agent identity and versioned definition.
BIZ-07 — Managed 9to1-OS accounts and device policy
Business MUST provide device-level administrative controls for explicitly enrolled managed 9to1-OS Business accounts. Controls MUST cover supported app/package and Plugin installation/enablement restrictions, allowed features and Automations, required organisation/role Plugins, enforced settings, default-model/routing policy and Mesh-resource participation. Existing compatibility-framework and privileged-operation restrictions continue to apply beneath every launch surface.
The OS policy agent MUST verify policy origin/version, apply only the enrolled managed scope and report Applied, Pending, Failed, Unsupported or NonCompliant status with reasons. Local UI changes, direct API calls and alternate launch paths cannot bypass enforced settings. Offline endpoints retain their last valid policy and cannot claim a newly published policy was applied without acknowledgement. Revocation and next-contact reconciliation must be explicit.
Managed account policy is not automatic whole-device ownership. Personal users, personal artifacts and unenrolled devices remain outside the organisation’s authority. Destructive remote actions, full-device wipe, arbitrary privileged shell access and surveillance are not implicitly authorised by Business. Other operating systems may expose supported Mesh and app policy, but they must not claim complete 9to1-OS endpoint-management parity without an explicit capability implementation.
BIZ-08 — Cross-app enforcement and acceptance
Permissions, policy, membership and credit changes MUST propagate through supported authoritative services and invalidate affected cached grants before further protected server actions. Published configuration, delivered configuration and acknowledged enforcement remain different states. Long-running rollout, export and reassignment use resumable jobs with per-target results. Downgrade, service outage or partial rollout must preserve data and fail closed for newly unauthorised actions.
Acceptance MUST demonstrate a shared artifact edited through two apps without forking; denied access absent from search, preview and AI context; organisation Connect without access to personal messages; explicit two-account Mesh enrolment, bounded execution and revocation; shared-pool concurrency and individual ceilings; role-dependent rollover; a team Agent that cannot leak another member’s private context; and OS restrictions enforced below UI across restart/offline/reconnect. Each feature requires equivalent authorised API coverage, persistence, accessibility, failure/recovery and actual end-to-end evidence. Inclusion on a pricing card alone is not conformance.
Apps
Workspace Apps
Home
Product role and ownership
9-1 Home is the mandatory native ecosystem hub, platform shell and control plane for installed 9to1 applications. It is not merely a dashboard application. Home owns shared platform services that must have one canonical implementation across the ecosystem: app/package management, the Home Core service registry, shared Dulche lifecycle/broker coordination, permission/trust brokerage, account/subscription state, the Shared Productivity Engine, shared model/provider configuration, Action Graph rendering, Mesh coordination, notifications, shared search/index coordination and ecosystem-wide settings.
Other apps MUST consume Home-owned shared services through supported authenticated interfaces and MUST NOT silently launch incompatible private replacements when a Home service is unavailable. App-owned documents, projects and domain data remain owned by their respective apps/storage layers; Home MUST NOT become the only canonical copy of another app’s artifacts.
Home installation includes the Home Core background service/runtime required by native apps plus the Home user-facing CUI shell. Native apps require a compatible Home installation/Home Core service, but the visible Home window does not need to remain open while other apps run. On 9to1-OS, Home Core may be integrated as a system component while preserving the same service contracts.
Home shell and navigation
The Home shell MUST be dashboard/home-oriented rather than primarily a conventional settings application. Its stable primary navigation MUST provide at least Home/Dashboard, Apps, Library, Events, Discover, Mesh and Settings. Account/profile controls MAY live in persistent shell chrome. Chat remains a Spaces destination and MUST NOT become Home’s primary landing surface.
Navigation destinations MUST preserve their own scroll/filter/selection state while the Home process remains active where practical. Deep links from notifications, Go, other apps or the OS MUST be able to open the relevant Home destination/object directly without first routing through the Dashboard.
Dashboard
The 9-1 AI Dashboard is a generative briefing/dashboard surface, not a chat landing page. It MUST assemble permission-authorised cross-app information into a concise live brief and MUST derive every surfaced tile from identifiable source entities/events or an explicitly generated synthesis over identifiable sources.
Dashboard tiles MAY surface upcoming Planner items, tasks, recent files/artifacts, project progress, reminders, travel/routes, Agent or Automation status, relevant Mail/messages, package/update state, storage/account warnings and other timely ecosystem context. Every actionable tile MUST use typed app actions; the Dashboard MUST NOT use raw UI automation to perform app mutations.
Chat remains in Spaces. The Dashboard MAY expose a lightweight ask/action affordance, but its primary purpose is synthesis, prioritisation, status and quick action.
Dashboard layout and customisation
Dashboard layout is user-configurable. The user MUST be able to add supported fixed/provider tiles, remove/hide tiles, resize tiles where the tile declares supported sizes, drag/reorder tiles, arrange tiles into the supported responsive layout, pin/lock tiles against automated movement and restore/reset a layout.
The canonical DashboardLayout MUST use stable TileInstanceID values and store at least TileType, source/provider identity, position/order, declared size, user visibility state, pinned/locked state, tile-specific configuration and layout revision. Responsive rendering MAY adapt exact pixel/grid placement to the current window/device, but it MUST preserve the user’s semantic ordering/grouping and pinned constraints.
Manual user layout changes are authoritative. Automated generation/reordering MUST NOT silently overwrite a newer manual layout revision. When a layout conflict occurs across synced devices, Home MUST preserve both revisions or resolve through an explicit revision/merge policy rather than blind last-write-wins.
AI-generated tiles and AI layout control
Dashboard settings MUST expose two independent user controls: AllowAIGeneratedTiles and AllowAIReorder. These controls are opt-in/opt-out independently; disabling one MUST NOT implicitly disable the other.
When AllowAIGeneratedTiles = false, Dulche/Generative UI MUST NOT create new arbitrary Dashboard tile instances. Existing user-added/system/provider tiles remain usable, and AI MAY still generate content inside a tile whose explicit tile contract permits generated content.
When AllowAIGeneratedTiles = true, Dulche MAY create contextually useful temporary or persisted tiles through the safe Generative UI/CUI schema. Generated tiles MUST declare provenance, the source entities/events they summarise, their lifetime/persistence policy and available typed actions. Generated tiles MUST NOT inject arbitrary executable code.
When AllowAIReorder = false, Dulche MUST NOT move, resize, regroup, reorder or hide existing tiles. When AllowAIReorder = true, Dulche MAY optimise unpinned/unlocked tile placement according to user goals/context, but MUST NOT move or resize tiles marked pinned/locked, MUST preserve explicit hidden-tile choices, and MUST retain an undoable prior layout revision.
AI layout changes MUST be attributable in Events/audit history and MUST be reversible. A user action that manually repositions or pins a tile immediately supersedes older AI layout intent for that tile.
Dashboard tile provider contract
Apps and Home services MAY register Dashboard tile providers through a versioned provider contract. A provider MUST declare TileType, source app/service, supported sizes, required permissions, refresh policy, data dependencies, available actions, whether the tile can be instantiated manually, and whether its content may be generated/modified by Dulche.
Tile data MUST remain source-backed. A tile provider that loses access to its source MUST enter an unavailable/stale state with an explanation rather than silently displaying fabricated current data. Permission revocation MUST prevent future refresh/access and purge or redact cached sensitive content according to the owning source’s policy.
Apps surface and package management
Home Apps is the primary native app catalogue and management surface. It MUST show installed and available 9to1 apps/packages with stable PackageID/AppID, name/icon, installed version, available version, update channel, installation state, dependency/compatibility state, update availability and repair/rollback availability where supported.
Home MUST support install, uninstall, update, repair, launch/open, channel/version selection where allowed and rollback to a validated previous package version where retained. Uninstalling an app MUST NOT silently delete user-created artifacts owned by that app. Artifact-retention/deletion MUST be a separate explicit operation governed by the owning app/storage semantics.
Package installation/update MUST use staged validation and atomic activation. Integrity/signature verification, dependency resolution and Home/shared-service compatibility checks MUST complete before activation. A failed activation MUST leave the previous known-good package usable when rollback data is available.
Home and Launcher MUST consume one canonical package/update database and service. Launcher is the bootstrap/outside-Home client of the same package system; it MUST NOT maintain a second incompatible installer/updater state.
Library
Library is Home’s cross-app artifact index/browser, not a duplicate Files app and not a separate storage authority. It MUST surface canonical references to authorised artifacts across 9to1 apps, including recent, favourite/pinned, shared, generated/created and app/type-filtered content where applicable.
Every Library entry MUST identify the canonical owning app, stable artifact/entity ID, display name, artifact type, relevant location/owner/share metadata and last-modified state. Opening a Library item routes to the owning app/surface and MUST NOT create a duplicate artifact merely because the item is listed in Home.
Library search/filter/sort MUST use the shared search/index service but enforce current permissions at query/open time. Revoked or deleted artifacts MUST not remain usable through stale Library entries.
Events
Events is Home’s ecosystem activity/timeline surface. It is not Planner’s calendar. Events MUST aggregate authorised typed activity from apps/services such as Agent/Automation runs, package/update events, permission/trust decisions, important artifact changes, Mesh/device events, notifications and other meaningful system activity.
Each Event MUST have a stable EventID, timestamp, source app/service, event type, actor/caller identity where relevant, object/entity references, severity/category, human-readable summary and typed deep-link/action references where available. Events MAY reference RequestID/ActionGraphID for AI/agentic activity.
Events MUST preserve source provenance and MUST NOT invent event history from generated summaries. Home MAY generate a concise natural-language digest of events, but the underlying event records remain the authority.
Discover
9-1 Discover is the model browser/discovery surface inside Home. It MUST aggregate model/catalogue information from configured providers rather than depend on one catalogue. Search, filter and comparison MUST support model identity, provider/origin, modality, capabilities, architecture/parameter information when known, context limits, quantisation/format where known, local/cloud status, hardware-fit estimate, install/connection state, entitlement/cost class and privacy/residency information.
Discover MUST treat Chat, Image and Voice as first-class model categories. Advanced discovery additionally exposes Audio and Video models. Voice MUST NOT be buried under Audio: conversational/live voice is a primary model category because it has distinct runtime, quality and capability requirements.
Voice discovery MUST expose capability metadata such as Conversational compatibility, Monologue compatibility, Live Listener compatibility, Live Translate compatibility, visual understanding, tool/action support, streaming, interruption/turn-taking support, supported languages/accents and translation language pairs when known, one-way/bidirectional/multi-language live interpretation support, local/cloud execution, latency characteristics, privacy/residency and entitlement/cost.
Discover MUST recommend the highest-quality compatible Voice models/configurations for the user's required mode and constraints. Recommendation dimensions MAY include reasoning quality, speech naturalness, speech-recognition accuracy, expressiveness, instruction following, turn-taking quality, interruption handling, long-form coherence, audio-context understanding, visual capability, tool reliability and latency. Unknown measurements remain Unknown rather than being invented.
Voice recommendations MUST be contextual rather than a single universal ranking. Discover may surface labels such as Highest quality, Best for Conversational, Best for Monologue, Best for Live Listener, Best for Live Translate, Best local and Fastest when supported by actual capability/evaluation data. Each recommendation MUST explain the relevant reasons/constraints rather than presenting an unexplained badge. Live Translate recommendations should consider speech-recognition accuracy, translation quality, output-speech quality, latency, turn detection, code-switching and multi-language support where measured.
Discover MAY recommend either a native realtime Voice Model or, where 9to1 supports it, a compatible composite voice configuration. Composite implementation detail is secondary to the normal user-facing Voice selection and MUST NOT force ordinary users to manually assemble STT/reasoning/TTS pipelines.
When a selected Voice Model exposes multiple named voices, Discover MUST show those voices as selectable variants with the underlying Voice Model as secondary metadata. Voice-quality/model recommendations and named-voice selection are distinct concepts.
A model listing MUST preserve stable provider-scoped identity even when multiple providers expose the same human-readable model name. Unknown metadata MUST remain unknown rather than being fabricated.
Discover MUST support the relevant install/pull/connect/open-in-picker action for providers that expose those capabilities. Install/connect actions route through Dulche/provider/package APIs and the normal permission/account model.
Universal Model Picker
The Universal Model Picker is the single shared model/provider selection and routing interface for the 9to1 ecosystem. On Windows/regular 9to1 it is hosted by Home; on 9to1-OS the same canonical state is surfaced by the OS. Apps, Agents and AI surfaces MUST NOT create incompatible private model pickers, provider registries or fallback logic when this shared capability applies.
Compact picker and full manager
The compact picker is used inside apps, Agents and AI surfaces when selecting the effective model/route. The full manager lives in Home/Settings → AI/Models and adds provider configuration, installation/acquisition, aliases, defaults, route ordering, background routing, fallbacks, privacy, resource and lifecycle controls.
Entries expose stable Dulche model identity plus user-facing name/alias, provider/source, local/cloud/remote state, modalities/capabilities, tool/structured-output support, reasoning controls, context/output limits, loading/availability, privacy/residency, entitlement/cost where known and local RAM/VRAM fit where meaningful. Display names are never used as canonical identity.
Simple defaults and capability categories
The normal picker keeps the primary capability configuration approachable: Chat Model/Route, Image Model/Route and Voice Model/Voice. Advanced exposes Audio Model/Route and Video Model/Route. The user may instead choose one Active Model/Route and allow all compatible capabilities to inherit it, with ordered fallback resolving unsupported capabilities.
Chat is the primary general-purpose route for conversation, reasoning, writing, coding, tool use, agentic work and multimodal chat where supported.
Image supports an explicit Inherit from Active/Chat route. Inheritance means use that ordered route and its native image-generation/editing-capable candidates; it MUST NOT silently substitute an unrelated unconfigured image provider. A dedicated Image route is an explicit override.
Voice is the first-class conversational/live-voice selection used by Vision & Voice for supported Conversational, Monologue, Live Listener and Live Translate modes. When the selected Voice Model exposes named voices, the user-facing field is labelled Voice and selects VoiceID while showing VoiceModelID as secondary metadata. When there are no named variants the field remains Voice Model.
Advanced Audio covers dedicated transcription, synthesis, audio understanding/transformation or music/audio generation where applicable. Advanced Video covers video generation, editing/transformation or video-native understanding. These category routes may inherit the Active route or use explicit independent ordered routes.
Active and Background routes
Users may configure a single Active Model/Route for all foreground AI work or assign capability-specific/app/Agent overrides. Separately, a Background Model/Route can be configured for non-interactive work such as background summarisation, indexing/classification, Background Learning processing, permitted Automations AI work, proactive suggestions and other low-priority background tasks.
