If no Background route is configured, background work inherits the Active route subject to normal capability/privacy/policy filtering. A task-specific explicit model outranks Agent/app/category defaults; a configured Background route applies only to eligible background work and MUST NOT override an explicit Agent/task requirement.
Ordered Model Routes
Home/Dulche MUST support versioned ordered Model Routes shared by regular 9to1 and 9to1-OS. A Model Route is an ordered list of stable configured model identities plus per-entry enabled/disabled state and routing policy. Users can reorder candidates directly in Home, including by drag/reorder UI, without changing the models' canonical identities.
Example: an Active route may be ChatGPT 6 Sol → Gemma 4 → Fable 5. The ordering means use the highest-priority candidate that is both eligible and available for the request. The router MUST evaluate compatibility before invocation rather than deliberately sending impossible requests to higher entries first.
Foreground and background workloads may use different ordered routes. A user can therefore choose a powerful cloud model first for interactive work while using a small local model first for background work. Users who want simplicity can select a single model and leave fallback entries empty.
Eligibility-first routing
For every routed request Dulche first derives task requirements such as modality/capability, tool use, structured output, context/output requirements, reasoning support and foreground/background role. It then filters candidates against provider/model capability, privacy/locality policy, administrator policy, connection/authentication permission, user fallback policy, entitlement and other hard constraints before considering route priority.
After filtering, Dulche selects the highest-priority available candidate. A lower candidate may be used automatically when a higher candidate is unavailable because of a classified routing condition such as usage/quota exhaustion, provider/model outage, unsupported required capability, context incompatibility, authentication/provider unavailability when another authorised option exists, or local resource insufficiency after permitted reclamation.
Capability mismatch should normally be detected before invocation. For example, if the first two models in a route cannot generate video and the third can, a video-generation request routes directly to the third eligible model rather than failing through the first two.
Conditions that are not model fallback
Model fallback is not a generic retry mechanism. Errors such as missing user files, invalid tool arguments, target-app permission denial, required human approval, business-logic rejection or an external service action failure do not justify silently switching models unless the failure is independently classified as a model/provider-routing condition.
Fallback privacy and control
Each route and candidate can restrict fallback, including no fallback, local-only fallback, cloud-allowed fallback or provider-specific constraints. A route containing cloud candidates does not itself authorise sensitive context to leave the device. Privacy, administrator and task policies are evaluated before route ordering.
A request explicitly pinned to a model with fallback disabled MUST fail transparently rather than silently substitute another model. Likewise a local-only request cannot fall through to cloud merely because the local model is unavailable.
Routing transparency
The effective model and routing reason remain inspectable. Home/Dulche records route identity, selected model and skipped/fallback reasons where relevant, for example 'Sol skipped: usage exhausted; Gemma selected' or 'Sol skipped: video-generation unsupported; Fable selected'. This metadata may be surfaced subtly in normal UI and in more detail through diagnostics/Action Graph without cluttering every response.
Selection inheritance and overrides
The configuration hierarchy MUST be deterministic: request-specific explicit selection → Agent/task override → app/surface override → capability/category route → Background route for eligible background work or Active route for foreground work → configured route fallbacks. A lower-level explicit override wins, while inherited state is visibly distinguishable from an explicit override.
LLM Space and Desktop Space overrides MAY exist but remain scoped. Category overrides are independent; for example an LLM Space may override Chat while inheriting global Image/Voice/Audio/Video routes.
Reasoning and capability validation
The picker renders only reasoning/effort levels actually exposed by the selected model/provider. It MUST NOT invent Low/Medium/High controls for a model that does not support them. Incompatible explicit selections are blocked or clearly explained unless an authorised fallback route can satisfy the requirement.
Aliases and model identity
Users can assign friendly aliases/nicknames to models. Aliases are presentation conveniences and may be duplicated; all routing objects store stable provider-scoped Dulche ModelID values so duplicate names never create ambiguous execution.
Local model lifecycle
Where supported, the full manager provides discover/install or pull, import, verify, download progress, load, unload, remove, update/replace, rollback, storage-location and compatible CPU/GPU/offload configuration. These operations use Dulche Runtime/Den and provider/package APIs rather than a second model-host implementation.
Provider support
Routes may contain compatible local runtimes, configured commercial/cloud providers, self-hosted/OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Ollama, another Dulche device, enterprise endpoints and authorised provider/Plugin implementations. Provider authentication and credentials remain owned by the appropriate shared credential/provider system.
Resource awareness
For local candidates the picker may show estimated RAM/VRAM requirement, current availability, loading state and reclaimable resources when known. On 9to1-OS this integrates with the AI-aware resource manager; on other Home platforms it uses the available Dulche/runtime resource information without pretending OS-level reclamation exists where it does not.
Administrator and managed-profile policy
Managed profiles may limit approved models/providers, acquisition, external cloud use, maximum cost/usage class or fallback destinations. Policy filtering happens before user ordering so reordering a blocked provider cannot bypass a School/organisation restriction.
Universal Model Picker acceptance requirements
Regular 9to1/Home and 9to1-OS use one canonical Dulche model catalogue and versioned routing contract.
Users can use one Active Model for everything compatible or configure separate capability/app/Agent and Background routes.
Ordered model routing automatically falls through on classified quota, availability, capability, context or resource conditions while respecting privacy, permissions and admin policy.
Capability mismatch is filtered before invocation where knowable; model fallback is not misused for unrelated tool/app/business-logic failures.
Users can reorder, enable/disable and inspect route candidates and understand which model ultimately handled a request.
Voice named variants, Image inheritance, Advanced Audio/Video, reasoning controls, aliases and local-model lifecycle preserve the existing category-specific contracts.
Dulche runtime control
Home Core owns the single shared Dulche broker/runtime lifecycle for native 9to1 apps. It MAY host multiple logical endpoints/models concurrently subject to resource policy, but apps MUST attach to the shared broker rather than launching competing private model servers.
Home MUST expose shared Dulche service state including Starting, Ready, Degraded, Restarting and Stopped plus endpoint/model load state, resource pressure and health/diagnostic information required for recovery. Logical EndpointID/SessionID identity remains governed by the Dulche Runtime contract.
If the visible Home shell closes, Home Core MAY continue in the background. If Home Core crashes/restarts, attached apps MUST enter a degraded/reconnecting state for Home-dependent features, preserve their own user data, and reconnect to restored shared services. Apps MUST NOT launch private replacement Dulche servers during recovery.
Permission and trust broker
Home owns the operational permission/trust broker defined by App APIs and automation permissions. It stores and evaluates caller identity, scoped grants, blocks, temporary trust, 30-day Accept and Trust grants, Accept and Always Trust grants, expiry/revocation state and audit history.
Settings MUST expose a Permissions & Trust management surface where the user can inspect caller identity/origin, granted apps/actions/scopes, trust level, creation/expiry, last-use metadata where available, and revoke/block/unblock/narrow grants. Revocation MUST affect future actions immediately subject to in-flight action semantics defined by the target API.
Mesh
Mesh is a Home feature, not a standalone app. It connects authorised user/team devices so selected 9to1 context, projects, Agents and capabilities can operate across devices without requiring every workflow to live entirely in remote cloud infrastructure.
Every Mesh device MUST have a stable DeviceID bound to an authenticated device identity/key rather than a mutable device name. Pairing MUST require explicit user/account authorisation and establish an authenticated encrypted relationship. A device advertises supported 9to1 capabilities/services and versions; peers MUST NOT assume capabilities that were not advertised.
Mesh data sharing/sync MUST be namespace/object scoped. Personal Mesh may sync selected personal Den/chat/context/project state; Team/Organisation modes may sync explicitly shared team/org state while preserving personal/private namespaces. Joining Mesh MUST NOT automatically share all local files, secrets, model context or app data.
Remote capability invocation MUST use typed APIs and pass both caller-side and target-device permission/policy checks. Mesh MUST NOT become an implicit generic remote-desktop, mouse/keyboard or arbitrary-code-execution channel.
Lost/revoked devices MUST be removable from Home. Revocation invalidates future Mesh authentication/session material for that device and prevents further sync/remote calls. Offline devices queue only operations whose owning service explicitly supports safe offline replay/conflict handling.
Action Graph renderer
Home owns the shared user-facing Action Graph renderer/source. Dulche owns execution graph/log data and persistence semantics; Home provides the reusable CUI/Markdown presentation component used to display authorised graph data.
Any authorised app MAY host the shared renderer given an authorised RequestID/ActionGraphID. Home MUST NOT create a second execution history or mutate Dulche’s causal graph merely for presentation. Events, Agents, Spaces and other surfaces MAY deep-link into the same renderer.
Home does not own the primary Voice, Vision or AI Overlay session controls. Those live in Vision & Voice; Home remains responsible only for the shared runtime/model configuration and renderer/platform services they consume.
Persistent contextual AI bar
Home owns the reusable base component/service contract for the global persistent bottom AI bar required by interactive 9to1 apps. The shared component provides CUI rendering, Dulche connection, Universal Model Picker integration, permission/trust plumbing, request state and common Action Graph access.
Each host app MUST provide the bar with a permission-filtered semantic context snapshot and its typed supported actions. Home MUST NOT obtain app context through raw screen scraping when the host provides structured context. App-specific mutation semantics remain owned by the target app APIs.
Floating compose @ invocation menu
The shared Home-owned floating AI compose component MUST provide one searchable @ invocation menu for Plugins, Skills, Apps, Agents and Files. The menu is a single interaction surface with collapsible type sections rather than separate unrelated pickers. Typing @ opens the resource list; typing text after @ filters across all sections while preserving each result's type and identity.
Selecting an item inserts an inline invocation chip/token inside the compose field at the caret position. The rendered token MUST display the resource's icon where available plus its human-readable label, for example an Agent may render as '@[agent icon] John'. The token MUST use a distinct invoked visual state, including colour/style differentiation, while also using non-colour cues for accessibility. Editing/deleting the token removes or changes the invocation rather than leaving invisible hidden attachment state.
Invocation tokens MUST store stable canonical identities, not only display text: Plugin PackageID/version or resolved active version, SkillID/version, AppID, AgentID/DefinitionRevision where required and File/Artifact reference identity/revision or access token as appropriate. Duplicate display names MUST therefore remain unambiguous. The resolved invocation set is included in request metadata, FullLog and Action Graph.
The Plugins section lists Dulche Plugins enabled/available in the current scope; Skills lists eligible Dulche Skills including the built-in Persistent Skill; Agents lists Agents available through Dulche scope resolution; Files searches authorised files/artifacts without silently granting new access. Availability in the picker never grants permission to execute protected actions or read inaccessible content.
The Apps section MUST contain every installed/available first-party 9to1 app plus user-installed applications that 9to1 can classify as safely operable through a typed API/integration or, when separately authorised, Computer Use. App entries MUST expose whether their interaction path is Typed/API, Computer Use Required, or both. Selecting an app whose only route is Computer Use MUST NOT activate Computer Use by itself; the request also requires the explicit @Computer Use invocation.
Game executables and anti-cheat-protected game surfaces MUST be excluded from the operable Apps invocation results even when discovered through Steam, Epic Games Launcher or another launcher/library. If 9to1 cannot confidently distinguish an eligible ordinary application from a game/anti-cheat target, it MUST omit or mark the target unavailable for Computer Use rather than risk automation. Play remains the supported Agent-game route defined by its own contract.
@Computer Use is a reserved first-party system capability entry in the same searchable invocation surface. Selecting it creates the explicit ComputerUseInvocationID required by the Dulche Computer Use contract and makes its active state visible in the compose field before the request is submitted.
Cross-app execution visualisation
Models operating inside any 9to1 app MAY invoke another 9to1 app only when the user's request explicitly names/invokes that app, directly asks for an outcome owned by that app, or unambiguously implies the owning app from the requested artifact/action. For example, 'create a presentation' resolves to Present; 'make a spreadsheet' resolves to Data; an unrelated app MUST NOT be opened merely because the model thinks it might be useful.
Cross-app intent resolution MUST bind to the owning app's stable AppID and typed capability contract. If the required app is not running, Home MAY launch/open it automatically when that is part of fulfilling the request. The target artifact remains canonical in its owning app, and the originating app/Space receives references/status rather than an unmanaged duplicate.
Typed app APIs and shared semantic actions are the normal execution path. Computer Use is not a fallback for missing/failed APIs and remains unavailable unless @Computer Use was explicitly invoked. Permission, review, edit/suggest/view state, conflicts and external-side-effect rules of the target app still apply to cross-app work.
Where an app has a visible editing surface, the user SHOULD be able to watch model-driven edits occur in real time. Home/shared app infrastructure MUST provide an execution-visualisation stream that maps semantic actions to visible UI changes such as objects moving, text appearing, selections changing, slides being created or a virtual cursor hovering over the affected target.
The execution visualiser is representational, not the control mechanism. A virtual cursor MUST be visually distinguishable from the user's real pointer and MUST NOT generate mouse/keyboard input merely to make the animation believable. The canonical typed API/action result remains authoritative; visual animation follows confirmed/provisional semantic events and MUST reconcile to final app state after errors, retries or rollback.
AI conversation presentation settings
Home Settings MUST expose global conversation presentation preferences for Plain text versus Speech bubbles. The preference applies to compatible 9to1 conversational/AI surfaces through the shared renderer rather than each app inventing a different message layout.
User-message alignment and model-message alignment MUST be independently configurable as Left or Right. All four combinations are valid, including both parties on the same side. Alignment changes presentation only and MUST NOT alter message order, authorship, accessibility reading order or exported conversation data.
The selected Dulche thinking-log mode (Precise, Concise, Detailed or Ramble) MUST be configurable in the same AI/conversation settings family. Inline thinking/work regions render beneath or between message text according to chronology; when Speech bubbles are enabled, the thinking/work region visually belongs beneath the relevant model bubble without being styled as ordinary model-authored message text.
Thinking/work presentation MUST use lower visual emphasis than normal chat while remaining readable and accessible. Collapsed 'Thought for ...'/'Worked for ...', ETA status, blockers and Problem events MUST use the same shared renderer across apps so equivalent Runtime state is not represented differently by each product.
Shared Productivity Engine
Home owns the Shared Productivity Engine used by Write, Present, Canvas, Boards and Spaces for overlapping document/object behaviours. The engine is a shared canonical object/rendering/action layer, not five copied implementations. App shells MAY provide different workflows and layout chrome, but a shared object type MUST use the same schema, formatting semantics, rendering rules and typed object actions wherever that type is supported.
The initial required shared object families include rich text/paragraphs, headings, lists/checklists, code blocks, equations, tables, images/media, drawings/ink, graph objects and typed embedded 9to1 artifact references. The registry MUST be extensible so a new shared object type can be implemented once and enabled in multiple supporting surfaces without rewriting its core editor/renderer.
App-specific document structures remain allowed. Present still owns slides and presentation-level layout; Canvas still owns its infinite spatial surface; Boards owns Board/Page hierarchy and Board-specific layout. The shared engine standardises reusable embedded/shared objects rather than forcing one top-level document model.
Canonical object identity, schemas and style registry
Every shared object instance MUST have a stable ObjectID within its owning artifact plus a versioned ObjectType/schema identifier. Object content, formatting, accessibility metadata, asset references and app-neutral layout properties MUST be serialisable independently from transient UI state. Unknown required schema versions MUST fail explicitly rather than being silently flattened or reinterpreted.
Shared object schemas MUST preserve enough information for semantically identical rendering/editing across participating apps. If an app cannot support a property, it MUST retain that property in the object payload when round-tripping and surface the limitation instead of destructively stripping it.
The engine MUST provide a shared versioned style registry for reusable text/paragraph/object style definitions. Style definitions use stable StyleID identity independent of display name so renaming a style does not detach existing objects. App-specific style extensions MAY exist but MUST preserve shared base properties when transferred.
Cross-app copy, paste and embeds
The engine MUST provide a versioned ProductivityObjectBundle clipboard/transfer format containing shared object payloads, style definitions, asset references, accessibility metadata and a portable fallback representation. Copying a supported object from one participating app and pasting it into another MUST preserve the same shared-object semantics and appearance rather than converting it to an image or lossy app-specific approximation.
When the destination supports the same shared object type, paste creates/imports a native shared object instance using the same schema. When the destination does not support that object type but supports embedded 9to1 artifacts, the UI MUST offer an embed/reference path. Destructive flattening is allowed only as an explicit export/paste-as-static action.
Spaces MUST use the Shared Productivity Engine for rich pasted/embedded content so tables, code blocks, drawings, graphs and other shared objects preserve their structure instead of degrading to plain text. Spaces may present a conversational shell around the object, but editing MUST route through the same shared object actions.
Rendering, editing, undo and actions
The engine MUST provide shared selection, focus, formatting, object insertion/removal, resize/transform where applicable, clipboard, accessibility and undoable action primitives for shared object types. Shared actions MUST have stable typed representations so compatible apps can participate in undo/recovery and AI/Automation execution without reproducing hidden per-app commands.
App-specific shells MAY add contextual commands, but MUST NOT fork the underlying object semantics into incompatible versions. Object actions MUST be exposed through typed APIs and usable by UI, Spaces, Automations and Dulche-driven AI without raw UI simulation.
The shared engine MUST emit semantic selection/context information for the persistent AI bar and app-specific contextual toolbars. This context MUST contain stable object/selection identity rather than requiring consumers to infer meaning from rendered pixels.
Drawing engine
The shared engine MUST expose the Rnote-derived drawing/ink engine as a reusable shared object/layer so Canvas and Boards use the same stroke model, pen/eraser behaviours and serialisation primitives. Other productivity surfaces MAY opt into the same drawing object without implementing a separate ink stack.
Deployment boundary and compatibility
Home Core MUST expose the Shared Productivity Engine as a versioned shared platform capability. Apps may link/embed approved shared engine libraries/components as part of their package for rendering performance, but the canonical schema registry, compatibility negotiation and shared service/version authority remain Home-owned. Apps MUST validate compatible engine/schema versions during startup.
Shared object schemas and ProductivityObjectBundle MUST be versioned independently of individual app versions. Home MUST expose compatibility negotiation so an older app can detect a newer unsupported shared object type/property before editing. Compatible unknown optional properties MUST be preserved; incompatible required features MUST produce a structured compatibility state rather than silent data loss.
Shared Productivity Engine API
9to1.ProductivityEngine.ListObjectTypes();
9to1.ProductivityEngine.GetObjectSchema(objectType);
9to1.ProductivityEngine.ListStyles(scope?);
9to1.ProductivityEngine.GetStyle(styleID);

9to1.ProductivityEngine.CanPaste(bundle, targetContext);

9to1.ProductivityEngine.GetCompatibility(appID, appVersion);
The above are minimum cross-app entry points. Each shared object type MUST also expose its typed creation/update/query actions through the owning app/API surface required by the global API-parity rule.
Settings
Home Settings owns ecosystem-wide settings only. The Settings surface MUST include at least Account & Subscription, Appearance/CUI, AI & Models, Permissions & Trust, Apps & Updates, Storage, Mesh & Devices, Privacy, Accessibility, Notifications and Advanced/Diagnostics. App-specific preferences remain in the owning app unless a setting intentionally governs multiple apps.
Settings changes MUST use typed settings keys/schemas with validation and explicit scope (device, account, workspace/team or organisation where applicable). Unknown or incompatible settings versions MUST NOT be silently discarded during upgrade/downgrade.
Account and subscription surface
Home MUST provide the primary native CAKE ID account/subscription surface. It displays authenticated user identity, organisation/workspace context where applicable, current configured subscription/preset source, EntitlementPriceMonthly, EffectiveThresholds, EffectiveEntitlements, AI Dust balance/allocation/usage, storage allocation/usage, site limits/usage and active sessions/devices using server-authoritative values.
Home MUST NOT recalculate paid entitlements locally from a displayed tier label. Checkout, plan changes and sensitive billing management hand off to the trusted authenticated CAKEMODS billing flow defined by the Accounts & Subscription contract. Sign-out/session revocation actions MUST preserve local user data according to each app’s offline/storage policy rather than deleting it by default.
Notifications
Home owns the native 9to1 notification service/centre. Apps publish typed notifications containing NotificationID, source app/service, category/severity, title/body, created time, read/dismissed state, related entity references and typed actions/deep links. Notifications MUST NOT encode consequential behaviour only as arbitrary executable callbacks.
Home MUST support notification history, read/unread state, dismiss/clear subject to retention policy, per-source/category preferences and deep-link actions. Where Windows/9to1-OS system notifications are available, Home MAY bridge eligible notifications to the OS while retaining the canonical 9to1 notification record/state.
Shared search and Go indexing
Home owns/co-ordinates the shared searchable-entity index consumed by Go and Home Library/Search. Apps MUST publish supported searchable entity metadata through a typed indexing contract rather than Home scraping arbitrary app databases.
Search records MUST include stable source app, EntityID/type, title/display metadata, search/index text or vector references as permitted, modification state and current access-scope metadata. Search results MUST re-check current authorisation before exposing sensitive content or opening an entity; stale index access MUST NOT bypass revoked permissions.
On deletion/revocation, apps MUST be able to invalidate/remove affected index records. Home may maintain rebuildable indexes/caches, but the index MUST NOT become the only canonical copy of source content.
Service registry and compatibility handshake
Home Core MUST expose a machine-readable service registry describing Home-owned platform capabilities and versions. At minimum it includes Dulche broker/runtime coordination, permission/trust broker, Shared Productivity Engine, package/update service, notifications, search/index, Mesh and account/session capability availability.
Before normal startup, every native 9to1 app MUST complete a compatibility handshake against Home Core and declare the required service/capability versions it needs. Missing/incompatible required services result in the global Home repair/update/bootstrap flow rather than undefined partial operation.
Service identity/version MUST be explicit; apps MUST NOT infer compatibility solely from the Home marketing version string.
Startup, background lifecycle and recovery
Home Core MUST auto-start on demand or at session startup when required by installed 9to1 apps. Closing the visible Home window MUST NOT necessarily stop Home Core. Home Core shutdown is allowed only when no required dependent operation is active or when the user/system explicitly requests full 9to1 service shutdown.
Home Core persistent state MUST use crash-safe versioned storage. Corrupt or incompatible Home state MUST enter a diagnosable recovery/repair mode; Home MUST NOT silently discard permission grants, package state, device identities or other durable control-plane state to regain startup.
If a Home service fails while apps are open, dependent apps MUST receive a structured service-unavailable/degraded signal. They MUST preserve their own artifact state and block only operations that require the failed service. When the service recovers, clients reconnect/resynchronise through stable IDs/revisions rather than restarting with assumed fresh state.
Home data/state model
Home MUST maintain stable IDs/versioned records for installed packages/apps, Home services, Dashboard layouts/tiles, Mesh devices/pairings, notification records, search index records, permission/trust grants, account/session cache metadata and other Home-owned settings/control-plane entities. Display names, paths and UI ordering are not identity.
Caches/indexes that are rebuildable MUST be marked as non-authoritative. Durable grants, package activation state, device trust and user layout/settings state MUST be recoverable and versioned. Home MUST distinguish device-local state from account/workspace-synchronised state explicitly.

These are minimum canonical entry points. Every additional user-visible Home operation MUST have an equivalent supported API/domain action under the global API-parity rule. APIs MUST return structured state/errors and use stable IDs/revision checks for consequential or concurrent mutations.
Security boundary
Home Core is a high-privilege local control plane. All local IPC/service calls MUST authenticate/identify the caller and evaluate the caller’s effective scopes before exposing privileged operations. Executable filename, window title or self-asserted display name MUST NOT be accepted as caller identity.
Installed signed/registered apps MAY use package identity plus Home-issued process/session credentials. Development/self-built callers MAY use an explicit registered developer/project identity with tamper-evident binding as defined by the global permission model. Trust MUST NOT silently transfer after a material caller identity/signing/content change.
Secrets/credentials MUST be stored through secure credential references and MUST NOT be persisted in plaintext Home configuration, logs, Events, Dashboard tiles or package manifests. Home logs/audits MUST redact secret payloads while retaining accurate action/provenance records.
Platform behaviour
Windows: Home provides the full native hub/shell, Home Core background services and the Home-hosted Universal Model Picker. Native apps depend on the compatible Home installation/Home Core handshake.
9to1-OS: Home Core/shared service contracts remain authoritative platform services, but selected controls may be integrated into OS-native system surfaces. The Universal Model Picker is OS-hosted while using the same canonical Dulche/model/provider state. 9to1-OS MUST NOT create divergent duplicate settings/package/model databases.
Web: the Home web surface uses CAKE ID and server-hosted equivalents for account, Library, Dashboard, notifications, search and other supported cloud capabilities. It MUST capability-negotiate and clearly mark local-only/native-only functions such as local package management, local models/devices or unavailable Home Core services rather than pretending they exist in-browser.
Failure behaviour
Home APIs/services MUST return structured failures including HomeServiceUnavailable, HomeServiceIncompatible, PackageIntegrityFailed, PackageDependencyConflict, PackageActivationFailed, DashboardRevisionConflict, TileProviderUnavailable, PermissionDenied, DeviceRevoked, MeshUnavailable, IndexUnavailable and AccountServiceUnavailable in addition to the global error contract.
Failures in one Home service MUST NOT automatically corrupt or erase unrelated Home state. For example, Discover/provider failure must not invalidate package state; search-index corruption must be recoverable by rebuilding the index; Dashboard tile-provider failure must degrade only affected tiles.
Acceptance requirements
Home is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:
A native app refuses normal startup when Home is not installed and successfully resumes through the trusted Install Home/bootstrap flow.
Closing the visible Home window does not break dependent apps while Home Core remains healthy.
A Home Core/service crash produces structured degraded state in attached apps, preserves user artifacts and reconnects after service recovery without spawning duplicate private services.
Dashboard manual tile add/remove/resize/reorder/pin state persists across restart and responsive window sizes.
AllowAIGeneratedTiles=false prevents arbitrary generated tile creation while existing tiles continue to function.
AllowAIReorder=false prevents AI movement/layout changes; when enabled, AI cannot move pinned/locked tiles and every AI layout change is reversible.
Generated Dashboard tiles expose source provenance and fail stale/unavailable rather than fabricating live data.
Apps install/update/repair/rollback uses the shared package database and survives a failed staged activation without deleting user artifacts.
Library opens the same canonical artifact in its owning app rather than creating a duplicate.
Events preserve typed source records and link to the corresponding Action Graph/entity where applicable.
Discover aggregates at least two configured model/provider sources without identity collisions and performs a valid install/connect action.
Universal Model Picker override precedence and fallback policy resolve deterministically and do not cross local-to-cloud boundaries when policy forbids it.
Permission/trust grants can be inspected, narrowed/revoked/blocked and future calls immediately respect the updated state.
Mesh pairing establishes stable device identity; capability calls obey both ends’ permissions; device revocation prevents subsequent sync/invocation.
Home notifications preserve read/dismiss state and typed deep links across restart and OS notification bridging.
Search/Library results stop exposing content after permission revocation/deletion and indexes can be rebuilt without source-data loss.
A representative shared productivity object can round-trip across Write, Present, Canvas, Boards and Spaces through the Shared Productivity Engine without schema/format loss.
Account/subscription values shown in Home match the server-authoritative CAKE ID entitlement state and are not inferred from preset labels.
An app with an incompatible required Home service version is blocked into update/repair instead of running against an undefined interface.
Home persistent control-plane state can recover from process interruption without silently dropping package activation state, device trust or permission grants.
Node Graph Framework
Home owns the shared Node Graph Framework used by Automations and Space graph editors. It is an editing/schema/validation/execution-visualisation framework, not a second automation or AI runtime. Product surfaces register domain-specific events, actions and node types; Dulche and owning apps execute the resulting authorised runtime actions.
The framework MUST provide a versioned graph data model, stable GraphID/NodeID/PortID identity, node registry, typed input/output ports, typed connections, node configuration schemas, pan/zoom/selection, grouping/comments, copy/paste/duplicate, undo/redo, validation, Draft/Active graph revision support, execution-state overlays and contextual AI-bar integration.
Connections MUST be type-checked. Incompatible ports cannot connect unless an explicit registered conversion node exists. Nodes and graph actions MUST reference canonical stable app/capability/entity IDs rather than screen coordinates or UI implementation details.
The framework MUST support product-defined capability profiles. For example, built-in Spaces receive a constrained Events & Extensions node registry while user-created Spaces and Automations may receive broader registries. A capability profile cannot expose an action prohibited by the product/security contract.
Graph mutation from the contextual AI bar MUST use typed graph APIs. AI may add/remove/configure nodes and connections only within the current capability profile and permissions, and MUST NOT simulate mouse/keyboard graph editing.
9to1.NodeGraph.Get(graphID);
9to1.NodeGraph.Create(config);
9to1.NodeGraph.AddNode(graphID, nodeType, config?);
9to1.NodeGraph.RemoveNode(graphID, nodeID);
9to1.NodeGraph.SetProperty(graphID, nodeID, property, value);
9to1.NodeGraph.Connect(graphID, outputPortID, inputPortID);
9to1.NodeGraph.Disconnect(graphID, connectionID);
9to1.NodeGraph.Validate(graphID, revision?);
9to1.NodeGraph.Activate(graphID, revision);
9to1.NodeGraph.ListNodeTypes(capabilityProfile);
Node Graph Framework compatibility and migration MUST be versioned. When a node/hook schema is retired, affected graphs enter a diagnosable migration/needs-attention state rather than silently dropping nodes or connections.
9to1 Admin
ADM-01 — Product role, access and platforms
9to1 Admin is a standalone Business-exclusive 9to1 application, not a renamed account-settings page or WordPress administration screen. It is the organisation-management interface for the Business features specified separately under Business features — functional specification. Business and Business + include it; the account-bound free Business grant defined for Jacob also applies. App access does not grant administrative permissions: every operation additionally requires the appropriate role and target scope.
Admin MUST have Windows, 9to1-OS and browser/web surfaces sharing the same CAKE ID, organisation entities, domain APIs and permission evaluation. Native clients use Home’s shared services. The web app uses authenticated shared web services without requiring a local Home installation for ordinary organisation administration. Device operations require an enrolled compatible endpoint; a browser cannot directly enforce unsupported local OS controls. Unsupported capabilities MUST remain distinguishable from denied permission or an offline device.
Admin owns management workflows and policy editing. The account/billing service owns subscriptions and ledgers; Spaces owns Team Spaces; Files owns shared-drive content; Connect owns communications; Home/Mesh owns pairing and device-resource execution; Dulche/Den owns Agents; the 9to1-OS policy service owns endpoint enforcement. Admin MUST invoke these canonical services rather than create duplicate content, Agent registries, payment records or a competing permission broker. This is a native CUI product built on those existing services; no new paid administration donor or hosting service is selected by this specification.
ADM-02 — Navigation and organisation lifecycle
The start screen MUST list organisations the user can manage, with an explicit organisation switcher and current organisation identity on every administrative screen. Navigation MUST include Overview; People; Roles & Permissions; Policies; Models, Apps & Features; Plugins & Settings; Usage & Credits; Billing; Team Space & Drive; Connect; Devices & Mesh; Team Agents; and Audit & Activity. Visibility is permission-filtered, while denial states explain the required capability without leaking inaccessible organisations.
Overview MUST show member/seat counts, resource allocation and consumption, pending invitations/approvals, policy-deployment status, blocked actions, device health and billing state, each with source freshness. Unknown or stale values MUST NOT appear as zero or healthy. Search, filtering, accessible keyboard operation, bulk-selection previews and per-item bulk results are required. Admin is not an artifact editor: blank-document/template import surfaces are not applicable; organisation creation, invitation and configuration import/export replace them.
Authorised owners MUST be able to create and edit organisation identity, manage ownership, inspect linked Business entitlement, archive/reactivate the organisation and request export or deletion. Ownership transfer requires authenticated acceptance by the recipient; removing or suspending the last active owner MUST be rejected. Archive is recoverable and distinct from permanent deletion. Deletion requires an impact preview, explicit confirmation and the applicable retention/export workflow, and MUST NOT delete a member’s personal account or personal artifacts.
ADM-03 — People, roles and permissions
People management MUST support invite, resend/revoke invitation, accept, list/search, assign/change roles, suspend, reinstate and remove membership. Membership states MUST distinguish Invited, Active, Suspended and Removed, with stable MembershipID and UserID. Invitations are time-bounded and single-use for the intended identity. Acceptance and capacity reservation MUST be transactional so concurrent requests cannot bypass the seat cap. The UI MUST distinguish members, pending/reserved invitations and external Connect correspondents; corresponding counting rules must be explicit, not hidden billing assumptions.
Roles MUST be editable capability sets, not just labels. Provide owner, administrator and member roles, plus separately assignable billing, usage-reporting, device-management, Agent-management and audit-reading capabilities. Custom roles MUST support scoped read, add/edit, delete/recovery and specialised administrative actions. A role editor MUST show effective permissions and inherited restrictions. A delegated administrator MUST NOT grant capabilities outside their own delegation boundary, elevate themselves to owner or modify protected grants. Membership alone does not grant access to every shared document, private conversation or Agent memory.
Suspension/removal MUST revoke organisation sessions/capabilities, block new organisation-funded jobs, remove applicable shared access and reconcile owned organisation resources and outstanding reservations. Show a transfer/reassignment preview for shared assets, scheduled Automations and Agent responsibilities. Already completed external actions remain historical facts. Revocation MUST leave personal accounts and unrelated organisations intact; offline devices must report pending revocation until enforcement is acknowledged.
ADM-04 — Enforced policy editor
Administrators MUST be able to enforce organisation-wide and role-specific policies, inspect their effective result for a selected member/device/Agent, and preview affected objects before publication. PolicySet and PolicyAssignment records MUST carry stable IDs, schema version, revision, scope, author, effective time and change reason. A change follows Draft → Validated → Published, with per-target delivery/enforcement status; publication is not proof that an offline endpoint applied it.
Restrictions MUST cover model/provider access; apps; individual app features/actions; Plugins and their capabilities; Agents and Automations, including creation, editing, invocation, schedules and external side effects. Restricted capabilities must be enforced by the owning service at dispatch, not merely hidden in the UI. APIs, command-line tools, modified clients and nested Agent/Plugin calls receive the same policy decisions.
Effective capability grants are the intersection of server entitlement, delegated role, organisation/role policy, object access, caller trust and applicable device/privacy restrictions. A denial at a required boundary cannot be overridden by a broader grant elsewhere. Conflicting mandatory settings or required-versus-blocked Plugin rules MUST produce a validation conflict instead of an arbitrary last-write-wins outcome. New sensitive requests remain subject to Home’s normal approval rules.
ADM-05 — Required Plugins, forced settings and default models
Admin MUST support required organisation-wide Plugins and additional requirements by role, with package identity, approved version/update policy, required configuration and deployment status. Required does not mean silently trusted: package integrity, compatibility, requested scopes and secret connections must validate before enablement. A blocked or failed required Plugin produces an actionable non-compliance state. Disabling an unsafe Plugin remains possible for authorised security response; updates cannot widen permissions without the required approval.
Administrators MUST be able to force supported organisation/role settings and separately supply editable defaults. Members see the effective value, whether it is locked and which policy supplies it. Settings must be addressed by versioned typed keys supported by the target app/device; unsupported settings cannot be reported as applied. Forced settings affect only the managed scope and cannot silently rewrite personal settings outside it.
Default-model configuration MUST support organisation defaults and role-specific defaults, plus permitted user overrides. The effective model must also satisfy model restrictions, entitlement, capability, privacy and local/cloud routing rules. An unavailable or prohibited default blocks with a clear reason or uses an explicitly authorised fallback; it MUST NOT silently send private local-only content to a cloud provider. Conflicting forced role defaults must be resolved explicitly in policy configuration before publication.
ADM-06 — Subscription assignment, usage controls and rollover
Usage & Credits MUST let authorised administrators assign a funded subscription/resource configuration to a member or role, choose a shared organisation pool or individually partitioned allocations, set limits, inspect consumption/reservations and move eligible unspent organisation-owned allocation between partitions. Changing a display tier or role MUST NOT mint credits, unlock an unfunded model band or duplicate an allocation. A cost-changing assignment requires the Billing approval flow rather than silently purchasing resources.
Controls MUST include organisation, role and member ceilings for AI usage and applicable storage/site resources; warnings and hard-stop behaviour; configured time windows; and model/Agent/Automation attribution. A hard ceiling is enforced before work is admitted. No paid overage or automatic top-up is enabled merely because a warning threshold is crossed. Reports MUST separate allocated, available, reserved, consumed, rolled-over and expired credits and display the reset/expiry policy and freshness.
Admins MUST be able to configure, by role, whether eligible expired/expiring credits may roll over, with explicit inheritance, allow or disallow settings and the supported carryover period/cap. This is a real server-enforced credit-lifecycle rule, not an interface label. Credit lots retain source allocation, original expiry, rollover policy/version and resulting expiry, with an auditable rollover event. Changes cannot spend the same credit twice or alter settled usage. Eligibility, funding and allowed carryover bounds come from the versioned billing policy; unresolved commercial durations are OPEN rather than guessed. Members MUST see their effective rollover rule.
ADM-07 — Billing, invoices and reporting
Billing MUST expose the current Business add-on, seat capacity, funded resource configurations, invoice/payment status and authorised invoice download, plus a preview of changes and their effective date. Separate the fixed organisation add-on from AI/storage/other resource costs. There is no per-seat fee. Usage allocation may change resource cost, but an invitation or role assignment must not conceal a seat charge.
Purchases, upgrades or other spending require an authorised human’s explicit approval of a current quote identifying organisation, currency, itemised amount, recurring terms and effective date. Paid carrier numbers, third-party services and hosting are separate spending decisions. Approval must be bound to the quote/version and protected against replay; a changed or expired quote requires a new decision. Raw payment details remain in the trusted billing flow, never in Admin client code, Plugins, prompts or logs.
Analytics MUST offer permission-filtered totals and breakdowns by period, member, role, model, app, Agent and pool, with exportable reports and reconciliation to ledger events. Estimates/forecasts are labelled separately from settled charges. Reporting is operational accounting, not covert inspection of message contents, documents or personal activity. Personal-account usage is excluded unless explicitly and validly brought into the organisation billing scope.
ADM-08 — Shared resources, devices and team Agents
Team Space & Drive MUST manage organisation ownership, role/group access, sharing restrictions, storage limits, access reviews, archival/recovery and export through Spaces/Files. Connect management MUST cover the organisation directory, channels/groups, delegated organisational identities, allowed external contact and Agent channel bindings through Connect. Administrative metadata access does not create a plaintext backdoor to encrypted or private conversations.
Devices & Mesh MUST expose enrolled devices, owner/account, platform, supported capabilities, trust/enrolment state, last contact, effective policy and resource contributions. Authorised actions MUST include enrolment approval, group/role assignment, policy deployment, access/resource revocation and inspection of acknowledged enforcement. Cross-account Mesh grants require explicit enrolled-device trust and configured compute/storage limits. A stale/offline device remains Pending or Unknown; a submitted command is not reported as executed.
Team Agents MUST list canonical organisation Agents and support create/import, assign owner/scope, edit/publish versions, configure model/tools/required Plugins and budgets, share invocation access, schedule approved work, pause/resume/stop, archive/recover and inspect authorised run history. AI Studio opens the same Agent for detailed authoring. Administrative control cannot silently copy private user memories, credentials or grants into a shared Agent. Revoked members cannot keep invoking an organisation Agent through an old endpoint.
ADM-09 — Audit, failure and recovery
Consequential management actions MUST record AuditEventID, OrgID, verified actor/delegation, action and target IDs, timestamp, policy/revision, approval reference where required, redacted before/after state and observed outcome. Policy evaluation denials, privilege changes, billing approvals, credit adjustments, device grants and Agent publication/revocation are auditable. Audit permission is separate from content access; secrets and unnecessary personal content are excluded. Administrators cannot silently edit historical audit entries.
Mutations use optimistic revision checks and idempotency keys. Multi-target jobs expose JobID, target-level Succeeded/Failed/Pending/Skipped/RolledBack states, retry eligibility and cancellation limits. Failed policy rollout retains the last acknowledged safe policy and offers scoped rollback, not an invented all-success state. Unknown billing/external-action outcomes must be reconciled before retry. Offline administrative clients may inspect permitted cached metadata with a stale marker but cannot assert that a new server policy or purchase has taken effect.
ADM-10 — Canonical data and API contract
Canonical records MUST include Organisation, Membership, Role, CapabilityGrant, PolicySet, PolicyAssignment, ResourcePool, MemberAllocation, CreditLot, DeviceEnrolment, MeshGrant, TeamAgentBinding, Approval, AdminJob and AuditEvent. Each carries stable IDs, OrgID where applicable, lifecycle and revision/schema metadata. Identity and subscription authority remain server-side; caches are derived and permission-filtered. Exports omit secrets and preserve portable configuration plus dependency references; imports validate compatibility and require a dry-run/impact preview before mutation.
The canonical management namespace is 9to1.Admin. Required action families are Organisations (List, Get, Create, Update, TransferOwnership, Archive, Restore, Export, RequestDeletion); Members (List, Invite, RevokeInvitation, AcceptInvitation, SetRoles, Suspend, Reinstate, Remove); Roles (List, Create, Update, Delete, GetEffectivePermissions); Policies (Get, Preview, Validate, Publish, GetDeployment, Rollback); Resources (GetUsage, SetAllocation, SetLimits, TransferAllocation, SetRolloverPolicy); Billing (GetConfiguration, PreviewChange, OpenCheckout, ListInvoices, DownloadInvoice); SharedResources (Get, PreviewAccessChange, ApplyAccessChange); Devices (List, Enrol, AssignPolicy, Revoke, GetEnforcement); Mesh (ListGrants, Grant, Revoke, SetLimits); Agents (List, Bind, Configure, Publish, SetAccess, SetBudget, ControlRun, Archive, Restore); and Audit/Jobs (List, Get, Export, Cancel where cancellable). Domain operations dispatch to their existing owning service; these are management entry points, not duplicate runtime implementations.
Every action contract MUST declare typed arguments/results, permission scope, risk, reversibility and external effects. Scoped requests include OrgID and stable target IDs; mutations include ExpectedRevision and IdempotencyKey. Collection APIs provide cursor pagination and bounded page sizes; jobs provide JobID, status and target results. Success returns canonical IDs, new revision and applied/pending status. Failures return structured codes including PermissionDenied, EntitlementRequired, SeatLimitReached, PolicyDenied, PolicyConflict, RevisionConflict, InsufficientCredits, QuotaExceeded, ApprovalRequired, QuoteExpired, DeviceOffline, UnsupportedCapability and ProviderUnavailable, with recoverability/retry metadata. UI-only management actions are non-conformant.
ADM-11 — Acceptance and release gates
Acceptance MUST prove: a non-Business account cannot gain Admin capabilities; Business access without an admin role does not grant privileged operations; Jacob’s verified free grant works without enabling another account; a Business organisation with 50 active seats cannot admit a 51st concurrently; and Business + has no subscription seat cap while ordinary resource/security limits still apply. Verify that adding an unfunded seat never creates a seat invoice.
End-to-end tests MUST cover organisation ownership transfer and last-owner protection; invite/suspend/remove with immediate server access revocation; custom-role restrictions through UI and direct API; blocked models/apps/features/Plugins/Automations; required Plugins by organisation and role; forced settings and default-model conflicts; shared versus individual budgets; role-based rollover; concurrency-safe credit reservation/settlement; itemised quote approval and retry protection; shared-resource ACLs; cross-account Mesh opt-in/revocation; and team-Agent isolation and lifecycle.
Platform tests MUST cover Windows, 9to1-OS and web, including browser administration without local Home, unsupported endpoint controls and offline rollout remaining pending. Test restart/persistence, stale revisions, partial bulk failure, rollback, secret redaction, report reconciliation, keyboard/focus/screen-reader operation and equivalent API behaviour. Lists MUST remain paginated, exports/rollouts asynchronous where long-running, and expensive reports must not block policy checks. A rendered dashboard or stub action is not implementation completion.
ADM-12 — Explicit open decisions
OPEN: exact billing-period and carryover durations/caps not already fixed by the authoritative subscription policy; how pending and suspended memberships count toward reserved seat capacity; any Business +-only feature beyond the absence of a seat cap; contractual retention/support commitments; and supported version boundaries for endpoint management. These require explicit canonical decisions before the relevant behaviour ships. Do not invent paid SSO/SCIM, unlimited compute/storage, support SLAs, remote full-device wipe or access to personal content as implicit Business features.
Files
Product role and donor-first implementation
9-1 Files is both the native CUI file-manager app and the 9to1 hosted storage service. The desktop/native product is donor-backed by Files/WinUI and MUST first reach behavioural/layout parity with the selected appropriate donor source before 9to1-specific extensions are treated as complete. CUI replaces the rendering/framework layer; the donor’s mature information architecture, workflows, interaction semantics and quality-of-life behaviour remain the baseline unless a scoped donor-parity exception is recorded.
The parity baseline includes applicable donor navigation/sidebar structure, toolbar/commands, tabs, back/forward history, breadcrumbs/address bar, file/folder views, details/grid layouts, sorting/grouping, context menus, properties, previews, search, tags/favourites, drag/drop, clipboard, archives, network/location handling, keyboard shortcuts, selection behaviour, file-operation UX, progress/conflict dialogs, session restoration and other user-visible donor behaviours available in the selected legally usable source.
A donor-parity manifest MUST identify the selected donor revision and classify each applicable donor feature as Preserve, Replace with 9to1-native equivalent or Not applicable. Proprietary donor AI is not copied; equivalent AI functionality uses Dulche/9to1 APIs. Subscription/account infrastructure specific to the donor is not inherited unless independently required by this specification.
Authority and ownership boundaries
Files owns file/folder identity, hosted storage, locations/providers, structural hierarchy, transfers, sync, versions, sharing/ACLs, Trash/recovery, file-operation history and filesystem-level collaboration. Files does NOT own semantic editing/collaboration inside another app’s document/project format.
The owning app remains authoritative for semantic file content and live in-document collaboration: Write owns Write-document collaboration, Present owns presentations, Boards owns Boards content, Canvas owns Canvas content, Data owns workbook/database semantics and Stack owns Git/Stack source-control semantics. Files stores and synchronises durable revisions produced by those apps but MUST NOT attempt to merge paragraphs, spreadsheet cells, Board blocks, Canvas strokes or Git histories generically.
Raw/unowned binary/text files use Files’ revisioned-content storage model. When two clients concurrently modify bytes and no owning semantic merge engine exists, Files MUST preserve both conflicting revisions or expose a structured conflict; it MUST NOT silently choose the newest wall-clock timestamp.
Canonical identity and item model
Every 9to1-hosted file and folder MUST have a stable FileID or FolderID independent of name, path, sort position or parent. Rename and move MUST preserve identity. Paths are human-facing projections of hierarchy and MUST NOT be used as canonical identity by other 9to1 apps.
Hosted file metadata MUST include at least FileID, ParentFolderID, Name, ItemType, content/media type, owner/scope, size, created/modified timestamps, current content revision, sync/availability state, sharing state and version metadata. Folders MUST expose equivalent stable identity and ordered/queriable child relationships.
Synced local materialisations of 9to1 Drive items MUST retain metadata linking the local file to the canonical hosted FileID and base/current remote revision. Identity MUST NOT be reconstructed from pathname alone.
Locations and provider abstraction
Files MUST expose all storage roots through one typed Location/Provider abstraction. Required native location classes include 9to1 Drive, local disks, removable storage and supported network locations. Connected cloud providers MAY be added through adapters.
Every provider MUST declare capabilities explicitly, including read, write, rename, move, copy, trash, permanent delete, versions, sharing, offline availability, search, streaming, server-side copy/move, change feeds and any provider-specific constraints. The UI and APIs MUST disable/report unsupported operations rather than pretending parity exists.
Provider authentication and secrets MUST be stored through secure credential references. Provider-specific OAuth/tokens MUST NOT be persisted in plaintext Files configuration or logs.
Desktop shell, tabs and views
The CUI desktop shell MUST preserve the donor’s applicable tabbed browsing, navigation history, breadcrumbs/address bar, command toolbar, sidebar/location hierarchy, selection behaviour and view-management semantics. Session restore MUST reopen the prior tab/location set where available; unavailable removable/network locations restore into an explicit unavailable state rather than being silently discarded.
Grid/list/details and other applicable donor view modes MUST be supported. Sort, group, visible columns, thumbnail size and compatible folder/view preferences MAY persist per-folder or per-location according to provider capability.
Folder colour customisation
Files MUST support native folder-colour customisation independently of any OneDrive-specific donor capability. Users can choose from presets or an arbitrary colour using a full colour wheel/picker, apply the chosen presentation to a folder and reset it to the default appearance.
Folder colour is Files presentation metadata associated with the stable folder identity, not a pathname-only hack. It must work for local folders and 9to1-hosted folders and should work for connected-provider folders where provider capability or Files-owned metadata permits. A provider that lacks native folder-colour metadata MUST NOT force Files to disable the feature if the presentation override can safely be stored by Files.
Where compatible with sync/account policy, folder-colour metadata may follow the canonical folder across devices. Files MUST expose the same typed operation to Dulche and Automations, enabling actions such as changing selected/project folder colours without GUI automation.
Native 9to1 creation and project integration
Files MUST replace Office-centric creation defaults with first-class 9to1 creation entries. The toolbar/context New menu MUST include at least Folder, Write document, Presentation, Spreadsheet/Data artifact, Board, Canvas and Stack project when the current location/provider can store the requested artifact.
Creation MUST invoke the owning app’s canonical API rather than having Files manufacture private document internals. For example, creating a Write document from Files calls the Write creation API and receives the resulting canonical ArtifactID/FileID. Files owns placement/storage; the owning app owns document structure.
Files MUST support Create Stack here and Create Stack from this folder for appropriate folders. The latter registers/imports the existing source location as a Stack project rather than creating a nested duplicate source tree. Stack identity/backing remains owned by Stack; Files supplies the selected backing location/reference.
App/project folders MAY expose a project-aware representation so users see a meaningful project entity instead of internal managed metadata by default. Advanced inspection MAY reveal underlying files when the owning app permits it. Files MUST respect app-managed/protected metadata markers and warn/block casual destructive edits that would corrupt managed project state.
9to1 Drive integration
9to1 Drive MUST appear directly in the normal Files sidebar/location tree alongside local drives and other providers. Hosted storage MUST NOT open into a separate incompatible cloud-files UI. Desktop, web and owning apps address the same canonical hosted objects by stable IDs.
A file uploaded through cakemods.com and later opened in desktop Files MUST refer to the same FileID/content revision, not a separately imported desktop copy. Local materialisation is a cache/replica of the hosted object associated with FileID/revision metadata.
Hosted storage MUST expose quota/allocation, used space and pending/reserved upload space where applicable. Quota exhaustion MUST fail structurally and MUST NOT leave invisible orphan uploads.
Rapid push-based sync architecture
Sync is a core correctness requirement. 9to1 Drive MUST use event/push-driven incremental synchronisation as the normal connected path. Polling/full rescans are recovery/fallback mechanisms and MUST NOT be the primary source of ordinary change propagation.
The server MUST produce ordered change events for filesystem-level changes including create, rename, move, metadata change, content-revision commit, delete, restore, share/ACL changes and relevant availability/sync metadata changes. Connected clients maintain a durable SyncCursor/last acknowledged server revision and apply deltas incrementally.
On reconnect, a client submits its last durable cursor plus pending local operation journal state; the server returns deltas since that cursor, the client reconciles queued local operations, then resumes the live stream. Duplicate/replayed operation IDs MUST be idempotent and MUST NOT perform consequential mutations twice.
Ordinary metadata operations such as rename/move/create MUST be pushed immediately after commit and processed continuously by connected clients. Intentional multi-minute delays for normal metadata propagation are non-conformant. Foreground/open artifacts and explicit manual sync receive scheduling priority over background hydration/prefetch.
Optimistic local operations
User-initiated structural operations SHOULD feel immediate. Files MAY optimistically apply a local rename/move/create to the UI before the remote round trip, but MUST record the operation durably as Pending with OperationID, expected/base revision and inverse/recovery metadata.
If the server accepts the mutation, the operation becomes committed/synced and remote clients receive the corresponding event. If validation fails, Files MUST reconcile/reverse the optimistic state and display the structured reason; it MUST NOT leave the UI pretending the server accepted a rejected mutation.
Sync and availability state
Hosted items MUST expose explicit sync/availability state rather than a generic spinner. Required states include CloudOnly, Hydrating, AvailableOffline, AlwaysAvailable, LocalChanges, Uploading, Synced, Conflict, Paused and Error. Internal implementations MAY maintain separate content and metadata states so lightweight metadata can become synced while content transfer continues.
CloudOnly means metadata is locally visible but content bytes are not guaranteed local. AvailableOffline means content is currently materialised and may be evicted by managed cache policy only when safe. AlwaysAvailable means the user has pinned the content and Files MUST retain a local copy until the user changes that policy or storage becomes critically unavailable and the user explicitly resolves the situation.
Opening, previewing or an owning app requesting bytes for CloudOnly content triggers hydration on demand. Hydration MUST expose progress/failure and MUST NOT claim the item is locally available before durable content validation completes.
Manual sync and sync-on-demand
Files MUST provide visible manual sync controls, including Sync now, Sync this item, Sync this folder/selection, Pause sync, Resume sync, retry eligible failures and refresh/reconcile from cloud. Manual sync is an acceleration/reconciliation control, not a substitute for reliable automatic sync.
Sync now MUST flush eligible pending local mutations, request current server deltas since the durable cursor, retry eligible transfers, reconcile conflicts that have deterministic policy and report the resulting pending/error/conflict state. It MUST NOT discard unsynced changes merely to match cloud state.
Offline-first behaviour
Locally materialised files/folders MUST remain usable offline according to their owning app/file-format capabilities. While offline, Files MUST allow safe queued structural operations including create folder, rename, move, delete/restore and reorganisation, and it MUST allow edits to locally available content through the owning app.
Offline mutations enter a durable ordered operation journal that survives Files/Home/process/device restart. On reconnect, operations are reconciled against remote revisions/permissions before commit. Blind last-write-wins based solely on timestamps is prohibited for conflicts.
Free up space MUST verify that the canonical hosted revision is durable and equivalent/newer before evicting local bytes. Items with unsynced local content MUST NOT be evicted. AlwaysAvailable items MUST NOT be evicted by normal cache cleanup.
Real-time filesystem collaboration
Files MUST provide real-time collaboration for filesystem structure and Files-owned metadata. Connected authorised clients viewing the same hierarchy should receive live create, rename, move, delete/restore, share/ACL and metadata updates without requiring manual refresh.
Structural mutations MUST carry stable OperationID, actor/caller identity, target object ID, base/expected revision, operation type and result revision. Simultaneous incompatible structural edits MUST produce a deterministic RevisionConflict/Conflict object rather than silently letting whichever request arrived last overwrite the other.
If an owning app has a file open by FileID and another collaborator moves/renames that file, Files MUST publish LocationChanged/metadata events while preserving FileID. The owning app continues editing the same canonical file without losing attachment simply because the path changed.
Semantic collaboration inside a file is exclusively owned by the file’s owning app. Files receives/commits durable revisions from that collaboration layer and exposes version/storage metadata, but it MUST NOT run a second generic content-collaboration engine over the same file.
Transfers
Copy, move, upload, download and provider-transfer operations MUST be represented as durable Transfer jobs with TransferID, item set, source/destination, bytes/items totals where known, progress, state, retryability, error list and pause/resume/cancel support where technically possible.
Hosted uploads/downloads MUST use resumable/chunked transfer when the service/provider supports it. Files/Home restart MUST resume from validated committed chunks where possible rather than restarting large transfers from zero.
Transfer completion MUST include integrity validation where hashes/checksums are supported. Integrity failure is a failed transfer and MUST NOT be represented as successful-with-warning.
Destination conflicts MUST use explicit policy: Ask, Replace, KeepBoth or Skip, with ApplyToRemaining where appropriate. Automated callers MUST specify a policy or receive ConflictRequiresDecision.
Version history and durable revisions
9to1 Drive files MUST have durable version history. Each durable revision MUST include VersionID/RevisionID, timestamp, actor/source, parent/base revision where relevant and content identity/hash where available. Restoring an older revision MUST create a new current revision or otherwise preserve the later history rather than deleting it.
Owning apps MAY commit incremental/semantic collaboration checkpoints, but Files stores the durable file/artifact revision boundary supplied by the app. Files MUST not reinterpret app-specific internal history as generic filesystem versions unless the owning app explicitly publishes those revisions.
Trash, delete and recovery
Normal hosted deletion MUST be soft/recoverable. Trash records MUST preserve stable item ID, original parent/location, deletion timestamp and restoration metadata. Permanent purge is a distinct high-risk operation.
Deleting a Files container or reference MUST NOT silently cascade-permanently-delete separately owned embedded/project artifacts unless the owning app explicitly defines cascade semantics and Files presents the impact before execution.
Sharing and ACLs
Hosted files/folders MUST support first-class sharing using stable account/team/organisation principal IDs. Required ACL concepts include owner, direct grants, inherited grants and viewer/editor-style capability roles or their equivalent typed scopes.
Folder permission inheritance MUST distinguish inherited from direct grants. Moving an item between differently permissioned folders MUST calculate/result in an explicit effective permission change and MUST NOT silently retain/remove direct grants contrary to the configured inheritance policy.
Shared with Me MUST reference canonical objects owned elsewhere rather than cloning them into the recipient’s Drive. Revocation affects future access immediately subject to already-downloaded/offline-data retention policy.
If public/link sharing is supported, link shares MUST use revocable ShareID/token state with explicit permission level and optional expiry/password where implemented. Raw file URLs MUST NOT themselves imply authority.
Search, metadata and previews
Files MUST support filename/folder search plus indexed metadata/content search where provider/file-type policy permits. Files publishes supported searchable entities to Home’s shared index; current permissions are rechecked when rendering/opening results.
Common item metadata MUST include provider/location, type, size, relevant timestamps, owner/sharing, sync/offline state, current revision and hashes/integrity data where available. App-specific metadata MUST be namespaced/versioned.
Files MUST provide preview/thumbnail contracts. Owning apps/providers MAY register read-only preview renderers for native artifacts. Preview MUST NOT mutate the source artifact or require launching a full app window unless no lightweight preview capability exists.
Open routing, context actions and drag/drop
Home’s app/file-handler registry determines default/open-with routing. Native 9to1 artifacts MUST expose enough type/version metadata that routing is not dependent solely on filename extension. Users MAY choose alternate compatible handlers where supported.
Installed apps MAY contribute typed registered context actions based on item type/capability, such as Open in Write, Add to Board, Open in Pictures, Create Stack from folder or other ecosystem actions. Context actions MUST be declared through Home’s registry and MUST NOT inject arbitrary untrusted shell code into Files.
Drag/drop and clipboard operations MUST preserve operation intent, source identity and provider capability. Cross-provider drag MUST make copy-vs-move semantics explicit. A cut/paste MUST NOT delete the source until destination commit succeeds.
AI bar and privacy
Files MUST host the global persistent contextual AI bar. The Files context snapshot includes current location/provider, selected FileIDs/FolderIDs, artifact types, sync state and permissions. AI requests use typed Files/owning-app/Stack actions for operations such as organise, rename, move, convert, summarise or create a Stack.
Selecting a private local file MUST NOT silently upload file content to a cloud model. Dulche’s local/cloud privacy and permission rules apply. Context handoff MUST identify the exact file/revision being provided and whether bytes/content leave the device.
Files MUST remain fully functional with AI disabled/unavailable. AI is additive and MUST NOT replace essential manual file-management UI.
Operation journal, undo and change feed
Consequential filesystem operations MUST be recorded in a durable operation journal with OperationID, actor/caller, target object IDs, source/destination where applicable, base/result revisions, state and structured error/result. The journal supports crash recovery, sync reconciliation and auditability.
Safely reversible operations such as rename, move and soft-delete SHOULD expose undo by performing a real inverse storage mutation against current revision checks. Undo MUST NOT be UI-only fiction and MUST fail explicitly if intervening changes make the inverse unsafe.
Files MUST expose a resumable typed change feed with stable event IDs/cursors for create/change/move/share/delete/restore/sync-state and other supported filesystem events. Automations/watchers can resume from a cursor without arbitrary full rescans.
Properties and sync diagnostics
A Properties/details surface MUST expose stable identity, path/location, provider, type, size, timestamps, owner/sharing, sync/offline state, current version/history access, app association and provider-specific metadata where available.
Files MUST provide clear sync diagnostics for 9to1 Drive, including current connectivity/server contact, pending uploads/downloads, pending structural operations, conflicts, paused/error state, offline-pinned usage and local cache usage. Item-level errors MUST expose local/base/cloud revision information where relevant and provide Resolve/Retry/View details actions.
Safety and filesystem edge cases
Provider adapters and local materialisation MUST define handling for illegal/reserved filenames, case sensitivity, path length, path traversal, symlinks/reparse points and unsupported metadata. Remote names MUST NOT escape the intended local sync root or overwrite unrelated local paths.
Filesystem shortcuts/symlinks MUST remain distinct from 9to1 artifact references/shortcuts. Copying a reference MUST NOT accidentally clone the referenced canonical artifact unless the user explicitly chooses duplication.
