Failure behaviour
Play MUST return structured failures including GameNotFound, GameRevisionUnavailable, InvalidGameDefinition, MatchNotFound, MatchAlreadyStarted, MatchNotJoinable, ContestantNotFound, ContestantNotEligible, ContestantViewDenied, NotContestantTurn, RoundNotActive, SubmissionAlreadyLocked, SubmissionDeadlinePassed, ActionUnavailable, IllegalAction, CapabilityDeniedByGame, JudgeUnavailable, ResolutionFailed, RecoveryUnavailable and RevisionConflict in addition to normal Dulche/Home/tool failures.
Acceptance requirements
Play is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:
A user can generate and start a maths quiz against ten AI Agent contestants from a natural-language request.
Persistent Dulche Agents can enter a Match without being cloned into a Play-private Agent registry.
Automatically filled SessionAgent opponents remain session-scoped unless explicitly saved.
Every contestant receives an isolated authorised view and cannot access sealed competitors' answers, hidden roles or judge/reference state.
A simultaneous quiz keeps submissions sealed until reveal/deadline and records authoritative timing when speed affects scoring.
Maths correctness/scoring uses deterministic validation where available rather than an unnecessary LLM judge.
Agent contestants act through typed game actions and illegal/unavailable actions fail without mutating MatchState.
Game-specific tool restrictions are enforced at runtime, including a no-web/no-code/no-calculator quiz profile.
Teams can mix humans and Agents while team-private state remains isolated from opponents.
An Agent-vs-Agent spectator Match can run without the user occupying a contestant slot.
Canonical MatchState remains authoritative over generated narrative/UI text.
Reconnect/recovery preserves locked submissions, scores and already-resolved state.
Play can hand off explicitly to an Experiences Space without merging MatchState and ExperienceState implicitly.
Core game creation, Match, contestant, action, scoring and replay operations have equivalent typed API coverage.
Productivity Apps
Write
Product role
9to1 Write is the production document/word-processing surface. It MUST behave like a mature word processor rather than a web editor, site builder, Markdown editor, collection of HTML blocks or browser contenteditable surface. LibreOffice Writer/LibreOfficeKit is the mature donor/layout/format engine for text-oriented documents; 9to1 owns the CUI shell, shared Productivity Engine integration, collaboration, AI, Sections model and native extensions.
The document surface MUST use an actual structured document model with paragraph/run/style/section/table/object/reference/review semantics and real layout/text measurement. Caret movement, selection, rich clipboard, IME input, undo/redo transactions, object anchoring, line wrapping, pagination, spelling/grammar ranges, accessibility semantics and large-document behaviour MUST be implemented as document-editor behaviour, not emulated with disconnected DOM widgets.
Continuous view is a presentation of the same structured word-processing document, not conversion into HTML. A document MUST switch between supported views without changing its canonical content or losing document semantics.
Donor parity and objective word-processor behaviour
All applicable LibreOffice Writer functionality, quality-of-life behaviour, keyboard interactions, menus/workflows and file-format depth MUST be preserved or appropriately adapted unless technically impossible and explicitly documented. The donor source is authoritative for inherited functionality; Write MUST NOT ship as a simplified rich-text clone simply because a smaller editor is easier to implement.
Inherited/core capability includes, where applicable, character and paragraph formatting; custom styles; page styles; headers/footers; sections; columns; page/section breaks; lists/outlines; tables; images/drawings/shapes; equations; fields; bookmarks; cross-references; captions; footnotes/endnotes; tables of contents; indexes; citations/bibliographies; comments; tracked changes; document comparison; spelling/grammar/language features; find/replace; hyphenation; print/page layout; mail merge; document properties; object anchoring/wrapping; export/print and other mature Writer functionality.
Launch and file entry
Write opens to the shared modern Launch Screen contract with Blank document, Templates, Recent, Favourites, Shared with me, search, Open and Import. Entries MUST be backed by real Files/Drive data rather than mock cards. Creating/opening/importing a document establishes the canonical Write artifact before entering the editor.
Editor shell
Write MUST NOT use a permanent Office-style ribbon. The editing shell consists of a document-title row, a floating contextual toolbar immediately below the title at the top of the document area, an optional collapsible Sections sidebar, the document canvas and the persistent shared AI bar at the bottom.
The Home button sits immediately to the left of the document title and opens an Office-style backstage/file menu for document-level operations such as Info, New, Open, Recent, Save/Save a copy, Share, Export, Print, Version history, Document properties and Settings. Closing the menu returns to the same document/selection position.
Floating contextual toolbar
The floating toolbar stays in a stable position immediately below the title while its contextual controls change according to the current semantic selection. Text, heading, image, table, reference/review and other contexts expose their own relevant operations. An operation that cannot apply to the current selection MUST NOT appear merely because it exists elsewhere in Write; for example Crop image cannot appear when no image is selected.
Three controls are persistent regardless of selection: +, Eye and overflow […]. They remain present even as all other controls change. When horizontal space is constrained, lower-priority contextual actions move into overflow before these persistent controls disappear.
The overflow […] menu contains additional actions relevant to the current context that did not fit or were deprioritised on the main bar. It is not a generic dump of all Write commands. The menu for a table selection differs from the menu for text or an image and MUST exclude inapplicable actions.
Right-click/context menus expose the same semantic action model in menu form. Context menus and the floating bar call the same typed Write/Productivity APIs rather than maintaining parallel behaviour.
Pinned toolbar actions
Users MUST be able to pin supported contextual actions to the top bar and reorder/reset their pinned preferences. Pinning means prioritise this action whenever it is applicable; it MUST NOT force an irrelevant disabled action to occupy the toolbar in unrelated contexts. Pinning is per-user UI preference rather than collaborative document state.
Toolbar priority SHOULD resolve from the most important current-context control, then applicable user-pinned controls, then common contextual actions, followed by the persistent +, Eye and […] controls.
Universal Insert (+)
The persistent + control is the universal Insert entry point. It opens a searchable, context-aware insertion palette rather than requiring an Insert ribbon. The complete palette MUST expose applicable content/structure/reference/9to1 artifact options while prioritising items relevant to the current caret/object context.
Insertion types SHOULD include tables, images, drawings, equations, code blocks, text boxes, shapes/callouts, horizontal lines, page/section breaks, columns, headers/footers, footnotes, citations, cross-references, bookmarks, captions, table of contents, special characters, fields, links/files and supported embedded 9to1 artifacts such as Canvas, Board, Data ranges/charts, Picture, Planner items, Maps and Graphs.
Eye / visibility controls
The persistent Eye control owns view/visibility options rather than document-format mutations. Its menu MUST include the current Write View mode and may include Sections visibility, Comments, spelling/grammar marks, formatting marks, ruler, page boundaries, object anchors, alignment/snap guides and the floating word/character count where applicable.
Most Eye settings are per-user view preferences and MUST NOT change what collaborators see. Contextually useful visibility aids MAY appear only when relevant, for example object bounds/anchors/guides when an object is selected.
Floating document statistics
When enabled from Eye, an unobtrusive document-statistics indicator floats in the bottom-right of the document area without becoming document content or consuming page layout. It SHOULD show document word and character counts, and when text is selected it SHOULD prioritise selection word/character counts. Clicking it MAY reveal expanded statistics such as characters without spaces and page count where meaningful.
The statistics indicator and bottom AI bar MUST coexist without overlap at supported sizes.
Sections sidebar
Write has a Google-Docs-inspired collapsible Sections sidebar on the left. The product terminology is Sections, not Tabs. A Section is a stable user-created structural division of the same Write document and MAY contain nested Sections. Headings inside each Section are derived automatically from document heading/outline styles.
Every Section MUST have stable SectionID, DocumentID, optional ParentSectionID, Name, optional icon/metadata, ordering and revision/state information. Renaming/reordering/nesting MUST preserve SectionID so links, AI context and cross-references are not tied to visible names.
The expanded sidebar presents Sections as stronger/root nodes with the heading hierarchy beneath each Section. Clicking a heading navigates to it; changing heading style updates the outline live. Moving a heading moves its heading plus subordinate content using structured document operations. Moving a Section moves the Section's canonical content safely.
The sidebar has a + control for New section, New subsection, From selection and supported Import-as-section workflows. Section/headings support context actions such as rename, duplicate, move before/after/into, copy link, export section, delete and relevant AI/translation operations.
The Sections sidebar MUST be collapsible to a narrow edge/rail and resizable when expanded. Collapsed/expanded state and width are per-user/device preferences. Collapsing immediately returns horizontal space to the document canvas; navigation/AI actions MUST NOT forcibly reopen it. On narrow layouts the sidebar becomes a temporary drawer. Keyboard and non-drag movement/navigation alternatives are mandatory.
The Sections sidebar and an inserted Table of Contents are distinct. The sidebar is editing/navigation structure; + → Table of contents inserts a real document object generated from configured heading levels/styles.
View modes
Eye exposes three first-class Write View modes: Continuous, Pages and Book. Switching view is immediate presentation state over the same DocumentID, SectionIDs, ObjectIDs, selection, comments and revision. The user's view mode does not force collaborators into the same view.
Continuous is the default for new .9to1w documents unless the chosen template requires another view. It presents one seamless pageless writing surface with a sensible readable content width and no artificial sheet gaps. Real page breaks remain canonical and are shown as unobtrusive markers rather than forcing paper sheets.
Continuous view MUST retain page-aware document features such as headers/footers, footnotes, page numbers, margins, section/page breaks and columns in the underlying document model. The view may present them contextually rather than permanently rendering every page boundary.
Pages renders exact page layout using modern rounded pages, restrained elevation, clean spacing and a neutral workspace while preserving true margins, headers/footers, footnotes, page numbers and print pagination. It MUST not use dated harsh page chrome merely because the donor does.
Book renders publication-aware facing-page spreads and supports odd/even pages, right/left page semantics, mirrored inside/outside margins, binding gutter, different left/right headers/footers, section starts/front matter and deliberate blank-page behaviour. Narrow displays MAY show one page at a time while preserving spread semantics.
View mode is independent from Locked/Unlocked layout mode. Supported combinations include Continuous + Locked, Continuous + Unlocked, Pages + Locked, Pages + Unlocked, Book + Locked and Book + Unlocked.
Locked and Unlocked layout
Write MUST implement the same first-class Locked/Unlocked layout concept as Boards. LayoutMode is independent from the user's current View mode and from AI Read/Write mode.
Locked is the conventional word-processing flow and the default for ordinary documents. Paragraphs/inline content follow document structure and supported objects use anchors/wrapping rules so accidental free positioning is constrained.
Unlocked adds a professional free-positioned visual object layer for supported images, text boxes, shapes, drawings, charts, embedded artifacts, callouts, equations and tables where applicable. Users may drag, resize, rotate, overlap, layer, align, distribute and snap these objects without converting the whole document into arbitrary floating text boxes.
Unlocked object controls MUST support position/size/rotation; page/Section/paragraph/character anchoring where meaningful; inline/square/tight/behind/in-front/custom wrapping; aspect and position locks; z-order; align/distribute; grouping; snapping to margins, columns, guides, text bounds and other objects; and accessible non-drag alternatives.
Switching layout modes MUST preserve data and positions as far as the target representation supports. If an object cannot be represented safely under the requested mode/foreign format, Write MUST warn rather than silently discard/flatten it.
Styles and custom styles
Custom styles MUST be first-class and front-and-centre whenever the selected content supports styles. For text, the active semantic style control SHOULD normally be the first contextual toolbar control rather than leading with raw font/size controls.
Write MUST support built-in and arbitrary custom character/paragraph/document styles with stable StyleID, inheritance/overrides where supported, modify/create/update-from-selection, usage inspection and import/copy of style sets. Styles MAY control typography, paragraph/line spacing, indentation, alignment, borders/background, list behaviour, pagination/keep-with-next, language, outline level and semantic/accessibility role.
Changing a shared/custom style MUST update linked uses while preserving explicit local overrides according to the style model. Write SHOULD preview the scope/impact of broad style changes where useful.
Equivalent reusable style concepts SHOULD exist for tables and other supported object classes where they provide real value; these remain canonical style definitions rather than visual presets copied independently into each object.
Tables
Tables MUST support mature Writer/Office-level editing plus a stronger native .9to1w styling model. The contextual toolbar for a table SHOULD prioritise active Table Style plus common Borders, Fill, Padding, Alignment and structural actions, with less-common relevant actions in […].
Whole-table controls MUST include width/height and fixed/content/flexible sizing as supported; alignment; wrapping; position/anchor; table padding/margins; background/opacity; border; shadow; caption; repeating header rows; pagination/split behaviour; and native rounded-corner support.
Native .9to1w tables MUST support table corner radius, including linked or independent top-left/top-right/bottom-right/bottom-left radii. Foreign export MUST preserve this where the target format can represent it or explicitly warn/use a documented compatibility representation when it cannot.
Row/column controls SHOULD include explicit/flexible/min/max sizing, equal distribution, visibility/header designation, keep-together and appropriate responsive/fixed behaviour. Cell controls MUST include independent top/right/bottom/left padding, horizontal/vertical alignment, text direction, background/fill, border per side, border width/style/colour/opacity, merge/split, minimum dimensions and defined overflow behaviour.
Border editing MUST distinguish outer border, inner horizontal, inner vertical and individual cell edges. Cell padding MUST be directly discoverable and support linked/unlinked values rather than being buried in an obscure properties dialog.
Custom Table Styles MUST be reusable first-class definitions capable of controlling whole-table appearance, header rows, first/last columns, odd/even rows, typography, borders, corner radius, cell padding, alignment and backgrounds. Linked tables update when the style changes except for explicit local overrides.
Images, drawings and positioned objects
Images and visual objects MUST support professional crop, resize, aspect ratio, wrap, anchor, positioning, z-order, caption, alt text, replacement and supported compression/export controls. The shared Rnote-derived drawing object is used for handwriting/sketch/annotation/diagram content so supported drawings remain editable across Write, Boards and Canvas.
Multiple selected free objects expose align/distribute/group operations. Object controls and […] overflow remain contextual; irrelevant image controls MUST not appear for text/table selections.
References and document structure
References is a first-class semantic capability even though Write does not expose a permanent References ribbon. +, contextual controls, right-click and […] provide footnotes/endnotes, citations/bibliography, table of contents, captions, cross-references, bookmarks, indexes and fields where supported.
Citation/reference data MUST be structured rather than only formatted prose so Agents and APIs can insert, validate, update and export references safely. Section/heading links and cross-references SHOULD use stable IDs rather than visible text/page numbers as identity.
Review, comments and collaboration
Write MUST support comments, tracked/suggested changes, accept/reject, previous/next change, document comparison and version history using real document/review semantics. AI edits in Suggest mode create suggestions rather than silently accepted direct changes.
Realtime collaboration MUST use the normal 9to1 shared-artifact model for presence, cursors/selections, concurrent editing, comments, permissions/sharing and revision/conflict semantics. Naive timestamp last-writer-wins overwrite is non-conformant.
Native format and foreign document formats
.9to1w is the versioned native Write format and MUST preserve the full native document model, stable Productivity object identity, Sections, custom styles/table styles, embedded 9to1 artifact references, review/collaboration metadata, drawings/graphs, supported AI provenance and native features that foreign formats cannot represent. Migrations MUST be deterministic and preserve compatible unknown optional data.
Write MUST support reliable DOCX and ODT import/export plus supported Markdown/TXT interchange and PDF export. Import/export fidelity is a release criterion, not a demo feature. Unsupported or lossy foreign-format behaviour MUST be surfaced rather than silently deleting content to force compatibility.
PDF opening and editing
Write MUST open and edit PDFs as first-class fixed-layout documents; PDF support is not export-only and MUST NOT simply convert every PDF into HTML or an approximate web editor. The Write shell remains consistent while an appropriate PDF/page-object engine (including applicable LibreOffice Draw/PDF capabilities or equivalent mature implementation) owns fixed-layout PDF object semantics.
A digitally structured PDF SHOULD preserve selectable/editable native text, fonts, images, vector/page objects, links, annotations, forms/layers where supported and page geometry. Such PDFs default to Pages view and Unlocked layout because fixed page geometry is intrinsic.
Scanned PDFs MUST be recognised as image/scanned content rather than falsely presented as native text. Write SHOULD offer explicit Recognise text/OCR-style transformation, preserve correspondence to the original page image and expose uncertain/low-confidence recognition rather than claiming perfect extraction. Mixed PDFs are handled page/object-by-page/object rather than forcing one simplistic document-wide mode.
PDF editing MUST support useful fixed-layout workflows where technically supported: editing/moving existing text blocks, inserting/deleting text, images and objects, resize/crop, drawings/shapes, page rearrange/insert/delete/rotate, combine/extract pages, links, annotations/comments/highlights, proper redaction, supported form fields/signatures and headers/footers/page numbers.
Before the first destructive PDF save, Write MUST preserve an original recoverable revision/backup and maintain normal version history. PDF AI operations use semantic PDF text/object structure when available and MUST NOT OCR screenshots of text that the PDF already exposes semantically.
Continuous MUST NOT be forced onto a fixed-layout PDF. PDF defaults to Pages; only views/reflow operations that are meaningful for the active PDF are exposed, with fidelity implications made explicit.
Persistent AI bar in Write
Write implements the platform-wide shared AI-bar Read-only / Write-mode contract. In Read-only, Dulche can semantically inspect/search/compare the full authorised document, including off-screen Sections, headings, objects, styles, comments, references, tables and embedded artifact metadata, but cannot mutate the document. In Write mode it can use typed Write/Productivity actions subject to host editing/review/permission state.
The AI context MUST expose stable DocumentID, document revision, current SectionID/heading/object, selection ranges/ObjectIDs, document structure, styles, comments, references, tables/images/embedded artifacts and available typed actions as authorised. Viewport visibility is not the AI's document boundary. Visual rendering may supplement this when layout must be inspected, but semantic access is primary.
AI Read/Write mode is separate from document Edit/Suggest/View and Locked/Unlocked. For example AI Write mode + Suggest creates tracked suggestions; AI Write mode + Edit may perform direct typed edits; AI Read-only always prohibits mutations. The bar MUST NOT use mouse/keyboard simulation instead of Write APIs.
The AI bar supports actions such as rewrite/shorten/expand, restructure, create/move Sections, apply/change styles, manipulate tables, insert objects/references, inspect missing citations, translate, compare Sections and perform other authorised semantic edits. Broad edits remain revision-safe, undoable/versioned and subject to normal conflict handling.
Agents, sources and Translate integration
Write MAY expose applicable Global, Write-scoped, Space and contextual Dulche Agents through the shared Agent picker. Specialist writing Agents such as Editor, Proofreader, Citation Assistant or Long-form Writer are canonical Dulche Agents, not private hard-coded AI runtimes.
Documents MAY reference authorised source sets/files without unnecessarily duplicating them into the document. Source-backed AI work SHOULD preserve provenance where appropriate.
Selection-level Translate invokes Dulche Translate directly for simple translation. Continue in Translate opens/preserves context in the built-in Translate Space for larger localisation workflows. Whole-document translation can produce separate Write derivatives/locale variants while preserving structure and source provenance.
Embedded 9to1 artifacts and interoperability
Write MAY embed/reference supported Boards, Canvas, Data ranges/charts, Picture assets, Planner items, Maps, Graphs and other canonical 9to1 artifacts as live embeds, linked previews or explicit snapshots according to the target type and permissions. Embedding MUST reference canonical entities rather than creating unmanaged duplicate state.
Shared Productivity Engine bundles and object identities MUST support rich cross-app copy/paste/conversion where semantics are compatible; unsupported conversion MUST fail explicitly rather than silently flattening required behaviour.
Navigation, search and long-document performance
Write MUST provide document search/find-replace and efficient navigation for large documents. Sections/headings are semantic navigation, not a DOM outline derived from whatever is currently rendered. Long documents MUST not require eagerly rendering every page/object to remain editable.
Switching Continuous/Pages/Book, opening/collapsing Sections, enabling counts/marks and changing selections MUST avoid unnecessary full-document re-rendering where the document engine can update incrementally.
Recovery, persistence and accessibility
Write MUST support autosave, unsaved-draft protection, crash recovery, revision/version history, conflict recovery and safe interrupted-save behaviour. A crash or partial write MUST not casually lose a user's document. Save/reopen workflows are part of acceptance testing.
Keyboard-only operation, screen-reader semantics, focus indicators, scalable typography/zoom, accessible toolbar/context menus, non-drag alternatives for movement/layout, readable selection/review state and narrow-screen adaptation are mandatory. The Sections drawer, toolbar, floating statistics and AI bar must remain usable without overlap at supported scale factors.

Failure behaviour
Write MUST return structured failures including DocumentNotFound, UnsupportedDocumentVersion, ImportUnsupported, ImportLossy, ExportUnsupported, ExportLossy, SectionNotFound, StyleNotFound, TableNotFound, ObjectNotFound, InvalidRange, RevisionConflict, PermissionDenied, ReadOnlyDocument, LayoutConversionLoss, PDFUnsupported, PDFObjectNotEditable, OCRUnavailable, OCRUncertain, PDFBackupFailed, RecoveryUnavailable and ProviderUnavailable in addition to shared Home/Dulche/Files failures.
Acceptance requirements
Write is implementation-complete only when acceptance coverage verifies at least:
Write uses a real structured word-processing/document engine and is not implemented as a generic HTML/contenteditable/web editor.
A new .9to1w opens in Continuous view by default and can switch to Pages and Book without changing canonical content or losing selection/state.
Pages renders modern rounded pages with exact pagination; Book renders correct facing-page/book layout semantics.
The floating contextual toolbar sits directly beneath the title, stays positionally stable and changes only to relevant controls.
+, Eye and […] remain persistent across text, image, table and other selection contexts.
[…] contains only additional actions relevant to the current context; inapplicable actions such as Crop with no image are absent.
Users can pin/reorder contextual actions and pinned actions appear only when applicable.
+ opens a real searchable insertion palette that inserts supported document/reference/9to1 objects.
Eye toggles view/visibility features including Continuous/Pages/Book, Sections and word/character count where applicable.
Floating word/character count appears at bottom-right without becoming document content or overlapping the AI bar.
The Sections sidebar is collapsible/resizable, uses stable SectionIDs, includes live heading outline and supports nested Sections and accessible movement.
Locked mode preserves conventional document flow; Unlocked mode provides real free placement, z-order, snapping, alignment/distribution and wrapping without converting normal body text into arbitrary boxes.
Custom text styles are front-and-centre in applicable contexts and create/update/apply through stable StyleIDs.
Native tables support reusable custom Table Styles, independent cell padding, advanced borders and rounded corners including independent corner radii.
Write preserves applicable LibreOffice Writer donor functionality/QoL rather than shipping a simplified editor.
DOCX and ODT import/export plus native .9to1w and supported Markdown/TXT/PDF export complete real save-close-reopen workflows with fidelity checks.
Write opens digital, scanned and mixed PDFs through an appropriate fixed-layout editor, defaults PDFs to Pages/Unlocked and never pretends scanned text is native.
PDF text/object/page editing and destructive-save backup/version recovery work for supported PDF cases; backup failure is surfaced rather than ignored.
The shared AI bar can semantically read the entire authorised document in Read-only mode and cannot mutate it.
AI Write mode edits through typed APIs and obeys Edit/Suggest/View, permission, undo/version and conflict semantics.
AI context is not limited to the viewport and does not substitute screenshot/OCR for available semantic document/PDF text.
Realtime collaboration preserves concurrent edits/comments/review without naive timestamp last-writer-wins data loss.
Crash/interrupted-save recovery and realistic create/open-edit-save-close-reopen validation preserve document content.
Toolbar, Sections, page/book views, review state, free-layout controls and AI bar remain keyboard/screen-reader/zoom accessible.
Core Write operations have equivalent typed API coverage and no visible toolbar/menu action is a placeholder or disconnected fake.
Write MUST use Home’s Shared Productivity Engine for every shared object type it supports. Shared objects copied between Write, Present, Canvas, Boards and Spaces MUST preserve the common object schema, formatting and behaviour rather than being converted into Write-only representations.
Present
Purpose, ownership and conformance
9-1 Present is the CUI presentation authoring, presenting and interactive-runtime application. LibreOffice Impress/Draw is the donor foundation for applicable mature presentation editing, interoperability and quality-of-life behaviour. 9-1 owns the CUI shell, the native .9to1p model, the Actions runtime, typed APIs, AI integration, component model and cross-app semantics.
Applicable donor functionality MUST be preserved unless a scoped donor-parity exception is recorded in the canonical donor-parity manifest. Present MUST NOT ship as a reduced slide editor whose only conformance evidence is file opening or basic text/shape editing.
Present MUST use Home's Shared Productivity Engine for every registered shared object type that it supports. Shared text, tables, charts/graphs, images/media, drawings/ink and other shared objects copied between Present, Write, Canvas, Boards and Spaces MUST preserve the shared object schema, semantic identifiers, formatting, accessibility metadata and clipboard representation.
Release boundary:
Present owns PresentationID, SlideID, slide order, slide composition, presentation-level state, slide-local state, speaker notes references, presentation sessions and the Actions graph.
Home owns shared productivity object schemas, permission brokerage, shared AI/runtime services, common clipboard bundles and other platform services defined in Home.
Present MUST NOT introduce a second private implementation of a Home-owned shared object or platform service.
The native .9to1p representation is authoritative for full-fidelity 9-1 behaviour.
Normative applicability and capability negotiation
Terms such as applicable, supported and available are not discretionary escape hatches in this section. They are resolved from explicit manifests or runtime capability declarations.
A donor feature is applicable unless it is classified in the Present donor-parity manifest as Replace with 9-1-native equivalent or Not applicable with a recorded technical/legal reason.
A platform capability is supported only when the platform capability registry declares the required capability and version for the active device/runtime.
A file-format construct is representable only when the import/export capability matrix declares a mapping for the source construct and target format/version.
Failure of a required capability check MUST produce a typed unavailable/unsupported result and the specified fallback or CompatibilityIssue; silent omission is prohibited.
An implementation MUST NOT reinterpret a MUST requirement as optional merely because its current code path does not implement the required capability.
Landing page, file lifecycle and persistence
Present MUST implement the global launch-screen contract. The launch surface MUST expose Create New, Open/Import, recent presentations and real template/theme discovery. Recent items MUST be derived from persisted history; fabricated recent files are prohibited except for explicitly labelled onboarding or template content.
The release file contract MUST support native .9to1p plus PPTX and ODP import/export. Static output MUST support PDF and image export. Present MUST provide complete create -> edit -> save -> close -> reopen workflows with autosave, crash/interrupted-save recovery, revision tracking and conflict-safe persistence.
A failed save, partial media write, unresolved revision conflict or recovery failure MUST be surfaced as an explicit error state.
Present MUST NOT report success until the target revision and all referenced persisted objects required for the save have been committed.
Recovery MUST preserve the last known-good durable revision and MUST NOT overwrite it with a partially reconstructed presentation.
Canonical data model and identity
All persistent entities MUST use stable opaque IDs. Slide number, slide title, list position, object name and file path are mutable presentation attributes and MUST NOT be used as persistent identity.
Presentation {
  PresentationID: StableID
  SchemaVersion: Version
  RevisionID: RevisionID
  SlideOrder: SlideID[]
  ThemeRef: ThemeID + ThemeRevision
  MasterRefs: MasterID[]
  PresentationVariables: VariableMap
  ComponentTypes: ComponentTypeID[]
  ActionsGraphRef: GraphID + GraphRevision
  Settings: PresentationSettings
  Permissions: PermissionDescriptor
}
Slide {
  SlideID: StableID
  MasterID?: StableID
  LayoutID?: StableID
  ObjectOrder: ObjectID[]
  SlideVariables: VariableMap
  NotesID: StableID
  Hidden: boolean
  ActionsBindings: ActionBinding[]
  RevisionID: RevisionID
}
Reordering, renaming, hiding, duplicating or moving a slide MUST NOT mutate the identity of an existing SlideID. Duplicating a slide MUST allocate a new SlideID and new IDs for duplicated slide-owned objects while preserving references that are explicitly shared by definition.
A reference to a slide or object MUST resolve by stable ID. Position-based references such as 'slide 4' MAY be accepted as user input, but MUST be resolved to a stable ID before persistence or execution.
Required release defaults:
SpeakerWordsPerMinute = 130
IncludeHiddenSlidesInStatistics = true
LiveDrawingMode = OFF
LiveInkPersistence = SESSION_ONLY
IncludeSpeakerNotesInAudienceOutput = false
PersistSessionState = false
Changing a release default MUST create an explicit persisted setting override. Absence of an override means the release default above; implementations MUST NOT infer a different default from platform, file origin or prior session state.
Authoring shell and slide navigation
The editing shell MUST expose a persistent slide navigator, thumbnail view, slide sorter/grid view and searchable presentation outline. The same SlideID MUST back every representation of a slide.
Required slide operations:
Create, duplicate, delete/recover, reorder, hide/unhide and move slides between presentation sections.
Jump to slide by outline/search result, stable reference or user-visible position.
Multi-select slides for reorder, duplicate, delete, export and section assignment where the operation is semantically valid.
Preserve selection and focus predictably after slide mutations; deleting the active slide MUST move focus to a deterministic adjacent surviving slide.
The authoring shell MUST provide undo/redo, zoom, fit slide, fit selection, rulers, guides, grid, snapping controls and a status surface showing at least current slide/total slide count, zoom and relevant selection/document state. Keyboard-only navigation MUST cover the navigator, canvas, notes pane and inspectors.
Conventional object editing and layout
Present MUST provide mature slide-object editing for text, shapes, lines/connectors, images, shared tables/charts/graphs, drawings, media, code objects, 3D objects, Generative UI objects and supported embedded/shared objects.
Every spatial object type that declares geometric editing MUST support the applicable subset of:
Create, duplicate, delete, multi-select, group/ungroup and lock/unlock.
Move, resize, rotate, flip, z-order change, align and distribute.
Snap to grid/guides/objects and enter exact position, size and rotation values.
Crop or mask only for object types whose renderer declares crop/mask support.
Style copy/paste without silently copying object identity, runtime state or permissions.
Shape and text styling MUST persist actual stored values. Inspectors, toolbars and keyboard commands MUST read from and write to the same canonical object properties; a visible control that does not mutate the corresponding stored property is non-conformant.
Present MUST support object naming and a selection/object tree. The tree MUST expose stacking order, locked/hidden state and semantic object identity. Reordering the tree MUST change z-order only when the selected object type participates in z-order.
Themes, masters, layouts and templates
Present MUST support theme colours, theme fonts, backgrounds, reusable style tokens, slide masters, slide layouts, placeholders and reusable templates.
A slide linked to a layout MUST inherit layout/master properties unless that property has an explicit slide-level override.
Changing a master or layout MUST update linked slides without deleting valid slide-level overrides.
Reset Layout MUST remove only slide-level overrides governed by the selected layout; it MUST NOT delete unrelated slide-owned objects.
PPTX/ODP import MUST preserve representable master/layout relationships instead of flattening every slide to unrelated absolute objects.
Notes-page and handout layout data present in an imported format MUST be retained when the source construct maps to a declared Present capability. If no declared mapping exists, import MUST emit a CompatibilityIssue rather than silently dropping the construct.
Speaker notes and notes workflow
Every slide MUST have first-class speaker notes identified by a stable NotesID. Notes are authoring content associated with a SlideID and are not audience-slide content.
SpeakerNotes {
  NotesID: StableID
  SlideID: StableID
  Content: SharedRichTextDocument
  Locale?: LocaleID
  RevisionID: RevisionID
}
Notes MUST be editable in a dedicated notes pane and a full Notes view.
Notes MUST support shared rich-text editing, lists, links, proofing and supported shared embedded objects.
Notes MUST be searchable and addressable by typed APIs.
The shared Dictation capability MUST operate in speaker notes.
Notes MUST appear in Presenter View and notes-page print/export when explicitly selected.
Normal slideshow output, ordinary audience capture, PDF/image export and generated video MUST exclude speaker notes by default.
A notes-inclusive export MUST require an explicit notes output mode; it MUST NOT be inferred from the presence of notes.
PPTX/ODP import/export MUST preserve speaker notes when the destination format supports them. Loss or degradation MUST be listed in the compatibility report.
Word, character and speaking statistics
Present MUST provide live text statistics for presentation content. The statistics engine MUST expose the following explicit scopes: SELECTION, CURRENT_SLIDE, CURRENT_NOTES, ALL_SLIDES, ALL_NOTES and PRESENTATION_COMBINED.
PresentationTextStatistics {
  Scope: StatisticsScope
  WordCount: integer >= 0
  CharacterCountWithSpaces: integer >= 0
  CharacterCountWithoutSpaces: integer >= 0
  SlideTextWordCount?: integer >= 0
  NotesWordCount?: integer >= 0
  EstimatedSpeakingSeconds?: integer >= 0
}
Word boundaries MUST follow the platform Unicode word-segmentation implementation based on Unicode word-boundary rules. Character counts MUST count user-perceived Unicode grapheme clusters rather than UTF-16 code units. CharacterCountWithoutSpaces MUST exclude grapheme clusters classified by the platform Unicode implementation as whitespace.
Slide-text statistics include authored text visible in text-bearing slide objects and component labels in the selected scope.
Speaker-note statistics include only speaker-note rich-text content.
Comments, alt text, object names, Actions node labels, code source, hidden implementation metadata and compatibility metadata MUST NOT be included in ordinary word/character counts.
ALL_SLIDES MUST include hidden slides by default because they are part of the authored document; the statistics UI MUST provide an explicit Exclude hidden slides filter.
PRESENTATION_COMBINED MUST expose slide-text and notes counts separately in addition to the combined totals.
Estimated speaking time MUST be calculated from notes WordCount using SpeakerWordsPerMinute. The release default is 130 words/minute. The user MUST be able to change this value without altering the note text. EstimatedSpeakingSeconds = round(WordCount / SpeakerWordsPerMinute * 60).
Counts MUST update after a committed text edit without requiring a save/reopen cycle and MUST be accessible from normal authoring UI without inserting count text into the presentation.
Search, proofing, comments and collaboration
Present MUST provide presentation-wide search and replace across slide text and speaker notes. Every result MUST identify the SlideID, object/notes target and exact text range required to navigate to the match semantically.
Spell-check/proofing MUST operate on slide text and speaker notes and MUST preserve per-range language metadata.
Comments and replies MUST be anchorable to a SlideID, ObjectID and, where supported, a text range.
Realtime collaboration MUST preserve concurrent object, text, notes and comment edits using revision/conflict semantics; naive timestamp last-writer-wins data loss is prohibited.
Presence indicators and remote selections are session UI state and MUST NOT mutate presentation content.
Actions runtime and state model
Present MUST NOT implement an independent legacy animation engine or an independent transition runtime. All dynamic, timed, interactive and transition behaviour MUST be represented by a canonical typed Actions graph executed by the shared graph runtime.
ActionGraph {
  GraphID: StableID
  GraphRevision: RevisionID
  Nodes: ActionNode[]
  Edges: ActionEdge[]
  Entrypoints: ActionBinding[]
}
PresentationRuntimeState {
  GlobalVariables: VariableMap
  SlideVariables: Map<SlideID, VariableMap>
  ComponentState: Map<ComponentInstanceID, VariableMap>
  SessionState: VariableMap
}
Slides, objects, interactive components, media, code objects, 3D objects and live-drawing surfaces MUST expose versioned typed events. Event payloads MUST be schema-validated before graph execution.
The release event vocabulary MUST include at least:
PresentationStarted, PresentationEnded, SlideEntered, SlideLeft, NextSlideRequested and PreviousSlideRequested.
Clicked, DoubleClicked, PointerEntered, PointerLeft, Focused, Blurred and supported key/gesture events.
TimerElapsed and VariableChanged.
MediaStarted, MediaPaused, MediaPositionChanged, MediaEnded and MediaError.
ComponentValueChanged and ComponentSubmitted.
DrawingChanged and code-result/code-event output.
Actions MUST support conditions, branching, sequencing, parallel branches, delays/timers, reusable subgraphs and typed error paths. Actions MUST address targets by stable semantic IDs and MUST NOT simulate mouse/keyboard input when a typed capability exists.
Graph execution MUST be deterministic for the same graph revision, initial local state and deterministic inputs. When multiple nodes become runnable simultaneously, ordering MUST be defined by explicit dependencies/priority and a stable NodeID tie-breaker. External service results are recorded inputs and do not make the local scheduling order unspecified.
Cycles are permitted only when the runtime execution guard can bound them. Every event cascade MUST have a finite execution budget and loop detection. Exceeding the budget MUST terminate the affected cascade with a typed runtime error rather than freezing the presentation.
Starting a presentation creates a new PresentationSession with a defined initial state. SessionState and component runtime state reset on restart by default. Persistence requires an explicit author-configured persistence binding and the normal permission/write rules.
Transitions builder
The Transitions sidebar MUST remain available as a simple authoring surface, but it is a specialised Actions-graph editor. It MUST NOT invoke a second transition engine.
Choosing or editing a transition MUST create/update a marked Actions subgraph owned by that transition definition.
The sidebar MUST expose Open in Actions to reveal the exact generated subgraph.
Simple-editor changes MUST modify only nodes owned by the transition definition and MUST preserve user-authored extension nodes connected outside that owned region.
If an advanced graph edit makes the transition no longer representable by the simple sidebar, the sidebar MUST show a Custom/Advanced state rather than deleting or approximating the graph.
A transition completes only when its graph reaches the transition completion node. Slide navigation MUST commit exactly once per NavigationRequestID.
Interactive and reusable components
Present MUST ship first-class accessible Button, Switch, Text Input, Dropdown, Slider and Flashcard component types.
Components MUST expose typed properties, state, focus/keyboard semantics, accessibility role/name/value and versioned events.
Built-in hover, focus, pressed and value behaviour MUST work without requiring an author to construct a graph.
The same primitives MUST be exposed to authors through Actions; built-in components MUST NOT depend on a hidden private animation system.
ComponentType {
  ComponentTypeID: StableID
  DefinitionRevision: RevisionID
  VisualTree: ComponentNode[]
  PropertySchema: Schema
  StateSchema: Schema
  EventSchema: Schema
  ActionSchema: Schema
  DefaultValues: ValueMap
  Variants: Variant[]
  AccessibilitySemantics: AccessibilityDescriptor
  InternalActionsGraph: GraphID
  ExposedProperties: PropertyID[]
  ExposedEvents: EventTypeID[]
}
Users MUST be able to convert selected objects/components into a reusable Component Type. An instance MUST retain ComponentInstanceID, ComponentTypeID, ComponentDefinitionRevision, property overrides and instance state.
Linked instances MAY receive compatible definition updates only through an explicit update policy.
Detached/local copies MUST NOT receive future definition updates.
An incompatible component-definition update MUST NOT silently rewrite or invalidate an existing instance; it MUST require migration or retain the older definition revision.
Reusable component types MUST be storable in the user's/workspace component library.
Generative UI
Present's Insert surface MUST include Generative UI. The user may insert an existing generated UI artifact or request a new generated interactive surface through Dulche.
GenerativeUIObject {
  GenerativeUIObjectID: StableID
  SchemaRevision: RevisionID
  StateSchema: Schema
  EventSchema: Schema
  ActionsBindings: ActionBinding[]
  Permissions: PermissionDescriptor
}
Generated UI MUST execute in the approved shared CUI/Generative UI runtime.
Arbitrary raw HTML/JavaScript embedded directly into the presentation is prohibited.
Generated UI events MUST be connectable to the presentation Actions graph.
A generated UI object MAY be saved as a reusable Component Type only when its visual, state, event and action schemas use ComponentType-supported constructs and pass component validation.
Write, Present, Boards and Canvas MUST use the same canonical Generative UI representation rather than app-specific incompatible formats.
Runnable code, media, 3D and live ink
Runnable code:
A runnable-code object MUST store source, registered language/runtime ID, declared inputs, typed outputs, permissions and execution limits.
Execution MUST occur in a sandbox. Filesystem, network, account and device access are denied by default and may be granted only through declared platform capabilities.
CPU/time, memory and output limits MUST be enforced by the selected runtime provider. Limit violations MUST return typed errors.
Code results/events MUST be consumable by Actions and MAY update authorised presentation objects through typed APIs.
Audio and video:
Media objects MUST expose Play, Pause, Stop, Seek, SetVolume and SetPlaybackRate.
Media events MUST include Started, Paused, PositionChanged, Ended and Error.
Missing, offline or unsupported media MUST produce an explicit media error state; silent broken placeholders are prohibited.
Native 3D:
The initial supported interchange formats MUST include glTF and GLB.
3D objects MUST support transform, camera/orbit controls, camera presets, lighting/environment, material rendering, hotspots and Actions integration.
Model-intrinsic animation/timeline playback MUST be controlled through typed 3D Actions; it MUST NOT create a legacy presentation-animation subsystem.
Drawing/live ink:
Present MUST use the shared Rnote-derived structured drawing/ink model.
Live drawing modes are OFF, PRESENTER_ONLY and PARTICIPANTS where the collaboration surface supports participant input.
Live ink persistence modes are SESSION_ONLY, AUTO_SAVE and EXPLICIT_COMMIT.
DrawingChanged MUST be available to Actions and, when authorised, Dulche.
Slideshow runtime and Presenter View
PresentationSession {
  SessionID: StableID
  PresentationID: StableID
  SourceRevisionID: RevisionID
  ActiveSlideID: SlideID
  RuntimeState: PresentationRuntimeState
  RouteHistory: NavigationRecord[]
  StartedAt: Timestamp
  Status: RUNNING | PAUSED | ENDED | FAILED
}
Present MUST support full-screen and windowed slideshow playback and presenter/audience display selection when multiple display targets are available.
Presenter View MUST display current slide, next slide, speaker notes, slide navigator, elapsed timer, clock and presentation controls.
AudienceOutput and PresenterUI are separate render targets. Speaker notes, timers, controls, diagnostics and presenter-only overlays MUST NOT enter AudienceOutput unless the user explicitly selects a presenter-view recording/export mode.
The runtime MUST support keyboard navigation, slide jumping, hidden-slide rules, black/white blank screen, presenter pointer/laser, permitted live ink, live captions/subtitles where configured and interactive components/Actions.
Reduced-motion preference MUST be exposed to the Actions runtime. Motion-heavy Actions MUST provide a defined reduced-motion result rather than ignoring the preference.
Presenter notes MUST support presenter-side text sizing and auto-scroll/teleprompter behaviour without mutating stored note content.
A presentation session MUST execute against a defined SourceRevisionID. If the document changes during a live session, the runtime MUST either remain pinned to SourceRevisionID or apply an explicit safe live-update policy; it MUST NOT mix arbitrary object revisions silently.
Rehearsal, timings and recording
Present MUST support rehearsal of timings and structured session recording.
Rehearsal MUST record navigation and Action-path timing without converting the authored presentation into a fixed linear deck.
Recording MAY capture narration, camera, pointer/ink and the actual executed Action path subject to device permissions.
A recorded session MUST retain RouteHistory and timing data sufficient to replay or export the recorded route.
Replacing an existing recording MUST be reviewable and undoable; destructive replacement without a recoverable prior revision is prohibited.
AI-aware authoring and live presentation
The persistent AI bar MUST receive permission-filtered semantic context for all authorised slides, off-screen objects, speaker notes, Actions graphs, component definitions/state, media metadata, runnable code metadata, 3D objects, drawings and current presentation-session state. Semantic context MUST be preferred over screenshot/OCR interpretation.
Read-only AI mode MAY inspect, explain, summarise, rehearse and propose changes, but MUST NOT mutate the presentation or live runtime state.
Write AI mode MAY create/edit slides, notes, objects, components and Actions only through typed Present APIs and the normal permission, revision, undo and conflict semantics.
Requests such as branching on an audience answer, converting objects into a flashcard component or highlighting diagram regions on click MUST produce canonical typed graph/component mutations rather than UI automation.
AI-generated edits MUST be attributable to a revision/audit event and MUST be reversible through the normal revision/undo model.
Video, audio, podcast, print and static export
Present MUST generate Video, Audio and Podcast outputs from the canonical presentation model rather than from a detached textual summary.
Video rendering MUST execute the actual presentation runtime and timed Actions for a selected route.
Audio output MUST use presentation content and speaker/narration configuration without rendering slide visuals.
Podcast output MUST transform presentation content into a conversational treatment using selected Dulche Voice models/voices.
Generated narration/script and timeline MUST be previewable and editable before final rendering.
An interactive presentation may have multiple valid routes. Export MUST require one of RECORDED_SESSION, DEFAULT_ACTION_PATH or EXPLICIT_BRANCH_PATH. Present MUST NOT guess arbitrary button/quiz choices.
Static output MUST support full slides, selected slides, notes pages, outline text and configurable handout layouts with multiple slides per page where the target supports them.
PDF/image export MUST expose slide range, hidden-slide inclusion, background/transparency handling and notes inclusion.
Speaker notes are excluded from audience-facing static output by default.
Page size, orientation, margins and scaling MUST be explicit and previewable for print/handout output.
Import/export compatibility contract
Import/export MUST produce an explicit CompatibilityReport whenever a source or destination format cannot represent the complete native model.
CompatibilityIssue {
  IssueID: StableID
  Severity: INFO | WARNING | ERROR
  Direction: IMPORT | EXPORT
  FeatureType: string
  SourceTargetID?: StableID
  Description: string
  Resolution: TRANSLATED | DEGRADED | OMITTED | BLOCKED
}
Compatibility severity semantics:
INFO means the construct is translated without user-visible semantic loss; export/import may continue without acknowledgement.
WARNING means the construct is degraded or omitted but the operation can still produce a usable artifact; the issue MUST identify the exact affected source/target and resulting behaviour.
ERROR means continuing would violate the selected export/import policy, produce an invalid artifact or cause unaccepted destructive loss; the operation MUST block until the user changes the policy, removes the blocking feature or chooses a supported target.
TRANSLATED means the destination preserves the source semantics; DEGRADED means semantics remain usable but differ; OMITTED means the construct is absent from the result; BLOCKED means no result is committed.
PPTX/ODP legacy transitions and animations MUST be translated into Actions graphs when representable.
Present MUST NOT retain a hidden executable legacy animation engine solely for compatibility.
Unsupported or partially translated import behaviour MUST be listed in the CompatibilityReport.
PPTX/ODP export MUST compile the representable Actions subset into destination-native constructs.
Custom components, arbitrary stateful branching, runnable code, Generative UI, AI behaviours and richer interactive 3D logic that cannot be represented MUST be reported explicitly; silent disappearance is prohibited.
Import/export validation MUST cover slides, masters/layouts, text, speaker notes, media, supported charts/tables, links, accessibility metadata and representable Actions.
.9to1p is the authoritative full-fidelity format. A successful destination file creation is not sufficient evidence of compatibility.
Accessibility
Present MUST expose accessible semantics in both authoring and presentation runtimes.
Relevant visual objects MUST support alt text/description.
Slides MUST have an explicit reading order; interactive content MUST have an explicit focus order when reading order is insufficient.
Interactive components MUST expose accessible role, name, state/value and keyboard interaction.
Authoring and presenting MUST be operable without a pointer for required workflows.
Focus MUST be visible; required state MUST NOT be communicated only by colour.
Zoom/text scaling and reduced-motion behaviour MUST be supported.
An accessibility checker MUST identify at least missing required alt text, problematic reading/focus order and inaccessible interactive controls.
Accessibility metadata MUST round-trip through .9to1p and MUST be preserved in PPTX/ODP when the destination construct can represent it.
Security, permissions and external side effects
Present Actions, generated UI, runnable code, media, participant input and AI integrations MUST obey the platform permission broker and risk classification. A presentation MUST NOT gain arbitrary filesystem, network, account or device control merely because it is opened or presented.
Viewer interaction MUST NOT grant permissions that the presenting user/session does not already possess.
External side effects invoked from a slideshow MUST use the same confirmation, idempotency, audit and typed-error rules as the equivalent app/Automation action.
A denied permission MUST produce an explicit denied/error result that Actions can handle; the runtime MUST NOT silently substitute a weaker or different side effect.
Presentation content from untrusted sources MUST NOT be able to modify Home permissions or disable sandbox restrictions.
Typed Present API and mutation semantics
Present MUST expose versioned typed APIs sufficient for Spaces, Automations, Dulche and other authorised apps to inspect and mutate presentation state without UI simulation.
MutationRequest {
  BaseRevisionID: RevisionID
  OperationID: StableID
  ActorContext: PermissionFilteredActorContext
}
MutationResult {
  RevisionID: RevisionID
  ChangedIDs: StableID[]
  Warnings: Warning[]
  CompatibilityIssues: CompatibilityIssue[]
}
Mutation operations MUST reject a stale incompatible BaseRevisionID with REVISION_CONFLICT rather than silently overwriting newer edits. OperationID MUST support idempotent retry for operations declared retry-safe.
Required public capability groups:
Presentation/slide/object queries, including selection-safe semantic search.
CreateSlide, DuplicateSlide, MoveSlide, DeleteSlide and restore/recovery operations.
InsertObject, UpdateObject, DeleteObject and shared-object operations.
GetSpeakerNotes and SetSpeakerNotes.
GetStatistics with an explicit StatisticsScope.
Theme/master/layout read and mutation operations.
Actions.GetGraph, Actions.ValidateGraph and Actions.ApplyPatch.
Components.CreateType, Components.UpdateType and component-instance operations.
Media, 3D and drawing query/control operations.
StartPresentation, GetPresentationSession, NavigatePresentation, PausePresentation, ResumePresentation and EndPresentation.
Typed errors MUST distinguish at least NOT_FOUND, INVALID_ARGUMENT, PERMISSION_DENIED, REVISION_CONFLICT, UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE, RUNTIME_ERROR and CANCELLED. APIs MUST NOT collapse these states into a generic success=false result with no machine-readable reason.
Release acceptance criteria
Release conformance requires behaviour evidence. Source presence, UI screenshots or a successful build are insufficient on their own.
The release validation suite MUST demonstrate, at minimum:
Create -> edit -> save -> close -> reopen with slide/object identity, masters/layouts/themes and speaker notes preserved.
Live word/character statistics for selection, slide, notes and full-presentation scopes, including separate slide/notes totals and speaking-time calculation.
Mature conventional slide editing: multi-select, group, align/distribute, exact geometry, z-order, lock, crop/mask where applicable, guides/grid/snapping and object-tree operations.
A non-trivial Actions graph containing an event, condition, parallel/sequential work, state mutation and navigation.
A Transitions-sidebar edit that produces an Actions subgraph and survives Open in Actions plus a compatible round-trip back to the simple editor.
All required built-in interactive components and one reusable custom Component Type with revisioned linked instances.
A Generative UI object connected to Actions without raw HTML/JavaScript injection.
One sandboxed runnable-code example that emits a typed result and one denied-capability test.
Audio/video playback through typed controls and media events.
A supported glTF/GLB model with camera/hotspot Actions.
Structured live ink in at least SESSION_ONLY and EXPLICIT_COMMIT modes.
Presenter View with current/next slide, notes and timer while AudienceOutput remains free of presenter-only state.
Rehearsal/recording with recoverable RouteHistory.
PPTX/ODP import containing legacy transitions/animations with translated or explicitly reported results.
PPTX/ODP export with a CompatibilityReport for any non-representable native feature.
PDF/handout/notes-page export with explicit slide range and notes policy.
Keyboard-only authoring/presenting and accessibility-checker coverage.
AI Read-only versus Write enforcement and typed mutation auditability.
Crash/interrupted-save recovery and concurrent-edit/revision-conflict behaviour.
Cross-app shared-object clipboard fidelity for Present <-> Write, Present <-> Canvas and Present <-> Boards, using at least one shared text object and one non-text shared object supported by each tested endpoint.
Any acceptance case that fails by silently omitting data, silently degrading behaviour, bypassing typed APIs or exposing presenter-only/private state to the audience MUST block release conformance.
Canvas
Purpose, ownership and boundaries
9-1 Canvas is the handwriting, sketching, drawing and freeform spatial-authoring application in 9to1. Canvas owns Canvas artifacts, spatial composition, page/infinite-canvas geometry, drawing/ink editing, Canvas tool state, Canvas-specific view state and the Canvas domain API.
Canvas is not a Boards replacement and MUST NOT become a generic workspace/page system. Boards owns structured mixed-content workspaces and pages; Canvas owns freeform spatial drawing documents. Boards MAY host a live Canvas artifact, but the embedded Canvas remains owned by Canvas and retains its Canvas ArtifactID.
Canvas MUST use CUI for the visible application shell, menus, toolbars, inspectors, dialogs, launch screen and ordinary controls. A specialised accelerated drawing/rendering surface MAY exist as a CUI control for performance; .cui markup MUST NOT require each stroke sample to become an independent generic UI widget.
Donor and upstream contract
Rnote is the authoritative donor for mature handwriting, drawing, stroke, selection, rendering and applicable import/export behaviour. The implementation agent MUST obtain the latest appropriate stable Rnote source when the Canvas implementation pass begins, record the exact upstream repository, commit/release identifier and licence, and include the selected donor source in the Canvas source tree/build graph in accordance with the global Source & Donor Apps contract.
Canvas MUST maintain a donor-parity manifest generated from inspection of the selected Rnote revision. Every user-visible donor capability MUST be classified as PRESERVE, REPLACE_WITH_9TO1_NATIVE_EQUIVALENT or NOT_APPLICABLE. An unclassified donor feature is a release blocker, not permission to omit it.
PRESERVE means the donor behaviour, shortcuts, input semantics, quality-of-life behaviour and applicable data behaviour remain available through the 9to1 implementation.
REPLACE_WITH_9TO1_NATIVE_EQUIVALENT is used when 9to1 already owns the equivalent platform capability, including CUI shell/UI, Dulche AI, Home permission handling, Files storage integration or other shared 9to1 services.
NOT_APPLICABLE requires a concrete technical, legal or product-boundary reason and validation that its omission does not remove expected Canvas functionality.
Proprietary donor AI MUST NOT be copied. Any applicable AI-assisted behaviour is implemented through Dulche and the Canvas typed API.
Supported platforms and capability negotiation
Canvas MUST ship on every 9to1 platform for which the app is not explicitly exempt under the global platform/web rules. Desktop/native and web implementations MUST share the same Canvas artifact schema, stable identities, domain API semantics and server-side canonical entities.
Platform-specific input or rendering capability differences MUST be negotiated explicitly. Hardware capability absence MUST NOT be misrepresented as format incapability.
If pressure is unavailable, Canvas records and renders strokes using the declared non-pressure fallback without deleting pressure data already stored in the artifact.
If tilt, barrel buttons, palm rejection assistance or another device capability is unavailable, the UI MUST disable or omit only the dependent control and expose a capability-unavailable reason where the absence is user-relevant.
Opening an artifact on a lower-capability platform MUST preserve unsupported stored data for later use on a capable platform.
Canonical artifact model and identity
The native full-fidelity Canvas format is .9to1c. Persisted Canvas data MUST be schema-versioned. Readers MUST migrate, preserve or reject incompatible schema versions explicitly and MUST NOT guess the meaning of unknown fields.
CanvasArtifact {
  ArtifactID: StableID
  SchemaVersion: Version
  RevisionID: RevisionID
  DisplayName: string
  CanvasMode: INFINITE | PAGED
  PageOrder: PageID[]
  SharedResources: ResourceRef[]
  CollaborationMetadata: CollaborationState
  DocumentSettings: CanvasDocumentSettings
}
CanvasPage {
  PageID: StableID
  Bounds: InfiniteBounds | PageBounds
  Background: BackgroundDefinition
  LayerOrder: LayerID[]
  ObjectOrder: ObjectID[]
  RevisionID: RevisionID
}
CanvasObject {
  ObjectID: StableID
  ObjectTypeID: TypeID
  LayerID: LayerID
  Geometry: Geometry
  Transform: Transform
  Style: ObjectStyle
  Accessibility: AccessibilityMetadata
  SharedObjectRef?: SharedObjectReference
  RevisionID: RevisionID
}
InkStroke {
  StrokeID: StableID
  ToolDefinitionID: ToolDefinitionID
  Samples: StrokeSample[]
  ResolvedBrushProperties: BrushProperties
  Transform: Transform
  RevisionID: RevisionID
}
ArtifactID, PageID, LayerID, ObjectID and StrokeID MUST remain stable across rename, move, reorder, zoom, pan, style change and save/reopen. Display names, page positions, z-order and file paths MUST NOT be used as persistent identity.
Document mode and page-type model
Canvas MUST support both INFINITE and PAGED document modes as first-class modes selectable through the top-right quick-settings surface.
INFINITE mode provides a spatially unbounded working area for normal user workflows and MUST NOT expose an artificial page edge as document structure.
PAGED mode contains ordered PageID entities with explicit page size, orientation where applicable and page/background settings.
Page size, orientation, background and page ordering are document state and therefore collaborate, persist and travel with the artifact.
Changing between INFINITE and PAGED is a structural conversion, not a cosmetic toggle. The conversion workflow MUST preview the mapping of existing content, identify content that would cross/clash with generated page boundaries, and require explicit confirmation before committing a conversion that changes layout.
Conversion MUST be undoable/recoverable through document history and MUST NOT clip, discard or rasterise existing objects silently.
Persistence, autosave and recovery
Canvas persistence MUST be atomic at the smallest user-visible document mutation/revision boundary supported by the storage architecture. A partially written resource MUST NOT make the last known-good artifact revision unreadable.
Autosave MUST persist committed document mutations without requiring a manual Save command.
A save failure MUST surface an explicit unsaved/error state and retain recoverable local work.
Crash recovery MUST restore the last durable revision and recover newer journaled/temporary operations where available.
Imported source files MUST NOT be destructively overwritten merely because they were opened. Overwrite/export requires an explicit user operation appropriate to the source format.
Closing an artifact while durable persistence is unresolved MUST provide an explicit recovery choice rather than silently discarding changes.
Launch screen and document lifecycle
Canvas MUST implement the global launch-screen contract using real Files/storage state. Required launch capabilities are Create Blank, templates/starter canvases where supported, Recent, Favourites/Pinned, Shared with Me, search, Open and Import.
Create Blank MUST create a real Canvas artifact with a new ArtifactID and selected/default CanvasMode. Launch entries MUST NOT be mock cards.
Opening, renaming, moving, favouriting, sharing and deleting an entire Canvas artifact MUST integrate with Files' canonical artifact/storage semantics. Moving or renaming a file MUST NOT change ArtifactID.
Primary Canvas shell
The normal editing surface MUST prioritise the canvas and MUST NOT permanently reserve a ribbon, large left tool rail or large inspector panel for routine drawing.
Top-left document controls:
A compact ≡ pill opens the Canvas/application command surface for document/application commands assigned to it by the final CUI command model.
A neighbouring document-name pill displays the current DisplayName, for example Notebook 3, and provides document-level operations including rename, location/document information and applicable document collaboration/navigation commands.
Changing DisplayName MUST NOT change ArtifactID.
Bottom primary toolbar:
The canonical default order is Select, Pan, Pen, Eraser, Insert, Tools, AI. The toolbar is a floating horizontal CUI surface centred near the bottom of the primary canvas.
| Select | Pan | Pen | Eraser | Insert | Tools | AI |
The currently selected tool MUST display both its icon and human-readable name.
Non-selected tools MAY display icon-only in the compact state, but their names and primary shortcut MUST be exposed by hover and keyboard-focus tooltips.
The toolbar MUST remain usable with mouse, touch, stylus and keyboard navigation.
Responsive compaction MAY use controlled overflow or horizontal scrolling; tools MUST NOT silently disappear.
The active editing tool is document-session/editor state, not persisted canonical document content unless a specific tool setting is declared as a user preference.
Contextual tool-options host
When the active tool exposes contextual options, Canvas MUST render one secondary floating options surface immediately above the primary bottom toolbar. Tool implementations MUST declare their options through a common option schema rather than constructing unrelated private popup systems.
CanvasToolDefinition {
  ToolID: StableToolID
  DisplayName: string
  Icon: IconRef
  Shortcut?: Shortcut
  InputModes: InputMode[]
  Cursor: CursorDefinition
  OptionSchema?: ToolOptionSchema
  CapabilityRequirements: CapabilityID[]
  DomainActionMappings: ActionID[]
}
Selecting a tool activates it. Re-selecting the active tool MUST open/focus its deeper option surface when that tool has options. A long-press or context menu MAY expose secondary actions, but no required capability may exist only behind long-press.
Select and Pan
Select is the canonical object/stroke manipulation tool. It MUST support the applicable Rnote-derived selection modes plus shared-object selection semantics, including single selection, multi-selection and lasso/area selection where supported by the donor/object type.
Applicable selected content MUST support move, resize, rotate, duplicate, delete/recover, cut/copy/paste, group/ungroup, z-order/layer movement, alignment/distribution where meaningful and lock/unlock.
An operation unsupported by a selected object type MUST be disabled with a defined capability reason rather than appearing to succeed.
Pan is an explicit navigation tool. Pointer/stylus movement while Pan is active MUST navigate the viewport and MUST NOT create or modify drawing content.
Pen system and preset pens
Pen is the primary structured ink-authoring tool and MUST preserve applicable Rnote pen/brush behaviour. Pen options appear in the contextual tool-options surface above the bottom toolbar.
Canvas MUST ship with useful preset pens derived from the available drawing engines in the selected donor revision. Presets MUST cover the major donor-supported writing/drawing instrument classes that remain applicable, such as ordinary ink/ballpoint-style writing, fountain/variable-width ink, pencil and highlighter/marker behaviour where the donor supports them.
PenPreset {
  PenPresetID: StableID
  Name: string
  ToolEngineID: ToolEngineID
  TipOrNib: NibDefinition
  BaseWidth: Length
  PressureCurve?: Curve
  TiltResponse?: TiltDefinition
  Opacity: number
  Colour: Colour
  Smoothing: SmoothingDefinition
  Stabilisation: StabilisationDefinition
  EngineParameters: Map<string, TypedValue>
  Favourite: boolean
  RevisionID: RevisionID
}
The Pen menu MUST provide a Custom Pen workflow. Users MUST be able to create, preview, save, duplicate, rename, reorder, favourite, edit and delete/recover custom pen presets.
The custom-pen editor MUST expose only properties supported by the selected ToolEngineID.
Saving a pen preset MUST NOT retroactively alter existing strokes unexpectedly. Existing strokes retain resolved brush properties or an explicit versioned preset reference sufficient to reproduce their authored appearance.
Preset and custom pen selection MUST be keyboard and touch accessible.
Eraser
The Eraser tool MUST expose at least two user-facing modes in its contextual options:
Natural Eraser — drag over drawing content to erase according to the configured donor-supported erasure semantics, including partial/stroke behaviour where provided.
Quick Eraser — click/tap a target stroke or object to remove the complete resolved target immediately.
Quick Eraser deletion MUST use the same document history/domain delete operation as other Canvas deletion and therefore MUST remain undoable/recoverable. The target-resolution rule MUST be deterministic when objects overlap.
Insert catalogue and parity
Insert is the structured object insertion catalogue. Its first-level menu MUST use the following category order and each category opens a submenu to the right on desktop:
Text   >
Shapes >
Media  >
Table  >
Other  >
The first-level menu is category-only. Selecting/hovering a category MUST NOT insert a default object silently.
Text submenu:
Text Box — freely positioned shared rich-text object.
Heading — text object with a semantic heading role and heading defaults; it MUST NOT be implemented only as visually larger text.
Paragraph — text object with a semantic paragraph/body role and paragraph defaults.
Shapes submenu:
Opens the registered shared shape/line catalogue supported by Canvas, including applicable lines/connectors and shape families exposed by the Shared Productivity Engine.
Shapes MUST use the same canonical shared shape definitions and editing behaviour used by other 9to1 productivity surfaces rather than a reduced Canvas-only shape model.
Media submenu:
Image.
Audio.
Video.
Media objects MUST use the corresponding shared media representation and preserve editable metadata/behaviour rather than flattening to a thumbnail.
Table submenu:
Canvas MUST expose the shared table creation experience and the full Canvas-applicable shared table feature set.
Canvas MUST NOT implement a reduced Canvas-only table type. Table editing capabilities, structure and formatting come from the shared table engine; Canvas owns freeform placement/transform around the table.
Other submenu:
Other contains registered Canvas-compatible shared object types that do not warrant their own first-level category.
Graph MUST be available through Other using the canonical shared graph representation.
Other MAY include Link, File/Artifact, Embed, Equation, Code, Generative UI and additional registered shared types when the shared capability registry declares them Canvas-compatible.
Drawing MUST NOT appear as a separate Insert item because freeform pen/drawing is already a primary Canvas capability.
Insert catalogue parity has two mandatory dimensions:
Catalogue parity — every shared productivity object type declared Canvas-compatible by the shared capability registry MUST be reachable through Insert.
Behaviour parity — after insertion, the object MUST retain the shared object's complete applicable behaviour. Canvas MUST NOT replace a shared object with a feature-reduced Canvas-specific approximation.
InsertCategory {
  CategoryID: StableID
  DisplayName: string
  Icon: IconRef
  Order: integer
  Entries: InsertEntryID[]
}
InsertEntry {
  InsertEntryID: StableID
  ObjectTypeID: TypeID
  DisplayName: string
  Icon: IconRef
  CapabilityRequirements: CapabilityID[]
  CreateActionID: ActionID
}
The Insert UI MUST be generated from registered insertion capabilities plus the fixed category taxonomy above. Adding a registered shared object MUST NOT require a separate incompatible Canvas object implementation.
Desktop cascading menus MUST use conventional keyboard behaviour: Up/Down move, Right opens a submenu, Left returns, Enter/Space invokes and Escape closes the current menu level. Touch interaction MUST provide an explicit navigable submenu/back model and MUST NOT depend on hover.
Tools family
Tools is the home for specialised Canvas instruments that do not warrant permanent top-level toolbar slots. The exact list MUST be derived from the selected Rnote donor parity manifest and shared Canvas capabilities rather than an arbitrary hand-written subset.
Applicable geometry, line/arrow, ruler/measurement, fill/colour-picker, specialised selection and other donor tools MAY be organised here while retaining their donor behaviour. A tool moved into Tools is not optional merely because it is not a top-level button.
A future pin/favourite mechanism MAY allow users to promote specialised tools to the primary toolbar, but the default canonical toolbar remains Select, Pan, Pen, Eraser, Insert, Tools, AI.
Top-right quick-settings pill
A compact switch/settings pill MUST appear at the top-right of the Canvas editing surface. Activating it opens a dropdown for high-frequency document-level and editor-level settings. It is not a replacement for the complete Settings application.
Document-scoped quick settings MUST include:
Canvas/page type: INFINITE or PAGED.
Page size and orientation when PAGED.
Background colour/design, including registered ruled/grid/dot or other supported background patterns and their applicable spacing/design parameters.
Other document settings explicitly registered as quick-adjustable by Canvas.
Editor/user-scoped quick settings MUST include:
