Numeric, Boolean, text and structured/list values MUST be distinguishable. Incompatible assignments/connections are rejected or require an explicit conversion. Renaming a property MUST not break its bindings. Removing one previews dependent formulas and controls and requires repair or an explicit unresolved state rather than quietly replacing references with zero.
Derived calculations MUST follow validated dependencies. Circular combinational dependencies, invalid types, division/domain errors and unavailable inputs MUST be surfaced at their actual source, not hidden as plausible values. Simulations that require feedback MUST use explicit state/time-step semantics rather than relying on an uncontrolled formula cycle. Evaluation MUST have bounded resource use, cancellation and inspectable diagnostics. Long-running calculation MUST not block navigation or Stop.
Run/Preview shows the interactive output with Play/Run, Pause/Stop where time-based execution applies, Reset and inspectable current input/output values. Runtime experimentation MUST be separate from saved authoring defaults: moving a slider during a viewer session changes that session, not every reader's shared model. An editor can explicitly apply chosen inputs as new defaults. Reset restores the declared initial state; reopening an authored model MUST not silently resume unintended external actions. Controlled calculations with the same revision and inputs MUST behave consistently; nondeterministic inputs and random seeds MUST be declared when used.
TF-P03 — Safety, reuse and acceptance
Expressions and scripts MUST execute in the declared sandbox, not arbitrary host code. No file, network, credential, process or device access is implicitly granted by opening or running a Prototype. External actions, when supported, go through existing typed app APIs and Home permissions, with visible effects and cancellation rules. Reader preview MUST not execute consequential actions solely because an author embedded them. The model MUST remain inspectable when execution is blocked.
Measured/imported values, assumptions, calculations and outputs MUST be identifiable in the inspector and relevant output presentation. Units and declared limitations MUST be preserved. AI-generated assumptions MUST not be presented as measurements or validated predictions. AI edits are reviewable typed model operations with normal undo, validation and source permissions. Reusable components retain stable definitions and explicit dependency versions; a component update MUST not silently break existing instances.
Prototype integrates with Files, Spaces, Link, Boards and Paths through registered renderers, references and typed actions. A reader may adjust permitted local inputs without acquiring authoring rights. Native export/import preserves the model and declared dependencies; static output exports are labelled as non-interactive. Missing components keep their payload and show a repair state rather than disappearing.
Prototype acceptance MUST build a working calculator with two inputs, a typed formula and output; build a bounded time-based example with Run/Pause/Reset; bind a slider and switch; display a chart; reuse a component; reject invalid types and a dependency cycle; change inputs without changing saved defaults; recover from a runtime error; and prove that an untrusted script cannot reach host files or network without an authorised capability. Save/reopen and API-driven edits MUST preserve the same model and behaviour.
Paths
TF-H01 — Authoring, steps and route UI
Paths authors guided, repeatable interactive experiences with steps, choices, activities, checkpoints and branching routes. It is not a fixed presentation, an open-ended Binder overview or a sequence improvised afresh by AI. A Path may provide a guided process, exploration route or overview towards an outcome, with the available routes determined by its authored structure.
The authoring editor MUST provide a step library/outline, a route graph, a selected-step content editor, a condition/action inspector and Preview/Test. Add step offers information, choice, activity, checkpoint and outcome/end behaviour through typed step definitions. Steps can contain supported shared content and authorised embedded artifacts. Authors can reorder outline entries, connect or disconnect routes, label choices, designate the starting step, edit conditions, add checkpoints and define explicit completion outcomes. Graph position is not route identity or step order.
Each choice MUST have a human-readable label and stable target. Conditional routing MUST expose its condition, required values and fallback/error behaviour. No eligible route MUST show a recoverable blocked state rather than select a random next step. Multiple eligible automatic routes require an explicit authored priority/selection rule and MUST not depend on incidental storage order. Deliberate loops/retries are allowed when explicitly authored and controllable; accidental automatic loops, missing targets and unreachable required outcomes MUST be detected in validation.
Preview/Test MUST run against an identified draft revision with disposable test progress, offer reset and route inspection, and show the choice/condition responsible for each transition. Authors MUST be able to test alternative inputs and inspect unreachable/missing routes without modifying real users' progress. Updating the shared authored Path uses a deliberate validated revision commit; a preview session is not automatically the published reader revision.
TF-H02 — Reader experience and durable progress
The reader surface MUST show the current step, its content, available choices/actions, relevant checkpoint/completion status and a route/overview affordance when allowed by the authored Path. Continue appears only when its conditions are satisfied. Back/previous navigation, where permitted, MUST not repeat external side effects or silently clear completed work. Branch-dependent length MUST not be presented as a fictitious fixed percentage; show meaningful visited/checkpoint status instead.
Progress MUST be durable and separate from authored content, with stable PathID, authored RevisionID, UserID or clearly scoped guest-session identity, AttemptID, current StepID, visited route, responses, checkpoint states, completion outcome and timestamps. A signed-in reader can resume their authorised attempt after restart or on another compatible device. Guest/local-only progress MUST be labelled honestly and MUST NOT be represented as cross-device account sync.
Readers can restart/reset and complete the same Path more than once. Restart creates a new attempt with clean progress while preserving previous completed attempts under the declared retention policy. Clearing saved progress is a separate confirmed deletion operation. Checkpoints persist sufficient state for safe resume. An interrupted save or duplicate transition request MUST not create duplicate completions or repeat an externally consequential action. Sensitive responses and progress are not automatically exposed to every person who can read the authored Path.
Active attempts remain bound to their authored revision by default. When a newer revision is available, the reader MUST be told; switching/restarting requires an explicit action and a validated mapping or fresh attempt. Deleted/changed steps MUST not cause silent jumps into a different route. Opening an embedded file or Prototype obeys its own permissions, and completion MUST depend on an explicit typed result, not a fragile guess from visible pixels.
TF-H03 — Integration and acceptance
Paths owns step/route semantics and progress. Its graph reuses the shared graph editor, and embedded content reuses the shared object/owning-app systems. Activities that call another app or Automation remain subject to the user's actual permissions and the action's risk; a teacher/author cannot grant those rights merely by embedding the activity. AI can help author or explain a Path through typed operations but MUST not silently replace committed routing during a reader attempt.
Paths acceptance MUST create a branching experience with two outcomes, a required activity and checkpoint; preview both routes; detect a missing target and an automatic loop; resume a real attempt after restart; complete it twice with separate AttemptIDs; update the authored revision without corrupting an existing attempt; revoke a source permission; and prove that retrying a transition does not repeat an external action. Keyboard, screen-reader and narrow-screen users MUST be able to complete the same authored route.
Replay
TF-R01 — Explicit capture and source selection
Replay creates explorable records of how selected work developed. Its core model is semantic revisions, events, work states and checkpoints, not a raw screen recording. Optional screenshots, video and narration may accompany that record. Capture MUST be explicitly started and limited to the selected authorised sources; opening Replay MUST NOT begin recording unrelated work or private activity.
New capture MUST present a source picker, selected files/sub-objects, available capture capabilities per owning app, destination, retention/export implications and optional media settings. Unsupported semantic sources are identified before starting; the UI MUST not silently claim semantic capture when it can only obtain an image. Optional microphone/camera/screen access requires its own explicit selection and platform permissions. A preview of the scope MUST be available before Start.
During capture, show an unmistakable Recording/Paused state, selected-source summary, elapsed session information, Add checkpoint, annotation/narration controls and Pause/Stop. A source-scope change is explicit and timestamped. Stop MUST stop subscriptions and selected media capture, finalise durable state and show any pending/failed material. Losing permission to a source MUST stop future capture for that source and expose the limitation rather than continue through a cached unrestricted channel.
TF-R02 — Semantic timeline and playback UI
The editor/player MUST provide a chronological event/checkpoint timeline, source tracks/filtering, a central historical artifact viewer, a checkpoint/annotation list and an inspector showing the selected source revision and capture completeness. Users can label/reorder presentation chapters where supported without falsifying the underlying event order, add explanations and choose a shareable presentation range. Changes to Replay presentation MUST NOT rewrite the original source's history.
Playback MUST support play/pause, seek, previous/next checkpoint and adjustable playback speed for timed material. At a checkpoint the recipient can inspect the document, calculation, diagram or other supported artifact as it existed then. The historical viewer MUST be visibly read-only and identify the captured revision. It MUST NOT resolve a checkpoint to the source's latest content merely because that is easier to load. Narrative media follows the selected timeline while retaining accessible captions/transcripts when provided.
Capture records MUST include SessionID, authorised source identities, ordered EventIDs, event/revision provenance, CheckpointIDs, timestamps/sequence, required base revisions or validated snapshot references, annotations and media references. Replay stores enough authorised retained state or pinned revision dependencies to reconstruct the included checkpoints under the declared retention policy. It MUST NOT depend on an ephemeral cache that disappears after the app closes. Missing bases, gaps and unavailable retained sources produce an explicit incomplete-checkpoint state, not invented reconstruction.
A Continue from here action is available only when the owning app supports an independent copy from that checkpoint and permissions permit it. The action shows destination, copy scope and unavailable dependencies, creates a new canonical artifact through the owner and opens that copy. It MUST NOT restore the original over its current version or imply that a Replay viewer has edit rights to the source.
TF-R03 — Review, sharing, failure and acceptance
Before sharing/export, Replay MUST provide an included-material review showing files, revisions, annotations, optional recordings and recipient access implications. Referenced live access and an exported independent snapshot are distinct. Copy/export rights are required for retained source bytes shared independently. Excluding or redacting captured content MUST also address derived thumbnails, search text, transcripts and dependent snapshots; metadata MUST not leak a supposedly removed secret. A presentation trim alone MUST not be labelled permanent redaction.
Session state MUST distinguish Not started, Recording, Paused, Finalising, Ready, Incomplete and Error. Interruption recovery resumes from a durable checkpoint/journal without claiming the missing interval was captured. Storage/quota exhaustion, unavailable owning apps and media-device failure MUST be visible, bounded and recoverable. Media failure MUST not silently destroy valid semantic checkpoints. Delete/retention cleanup applies to Replay-owned captures and assets, not the original source documents.
Replay acceptance MUST capture selected changes in two supported artifacts, exclude an unrelated open file, pause/resume, create an annotated checkpoint, restart after interruption, inspect historical state after the original advances, reveal a missing dependency, stop on revoked permission and create an authorised independent copy. Export/share review MUST detect excluded material in thumbnails/transcripts and MUST not claim that view-only rights permit exporting source bytes.
Variants
TF-V01 — Integrated variant UI and branch identity
Variants MUST ship within Write, Data, Present, Canvas, Picture, Prototype and Sites. It is not a separate app or Files organisation type. Version history answers which earlier state to return to; Variants lets users explore multiple directions in parallel without overwriting the starting version merely to experiment.
Each supported app MUST expose a consistent Variants entry near the document/version controls. The panel lists the main/current working line and named alternatives with base/current revision, modified state and useful compare/merge status. Required actions are Create variant, Switch, Rename, Duplicate variant, Compare, Bring changes back/Merge and Archive/remove variant through the owning recovery rules. The active variant MUST remain clearly identified in the editor title/status and save destination. A user MUST not unknowingly type into the main version after switching to an alternative.
Creating a variant records a stable VariantID, parent/base RevisionID and its own revision head. Switching resolves unsaved work through save or an explicit recoverable decision, not silent discard. A variant is a separately addressable branch of the owning artifact, not a manually duplicated filename or Files shortcut. Autosave, undo/redo, collaboration, search/deep links and restart MUST retain the active branch identity. A deep link to a variant MUST not silently open Main.
TF-V02 — Comparison, selective merge and conflicts
Compare MUST allow selection of base/source/target variants and provide content-appropriate side-by-side or change-focused presentation. The interface MUST identify additions, removals, edits and conflicts, offer next/previous change and show what accepting a selected change will affect. Colour alone MUST not convey the difference. An edit to the source or target during comparison invalidates or refreshes the merge preview rather than permitting a stale overwrite.
Merge MUST be an owning-app semantic operation against explicit source, base and expected target revisions. It requires a preview, selected changes or a clearly labelled whole-version choice, validation and a final commit. Compatible independent changes can be combined; overlapping or incompatible changes remain visible for resolution. Resolution must state Keep target, Use source or the supported manual choice. The implementation MUST NOT guess away conflicts or claim a generic byte merge is safe for every artifact type.
If safe selective merge is unavailable for a particular content operation, the app MUST provide a faithful compare-and-choose workflow and explain its scope. Choosing the source creates a new target revision while retaining recoverable history; it MUST NOT erase the target's earlier line. A failed/cancelled merge leaves both branches intact. Retry is idempotent, and a revision mismatch returns a conflict rather than overwriting newer work. Archive/remove MUST not delete the only retained content without the normal recovery/confirmation contract.
TF-V03 — Required owning-app comparison semantics
Write MUST compare stable text/block structure, edits, formatting and referenced objects; text and formatting conflicts remain distinguishable. Data MUST compare sheets/tables, stable rows/columns/cells, values, formulas, schema and named dependencies; it MUST not splice unrelated rows merely because their current indices match. Present MUST compare slide identity/order, objects, content, layout and presentation-level dependencies.
Canvas MUST compare stable objects, geometry, strokes, grouping, connectors and source references. Picture MUST compare layers, masks, transformations, adjustments and image data using the actual supported document structure; incompatible raster edits require a visible choose/manual-resolution path rather than invented pixel-level semantic merging. Prototype MUST compare typed objects/properties, formulas, bindings, component definitions and relationships and validate the resulting model before commit.
Sites MUST compare pages, components, routes, content, assets and settings through Sites' own model. Comparing, switching or merging a site variant MUST NOT publish or change production deployment by itself. Deployment remains an explicit existing Sites operation with its separate permissions and confirmations. Secrets, credentials and live provider state MUST not be copied into a branch merely because project settings are versioned.
Variants acceptance MUST create, edit, switch, compare and bring changes back in all seven apps; retain the starting version; expose an overlapping conflict; exercise the safe whole-version fallback; reject a stale merge; recover after save interruption; and reopen at the selected branch. Test each app's specific content families above. A shared button bar without working per-app comparison/merge is not coverage.
Cross-app delivery and acceptance
TF-X01 — Embeds, Boards pages and conversational editing
Boards MUST be able to include a Flow or Binder as a page referencing the same canonical Link document. It MUST also support a Files Sheet as a live Files-owned organisation page, rather than mislabelling Sheet as a Link type. The same registered embedding contract applies to the other declared compatible organisation/artifact surfaces. The host page MUST identify the owning source, respect reader/editor capability, provide Open original and preserve navigation back to the Board.
A Binder or Flow placed on a Sheet MUST open through the Sheet's chosen policy while keeping the surrounding notes/files and viewport. A Stash on a Sheet remains an ordered group. A Prototype embedded in Link, Boards or a Path MUST retain its actual model and permitted session-local controls, not become a screenshot while being described as interactive. Replay checkpoint views remain historical. Every supported combination MUST reference canonical entities; unsupported combinations show their exact limitation instead of silently flattening or cloning.
Spaces and the persistent AI bar MUST use the same typed APIs as the UI for authorised creation, organisation and editing. The current artifact, selection, source scope, active variant and permissions MUST be supplied explicitly. AI suggestions that change organisation rules, dependencies, route logic or other significant behaviour must be inspectable and undoable. AI access remains a separate permission; opening a private file in an embed does not authorise cloud upload. Core manual workflows MUST remain usable when AI is disabled or unavailable.
TF-X02 — Canonical API action catalogue
New UI operations extend the existing canonical namespaces: 9to1.Files.Organisation, 9to1.Link, 9to1.Prototype, 9to1.Paths and 9to1.Replay. Variants actions live under the owning app's Variants capability, such as 9to1.Write.Variants; the shared implementation MUST not bypass that owner's semantics. Existing Files, shared-object and NodeGraph actions remain authoritative for their existing operations rather than being copied into incompatible new APIs.
Every mutation request MUST include the target stable IDs, typed payload, operation/idempotency key and expected revision, or an explicitly declared create precondition. Successful results identify affected objects, resulting revision and any job/change-event identity. Read/list operations accept explicit scope and filters and return bounded pages with continuation cursors. Long-running query, capture, evaluation, export and merge work exposes JobID, progress, cancellation and durable result/error. Events have stable IDs and resumable cursors. Home resolves caller identity, scopes and risk before dispatch; possession of an ID never grants access.
Files.Organisation MUST expose Create/Get/List, UpdateSettings, AddReference, RemoveReference, Reorder and the type-specific operations: Project section CRUD and assignment; Sheet object/geometry/ink/shape/connector edits and opening policy; Tree group/node/connection edits plus separately authorised Tree-layout reads; Smart rule/scope/pin updates and membership explanation; Timeline date-source/assigned-range/period edits; Pipeline stage/gate/approval/transition/mapping actions; Catalogue field/schema/local-value/view edits; Stash order/position/review/compare selection; and Matrix axis/cell/membership operations. Generic command payloads MUST have registered typed schemas, not arbitrary unvalidated JSON.
Link MUST expose document creation and retrieval, block/container CRUD, ordering/geometry, source/section/revision-policy updates, outline/search, preview and export/import. Source edits dispatch to the source owner's registered actions. Prototype MUST expose object/property/component CRUD, formula/binding/relationship/event/action updates, validation, evaluation/run/stop/reset and session-input changes. Persisting runtime values as defaults is a separate authoring action.
Paths MUST expose step/route/content CRUD, validation, preview/test sessions, authored revision commit, StartAttempt, GetProgress, SubmitResponse, Advance, checkpoint/resume, Restart and confirmed progress deletion. Reader-scoped progress actions MUST not allow changing another reader's attempt or the authored route. Replay MUST expose source capability inspection, capture creation/start/pause/resume/stop, scope changes, checkpoints/annotations, event/checkpoint retrieval, historical preview, independent-copy requests, review/redaction and export/delete. Variant APIs MUST expose branch create/list/get/rename/switch state, compare, merge preview, resolution, commit and archive/recover through each required owning app.
Action schemas MUST declare required target permissions, source permissions, reversible/destructive risk, external effects, limits and partial-success behaviour. Required structured errors include InvalidArgument, ItemNotFound, PermissionRequired, PermissionDenied, RevisionConflict, UnsupportedCapability, ProviderUnavailable, Offline, QuotaExceeded, MissingSource, MissingSourceSection, InvalidReferenceCycle, TypeMismatch, ValidationFailed, DependencyUnavailable, TransitionBlocked, CaptureIncomplete, MergeConflict and Cancelled, using existing canonical equivalents where already defined. Errors identify recoverability and the affected operation without leaking forbidden source details. Every action exposed by a context menu, keyboard command or editor control MUST be accounted for in the generated UI/API parity manifest.
TF-X03 — Platforms, responsive behaviour and resource limits
Windows, 9to1-OS and browser/web MUST implement the useful core authoring and reader experiences for this tranche using the same canonical formats, account identity, domain APIs and permissions. Native interfaces use CUI/Home; web uses the existing authenticated web-service contract and MUST not require arbitrary local filesystem/process access. A narrow viewport by itself is not a reason to replace an otherwise supported app with an unrelated simplified data model.
The operating contract's Android/Go timing exception remains limited to newly added complex Terra-form surfaces. Any temporary read-only/limited-editing mode MUST still provide source-aware navigation, faithful content, accessible controls, per-user reading/progress state where supported and a visible explanation of unavailable authoring. Tree viewers still receive only View. No disabled authoring control may pretend to save. Full Android/Go authoring parity remains required after the temporary fallback; existing stronger mobile functionality MUST not regress.
At narrow sizes, navigation and inspectors become drawers or dedicated subviews, command overflow remains discoverable and pop-ups may use full-screen routes with preserved Back state. Flow retains continuous reading; Binder retains outline and open/close exploration; Files collections retain meaningful contents views; Paths retains choices and progress; Replay retains seeking/checkpoint inspection; Variants retains source/target identity in sequential comparison. Complex spatial authoring MUST provide fit and accessible structural alternatives, not an unreadable scaled-down desktop screenshot.
Large collections/graphs/documents MUST use bounded incremental loading, preview hydration, virtualisation and subscription cleanup. Closed/off-screen embeds MUST not continue uncontrolled computation, media playback or capture. Source resolution and exports MUST detect recursion and bound dependency traversal. Query, evaluation, capture, import/export and merge limits MUST be declared by the relevant capability and shown before an operation that exceeds them; limits MUST not silently truncate content. Existing platform-wide performance/resource thresholds remain mandatory. Actual supported workload sizes and measured results MUST be recorded rather than invented completion claims.
TF-X04 — Acceptance matrix and release evidence
Every numbered Terra-form requirement group MUST have a traceable implementation and test mapping. Evidence MUST distinguish source/unit coverage from real UI, runtime, cross-app, provider and package validation. The per-feature acceptance journeys above are mandatory minimums, not optional demonstrations. Test both ordinary authoring and reader roles, source permissions independent of host permissions, empty/loading/error states, source move/rename/delete, undo/redo, reopen, offline recovery and concurrent revisions.
The Files matrix MUST cover all ten organisation types as parent and nested target, recording the exact reason for any genuinely incoherent or unsupported provider combination. Required cross-app journeys include Homework Project sections; the same file in Tree, Smart, Timeline and Pipeline without copies; a Sheet containing a Stash and Binder; the Annual report Flow; Flow/Binder/Sheet as Boards pages; an interactive Prototype in an authored Path; a Replay historical checkpoint after the source changes; and Variants in every one of the seven named apps. Tests MUST verify canonical IDs and actual content effects, not only screenshots of controls.
Visual/accessibility QA MUST inspect desktop and narrow/touch layouts, keyboard-only operation, screen-reader names/structure, visible focus, dialog return focus, 200% scaling, themes/contrast and reduced motion. Inspect normal, selected, loading, read-only, conflict and missing-source states. Verify that no pane overlaps the AI bar or prevents access to Save/Close/Back and that large canvases/graphs remain operable through their outlines. API tests MUST repeat consequential UI operations and prove equivalent permissions, validation, idempotency and results.
Recovery tests MUST interrupt source hydration, collection edits, native import/export, Prototype evaluation, Path progress writes, Replay finalisation and variant merge. Preserve originals and recoverable drafts, expose exact partial/failure state and prove safe retry. Resource tests MUST use populated realistic collections, long Flows, nested Binders, branching Paths and captured multi-source histories; record workload, platform and observed results. Empty fixtures alone do not establish production usability.
The release evidence ledger MUST identify each group as VERIFIED, IMPLEMENTED-UNVERIFIED, MISSING or BLOCKED, with tested revision/build, platform, evidence and exact remaining exception. A temporary Android/Go fallback is recorded as a scoped incomplete-authoring exception, not full parity. These tests add to, and do not replace or weaken, the operating contract, full active specification, donor parity, security, privacy, performance, native-device and package gates.
TF-X05 — Open naming decision and implementation defaults
The separate Playgrounds naming/product relationship to Prototype remains OPEN. This section does not authorise another overlapping standalone app. All other named Terra-form behaviours above are active shipping scope. No legacy migration is required for genuinely new formats unless real existing data needs it; any such data MUST be inspected and preserved before a format change.
Where a low-level representation or provider adapter detail remains unspecified, workers MUST choose the narrowest coherent implementation consistent with these visible behaviours, version and document its contract, and validate it. This discretion MUST NOT be used to invent another product, drop a required control/workflow, weaken ownership or security, flatten a native format, conceal an unsupported platform or defer a named feature. Material product changes outside these requirements require an explicit canonical decision.
Pass 3: Sol Happy
SH-01 — Purpose and required outcome
Sol Happy is the “systems online” development pass.
The pass brings the 9to1 ecosystem onto its real production infrastructure: public websites, browser applications, CAKE ID authentication, subscription billing, hosted files, hosted websites, cloud-backed application services and operational management.
The required outcome is a connected service that a user can access from a fresh device without a development environment. A user MUST be able to visit the website, create or access their account, open an eligible application in their browser, create and save real work, continue that work in a desktop application, purchase an available subscription and use the resources that subscription provides.
Public production services MUST NOT depend on a developer’s PC remaining online, a temporary development tunnel or a manually started local server.
Sol Happy includes completing the production integration of existing features. It MUST NOT become a separate, reduced product that merely resembles the desktop ecosystem.
All existing mandatory product, donor-parity, accessibility, privacy, security, API and interoperability requirements remain active. Pass 3 does not retrospectively excuse missing requirements from earlier passes. The existing definition of implementation-complete continues to require validated behaviour rather than source presence, successful builds or rendered interfaces.
SH-02 — Baseline, authority and deployment permissions
Before implementation begins, the coordinator MUST identify the authoritative repository, current accepted baseline, active workstreams, existing deployments and relevant infrastructure accounts. Existing work, credentials, production configuration and user data MUST be preserved.
The pass MUST maintain a requirement ledger using VERIFIED, IMPLEMENTED-UNVERIFIED, MISSING and BLOCKED, with evidence tied to the exact tested revision, environment and platform. Existing acceptance evidence MUST be re-evaluated where changes affect its validity.
This specification remains the product authority. Infrastructure notes, repository documentation and worker reports MUST NOT introduce competing requirements or silently narrow the pass.
Development, staging and production MUST be distinguishable. Test payments, test accounts, preview deployments and development storage MUST NOT be presented as live production services.
Approval to develop this pass is not blanket approval to spend money or change live production routing. Enabling billable services, increasing spending limits, making live test charges, changing production DNS, retiring WordPress or deleting production resources requires explicit authorisation covering the relevant action.
Independent implementation and testing MUST continue while a particular external approval is pending. A pending approval remains a visible deployment gate, not an excuse to stop unrelated work.
Sol Happy’s execution model and deadline MUST be specified separately. Terra-form’s deadline and temporary Android/Go fallback MUST NOT automatically become Pass 3 rules.
SH-03 — Production architecture and ownership
Cloudflare is the intended production hosting platform for the public websites, web applications, hosted files and hosted sites. Stripe provides subscription payment processing and associated billing services.
These providers MUST NOT replace 9to1’s product ownership boundaries.
CAKE ID and the shared account services own identity, sessions and entitlement evaluation. Files owns canonical file identity, storage operations, sharing, versions and synchronisation. Sites owns website authoring and deployment orchestration. Stripe supplies verified payment and subscription facts; it does not become the file-permission or application-authorisation system.
The proposed Cloudflare service mapping is:
Responsibility
Proposed implementation
Public website and browser-application delivery
Cloudflare-hosted, revision-pinned frontend deployments
Trusted API and integration entry points
Cloudflare Workers with explicitly scoped service bindings
File bytes, assets and deployment artifacts
R2, separated by purpose and access policy
Structured metadata and coordinated state
D1 and/or Durable Objects, selected against the required transaction and consistency contracts
Deferred processing and delivery
Queues and the existing job orchestration contracts
Cloudflare documents these services as different storage, coordination and task-processing building blocks. The exact combination MUST be validated against 9to1’s runtime, consistency, capacity and recovery requirements; it MUST NOT be selected merely because all services share one provider. Eventually consistent KV MUST NOT be the sole authority for operations requiring immediate, transactional enforcement. (developers.cloudflare.com)
Public first-party websites MUST be independently deployable from customer projects and customer build workloads. A failed customer deployment or exhausted customer allocation MUST NOT take the main website offline.
Every environment MUST have explicit resource bindings, secret references, deployment identities and rollback procedures. Private credentials MUST NOT enter browser bundles, public assets, repository history or ordinary diagnostic output.
SH-04 — WordPress-to-Cloudflare website migration
The pass MUST migrate the production website away from its WordPress runtime dependency.
The intended architecture for cakemods.com and 9to1.com is:
Editable Sites project → canonical Files/Stack source → validated build → Cloudflare production deployment.
Sites remains the authoring layer; the public websites are served from their separate production deployments. Published output MUST NOT become the only surviving copy of the website. This follows the existing Sites source and deployment authority contract.
Before migration, the implementer MUST inventory the actual website’s pages, routes, assets, redirects, navigation, forms, account links, downloads and backend dependencies. Every retained capability MUST have a working destination in the replacement.
The migration MUST preserve required content and useful behaviour. It MUST NOT substitute screenshots, flattened pages or an unrelated redesign for the existing site and editor functionality. The cakemods site-plugin remains the donor reference for applicable authoring behaviour.
Moving DNS or placing Cloudflare in front of the existing WordPress server does not satisfy the migration requirement. The replacement MUST operate without WordPress supplying its ordinary public runtime, account backend or content-management operations.
Domain registration MUST NOT be transferred again merely to complete hosting migration. Existing DNS configuration MUST be inspected, and unrelated records—including mail and verification records—MUST be preserved.
The replacement MUST first be validated in a non-production environment. Cutover requires a recoverable backup, a verified destination, a plan for any writes during migration and an authorised rollback path. WordPress MUST NOT be deleted or cancelled simply because the new homepage loads.
There is no requirement to invent a legacy consumer-data migration programme for data that does not exist. Any real accounts, content, submissions or other records discovered during inspection MUST nevertheless be preserved or deliberately migrated.
SH-05 — CAKE ID and account services online
Desktop and web MUST use the same CAKE ID, account identity, organisation context and entitlement services. Ordinary users MUST NOT require WordPress accounts.
Authentication MUST preserve the existing secure public-client contract, including the specified browser-based authorisation flow or an explicitly equivalent secure implementation. Clients MUST NOT contain provider credentials, billing secrets or entitlement-signing secrets.
The supported registration, sign-in, sign-out, recovery, profile, session-inspection and session-revocation journeys MUST work against the production backend. Any journey that sends verification or recovery email MUST use a configured delivery service and expose delivery failures honestly.
Any transition from WordPress-linked authentication MUST use verified account mappings and recovery rules. Matching a mutable username MUST NOT transfer account ownership, administrative authority or paid entitlements.
Jacob’s reserved @CroakyJake handle and account-bound free Business feature grant MUST survive the transition. That grant MUST NOT become an exemption from resource accounting, security permissions or third-party spending approval.
Browser applications MUST use authenticated equivalents of Home’s shared services without requiring a local Home installation. Permission approval, trust, revocation and audit semantics MUST remain consistent with native applications.
Personal and organisation contexts MUST remain separate throughout navigation, storage, billing, search and AI access. Switching accounts or organisations MUST NOT expose cached private information from the previous context.
SH-06 — Full browser versions of the applications
Every non-exempt Workspace and AI application MUST have a functional browser version.
The target is the same application on the web, not a companion dashboard, viewer-only edition or simplified alternative. At equivalent viewport sizes, the browser version MUST preserve the desktop application’s information architecture, tools, editor structure, commands, menus, selection behaviour, settings and supported workflows.
Browser-specific adaptations are permitted for actual capability differences and responsive layouts. They MUST NOT justify avoidable feature loss.
Web implementations MUST preserve CUI’s public semantics, shared component contracts, canonical state identities and supported actions. A browser-specific runtime is permitted; an independently redesigned, incompatible UI framework is not the intended outcome.
Each app MUST support its applicable create, open, edit, save, reopen, history, import/export, sharing and recovery operations. The shared contextual AI bar MUST operate on the real semantic artifact through authorised owning-app APIs.
The web inventory MUST include the active Terra-form additions: Link, Prototype, Paths, Replay, Files’ organisation types and Variants in their owning applications. These retain their existing ownership and terminology; they MUST NOT be reorganised into different products for the web implementation.
Each application MUST have a capability matrix identifying supported browser operations, equivalent adaptations and exact remaining restrictions. A restriction MUST identify the missing capability, affected operation, user-visible behaviour and validation evidence.
A desktop-only feature is not sufficient reason to omit an otherwise useful web app. Mini Computer retains its existing web exemption unless the required hosted-compute capability is explicitly provided. Other missing native capabilities MUST NOT be represented as available merely because a browser interface exists.
Direct links, browser refresh, back/forward navigation and account restoration MUST preserve the intended application and artifact context. Unsupported browsers MUST receive a meaningful compatibility state rather than a broken interface.
SH-07 — Files and 9to1 Drive production hosting
9to1 Drive MUST become a real hosted storage service used by the web and desktop applications.
A file uploaded in the browser and opened on desktop MUST retain the same FileID and durable revision history. Local materialisation is a managed replica, not an unrelated imported copy. Files remains responsible for storage and filesystem operations; the owning application remains responsible for semantic document editing and collaboration.
Private file storage MUST remain private. Protected downloads and shares MUST use access-controlled routes that enforce current account, organisation and object permissions. Possession of an object key MUST NOT grant access.
R2’s public development endpoint MUST NOT be used as the production delivery mechanism or as a substitute for protected sharing. Cloudflare explicitly identifies r2.dev as development-oriented rather than production hosting. (developers.cloudflare.com)
Transfers MUST have durable identities, resumable progress, cancellation, integrity validation and recoverable failure states. Upload completion MUST not be reported until both content and the authoritative metadata commit have succeeded. Interrupted operations MUST be reconciled without invisible orphan uploads or duplicated quota charges.
Storage enforcement MUST account for committed usage and in-flight reservations. Concurrent uploads MUST NOT overspend the same allocation.
Normal connected synchronisation MUST be push-based and incremental, with durable cursors and replay-safe reconciliation. Polling and full rescans remain recovery mechanisms rather than the ordinary propagation path.
Sharing, search, previews, AI retrieval, version restoration and Trash MUST operate on the same canonical objects and permissions. Restoring an earlier revision MUST preserve subsequent history. Ordinary deletion remains recoverable; permanent purge remains a distinct protected operation.
SH-08 — Sites publishing and customer hosting
Sites MUST publish real websites to Cloudflare through its existing deployment model.
A published deployment MUST identify its SiteID, source revision, build/configuration revision, environment, provider result and domain bindings. Preview and production MUST remain distinct.
Publishing MUST include actual asset delivery, route handling and any supported server-side functionality. Successful static deployment MUST NOT be used to claim that required forms, CMS, authentication or dynamic application behaviour also works.
Builds and customer-supplied code MUST execute within appropriately isolated, authorised environments. Customer code MUST NOT inherit the credentials or privileges of CAKE’s account, billing or administrative services.
A failed build or deployment MUST preserve the previous working deployment. Rollback MUST restore a known deployment without deleting newer source history. These behaviours extend the existing deployment and publishing safeguards.
First-party addresses, slug validation, reserved names, misleading-name review, custom-domain ownership verification and DNS/TLS readiness MUST implement the existing Sites contract. The default sites.9to1.uk/<site-slug> namespace MUST NOT silently become a different address scheme.
Browser isolation requires an explicit design decision. Different paths on the same hostname are not separate browser origins. The implementation MUST NOT assume that /site-a and /site-b isolate customer JavaScript, browser storage or other origin-scoped capabilities. A validated isolation design—or an explicitly approved namespace amendment—is required before arbitrary customer active content ships. (developer.mozilla.org)
Hosting limits MUST be enforced server-side. The existing Free-site inactivity policy MUST take affected sites offline without deleting their stored project data.
SH-09 — Real Stripe subscriptions and billing
Canonical plans and resource configuration
Stripe integration MUST implement the canonical subscription model rather than replace it with whatever is easiest to express in a pricing widget.
Preset identity, customised resource quantities, price-threshold entitlements and account-bound grants MUST remain distinct. The server MUST calculate effective access; clients MUST NOT grant resources from a displayed plan name or locally supplied price.
Existing preset definitions MUST remain versioned. Changing a commercial preset MUST NOT silently rewrite existing subscriber allocations. Unspecified quantities MUST remain unresolved rather than being invented during Stripe setup.
Checkout and activation
Checkout MUST begin from an authenticated, server-generated configuration quote. The quote MUST identify the account or organisation, resource configuration, currency, billing cadence, applicable charges and effective change timing.
The backend MUST bind Stripe customer, subscription, price and invoice identifiers to the correct canonical account or organisation. Usernames and client-supplied account claims MUST NOT determine that binding.
Returning to a success page MUST NOT itself activate paid resources. Activation requires verified payment/subscription state and a successful entitlement update.
A payment that succeeds while provisioning is delayed MUST produce a recoverable pending state. Retrying that operation MUST NOT charge the customer again.
Webhooks and reconciliation
Webhook processing MUST verify Stripe signatures against the raw request body, durably record accepted events and process them through retry-safe handlers.
The implementation MUST handle duplicate deliveries and out-of-order events. It MUST prevent both repeated event processing and repeated business effects, such as granting the same invoice’s allocation twice. Stripe does not guarantee event order, and its documentation explicitly requires duplicate-event handling. (docs.stripe.com)
The backend MUST support reconciliation against current Stripe objects after delivery failures or inconsistent local state. A delayed older event MUST NOT overwrite a newer valid subscription configuration.
Payment state, entitlement state and provisioning state MUST remain separately diagnosable.
Customer management and lifecycle
Users MUST be able to manage payment methods, inspect invoices, manage supported subscription configurations and cancel through authenticated billing flows.
Stripe’s customer portal MAY provide supported account-management functions. It MUST NOT be the only implementation of custom resource changes: Stripe documents limitations on updating subscriptions containing multiple products or usage-based billing. Those configurations require a compatible trusted CAKE billing flow. (docs.stripe.com)
Plan changes MUST preview the resulting price, resource allocation, effective date and any immediate charge or credit. Renewal failures, additional payment authentication, cancellation, refunds and disputes MUST map to explicit account states under the approved billing policy.
Billing failure or downgrade MUST NOT silently delete user files, site source or organisation content. Billing management, authorised export and recovery MUST remain available through the appropriate routes.
Business and Business + remain organisation add-ons with separately funded resources. Unlimited seat capacity MUST NOT be interpreted as unlimited storage or AI usage. Existing seat-remediation and account-bound grant rules remain applicable.
SH-10 — Cloud AI and connected application services
Cloud-backed features MUST use real provider connections, with credentials held by trusted services.
The AI gateway MUST enforce identity, organisation policy, model entitlement, resource limits and Dust before execution. It MUST support streaming, cancellation, provider failures and recoverable interrupted sessions.
Usage MUST follow the existing reserve → run → settle contract. Parallel requests MUST NOT spend the same balance twice, and uncertain provider outcomes MUST remain subject to reconciliation rather than arbitrary charging or credit creation. Local models and core local tools MUST NOT be charged as cloud AI usage.
Desktop, web and Personal API access MUST draw from the same applicable entitlement and usage services. Personal API access retains its existing eligibility and shared-allocation rules.
Every existing feature that declares an online dependency MUST have that dependency implemented and validated. This includes applicable collaboration, organisation services, provider connections, notifications, Forms responses, published integrations, Agents and Automations.
Execution location MUST be explicit. A browser task, a cloud-hosted task and a task requiring an enrolled desktop device are different capabilities. Closing a tab MUST NOT silently terminate a task advertised as cloud-hosted; an offline device MUST NOT be shown as executing work.
Long-running operations MUST expose durable job identity, progress, cancellation, retries and results. Reconnection MUST NOT repeat consequential actions. Persistent work MUST retain its authorised identity, scope and funding source.
SH-11 — Operations, security and release delivery
The production service MUST include health checks, actionable failure reporting, privacy-preserving diagnostics and alerts for material outages, failed billing processing, failed jobs and approaching resource limits.
Rate limits, account quotas and workload admission controls MUST prevent one customer from consuming another customer’s allocation or exhausting shared services without bounds. Spending alerts MUST NOT be treated as equivalent to an enforced spending ceiling.
Backups and recovery MUST cover canonical metadata, file revisions, account mappings, entitlement records, site source and deployment configuration—not merely a collection of uploaded bytes. Restoration MUST be tested, with documented recovery objectives.
The existing Privacy Ceiling applies to hosted services, provider integrations, telemetry, retention, exports and deletion propagation. Moving functionality online MUST NOT silently broaden AI access or weaken promised encryption.
Deployment pipelines MUST identify exact source revisions, validate changes before activation and support rollback. Database/schema and client updates MUST account for already-open browser sessions and older supported native clients.
Public download and update paths MUST provide real, verified release artifacts. Home and Launcher MUST continue using their shared package authority, integrity checks and staged activation rather than separate manually maintained update lists.
SH-12 — End-to-end acceptance
Acceptance MUST exercise the deployed services, not only mocks or isolated components.
Journey
Required evidence
Fresh-device onboarding
A new browser session can register or sign in, reach eligible apps and save persistent work without local Home or development tooling.
Web/desktop continuity
An artifact created on one surface opens and edits on the other with the same canonical identity, content, permissions and history.
Application parity
Every in-scope app passes its applicable browser workflows, accessibility checks and recorded capability matrix.
Storage integrity
Interrupted and concurrent uploads resume or fail safely; quotas remain correct; no corrupt file is reported as complete.
Subscription lifecycle
Checkout, verified activation, configuration changes, renewal failure and cancellation produce the correct account and resource states.
Billing replay
Duplicate, delayed and reordered events cannot duplicate charges, allocations or entitlement transitions.
Publishing
A real Sites project deploys, serves its required dynamic behaviour, verifies its domain and rolls back without losing source.
Isolation
Cross-account access, revoked sharing and malicious customer content cannot expose another account’s files, sessions or administrative services.
Recovery
A tested restore and redeployment recover the service from preserved canonical state.
Independent operation
Public websites and cloud-hosted services remain operational without the developer’s PC and survive representative customer-workload failures.
Payment failure scenarios MUST first be exercised using appropriate test facilities. Live-mode validation requires an authorised merchant configuration and explicit approval for any actual charge. Test-mode success alone MUST NOT be reported as proof of live billing.
Visual and interaction testing MUST cover populated workloads, narrow layouts, keyboard operation, screen-reader semantics, 200% scaling, themes, reduced motion and failure/recovery states.
SH-13 — Decisions required before affected functionality goes live
The following items remain explicit launch decisions rather than implementation guesses.
Commercial catalogue and lifecycle policy. Finalise all offered resource allocations, usage periods, rollover rules, configuration prices, downgrade behaviour, grace periods and retention consequences. The existing specification leaves material allocations and billing policies unresolved. Undefined configurations MUST NOT be offered for purchase.
Currency and entitlement-price calculation. Define how tax, discounts, promotional credits and non-monthly billing affect EntitlementPriceMonthly. Resolve the existing GBP resource pricing and USD Business add-ons through an approved billing policy. Stripe requires prices within a single multi-product subscription to use the same currency; silent relabelling or conversion is not acceptable. (docs.stripe.com)
Production service configuration. Confirm the account-authentication implementation, transactional delivery provider, database/coordination boundaries, supported runtime capabilities and environment ownership. Existing compatible infrastructure MUST be inspected before replacement.
Customer-site browser isolation. Approve the isolation mechanism for active content under the specified path-based public addresses. Any change to the canonical URL model requires an explicit specification amendment.
Operational and launch parameters. Confirm supported browser versions, measurable performance/capacity targets, recovery objectives, infrastructure budgets, merchant readiness and production cutover authorisation.
These decisions MUST block only their affected release paths. They MUST NOT be silently resolved by a worker, hidden behind defaults or used to stop independent implementation.
Release exit gate
Sol Happy is complete only when the required online services are implemented, integrated, deployed to their authorised environments and validated against the applicable specification.
Implemented, tested, deployed and commercially enabled MUST remain distinguishable states.
The final evidence ledger MUST identify the tested release, deployed service versions, functioning user journeys and every remaining blocker or approved scoped exception. No service may be described as online merely because its interface exists, a provider account has been connected or a test request succeeded.

Training Lab
Training Lab is an explicitly deferred AI Studio project/surface and is OUT OF SCOPE for the release candidate. It is reserved for future model-training/fine-tuning and related dataset/training workflows, but its exact product scope, supported training methods/backends, dataset model, safety constraints, artifact formats, resource scheduling, APIs and acceptance requirements are not yet specified.
Release-candidate AI Studio implementations MUST NOT expose Training Lab as an in-scope project type, navigation/sidebar entry, New Project option or partially functional placeholder. Future implementation requires a separate canonical specification before Training Lab becomes in scope.
